| 14 | **`OE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`/`OE_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD` are empty in `.env`**, so `${VAR:-kspass}` silently selected upstream's published passwords while the variables looked configured | **Fixed — DH-021.** Both are now `:?` required; an empty value fails loudly at `up` instead of quietly selecting a public password |
| 17 | **The provisioning executor's 900s timeout is far short of a real OpenMRS first boot (~49 min)**, so the first genuine facility provisioning would time out and be reported as failed while the stack was still coming up | **Fixed 2026-08-16 — per-verb timeouts.** Liban chose the longer-timeout option over detaching. Verbs that wait on the compose health graph (`provision`, `start`, `rotate_tls`) get 5400s; `backup_now` gets its own bound because it scales with stored data, not boot time; `status`/`stop` stay at 900s. Both long bounds are per-host configurable. The bound is asserted **against the real `docker-compose.yml`** — it must clear every `start_period` (the largest is 1800s) and the measured 49-minute cold boot — so a future gate with a longer grace period fails the suite rather than the first deployment. 371 tests, Ruff clean. Control-verified three ways: restoring 900s fails the two guards by name, wiring `provision` to the fast bound fails the per-verb tests, and running without the compose file mounted **fails instead of skipping**. ⚠️ Still unfixed by this: bug 18 below, and the fix has **not** been exercised against a real ~49-minute boot — no clinical stack has ever booted through the provisioning path |
| 18 | **The agent does not poll while a long job runs**, so a `stop`/`status`/`backup_now` issued during a ~50-minute provision is refused as stale when finally claimed (`JobValidator` rejects jobs older than 900s) | **Fixed 2026-08-20 — `execute` moved off the poll loop's thread (`poller.py`).** `poll_once` dispatches to a background execution slot and returns immediately; the loop's `fetch` cadence continues while a long job runs. Two slots, not one: `status` is read-only (`docker compose ps`/`config`) and always runs, including alongside an in-flight mutating job; every other verb (`provision`, `start`, `stop`, `rotate_tls`, `backup_now`) shares one **mutating** slot, so at most one runs at a time — a second one claimed while the first is in flight is refused immediately (`"busy"`) rather than racing two `docker compose` invocations against the same project. Staleness protection (ADR-022) is untouched: `JobValidator` still runs synchronously on the calling thread, before dispatch, with the same 900s window — the fix is that a `status` issued mid-provision is now validated and run promptly instead of waiting behind it. `executor.py`, `validation.py`, `jobs.py` and `queue.py` are all unchanged; the queue's per-host FIFO dispatch order is unchanged too. ⚠️ **A companion lifecycle-table fix was required to ship this safely.** Concurrent polling makes it newly possible for a duplicate `PROVISION` targeting a facility still `PROVISIONING` to be claimed and refused (busy, or the pre-existing `FacilityExistsLocally` check) *while the real attempt is genuinely still running* — under the old, blocking loop this could never happen, because nothing else could be claimed until the first job's `execute()` returned. `next_facility_state`'s `PROVISION` row previously treated any non-`succeeded` report as `DEGRADED`; a busy-refused duplicate would have flipped a healthy, still-provisioning facility to `DEGRADED` **permanently** (the row only fires from `PROVISIONING`, so the real attempt's later `succeeded` report would arrive too late to match it and correct it). Fixed in `app.py`: the row now only degrades on a genuine `failed` report; `refused` is a no-op, matching how every other row already treats a non-`succeeded` report. Only reachable via a compromised/buggy API bypassing `create_facility`'s conflict check — ADR-022's own stated residual risk — but the codebase's own precedent (`FacilityExistsLocally`) treats exactly that threat as real, so it was closed rather than logged as a caveat. 11 new tests (poller concurrency, staleness regression, lifecycle-table symmetry), **464 provisioning tests total** (from 453). **Control-tested, three breaks, each on a throwaway copy of the tree:** disabling the busy-refusal check (any verb dispatches regardless of what is already in flight) — **3 fail**; restoring the old binary `PROVISION` lifecycle row (`RUNNING if succeeded else DEGRADED`) — **2 fail**; reverting `poll_once` to call `execute` inline instead of dispatching to a thread, reproducing bug 18 exactly — **6 fail**, one unaffected (`test_the_mutating_slot_frees_once_the_job_finishes`, correctly: slot-clearing-after-completion holds regardless of the execution model, so that control has nothing to break). ⚠️ **The demo harness (`demo/agent_runner.py`) was checked, not just assumed safe.** It now dispatches non-blocking, so it can claim a second job while the first is still executing, and its `agent_outcomes.jsonl`/`agent_executed.jsonl` files can interleave writes from two threads. Checked what reads those files: nothing committed does (`grep` across `demo/harness_*.py` and `demo/README.md` finds no consumer) — they are write-only instrumentation for manual inspection today, so there is no ordering assumption this fix could violate. Worth re-checking if a harness is later built to read them. Not exercised against a real ~50-minute boot — no clinical stack has ever booted through the provisioning path, so the concurrency fix is proven at the poller/queue level, not against real `docker compose` timing |

## DH-011H1 / DH-011I1 — 2026-08-31 stop report (synthetic/disposable only)

**Human Decision Required: Yes.** Liban approved adding exactly `Add Orders` to the existing
`Daher Clinician Admission` role and instructed the implementation to stop if any other privilege
proved technically required. The CSV/Keycloak descriptions/static guards now carry that sole
increment; reception remains exactly registration-only and lab-tech has no OpenMRS role grant.
Liban also approved `Pilot Test Clinician` as the synthetic requester name and transport-only use
of one genuinely prior-proven mapping if one existed; real staff names, the real numeric OpenELIS
site number, and the clinical/lab-selected pilot list all remain pending.

The starting commit `c592b898711e8a01aa4aff892f885621b611a0bb` confirms DH-011E4/E4B is
committed DONE; this pass does not reopen it. DH-006 remains open and no clinical selection was
made.

The stop condition was reached on a genuinely fresh disposable OpenMRS database. The synthetic
clinician authenticated with the exact ten configured privileges, but a real native REST Test
Order attempt returned `400`: resolving its referenced Test concept requires the separate
`Get Concepts` privilege. Zero fixture order rows existed afterward. Reception and a synthetic
zero-role lab-tech were also denied before write (`Get Encounters` was their first missing payload
resolution privilege), and the order count stayed zero. **`Get Concepts` was not granted.** Until
Liban decides whether that second privilege is approved, the clinician-positive test and the
runtime remove-`Add Orders` isolation control cannot pass. ADR-034 records the decision and stop.
The committed configuration guard itself was negative-control tested on a throwaway copy: removing
`Add Orders` produced exactly two failures naming the missing privilege. What remains blocked is a
*runtime* isolation proof that gets past `Get Concepts` and then fails specifically on
`Add Orders`.

The already-running real facility stack was never queried, started, stopped, or mutated. All names,
patients, providers, concepts, and orders in this investigation were synthetic and existed only in
new `dh011h1` / `dh011h1omrs` Docker projects.

### DH-011H practitioner result

The patched pinned OpenELIS business FHIR path creates genuine native `clinlims.person` +
`clinlims.provider` state, but discards both the submitted Practitioner id and submitted source
identifier. The first `Pilot Test Clinician` create produced a random OpenELIS UUID; exact replay
returned `201` and created a second native provider/person. A different source UUID with the same
name created a third. No fuzzy match was attempted.

An order referencing the first OpenELIS-native UUID linked `sample_human.provider_id` correctly.
An omitted requester and a well-formed unknown requester each returned `201` and created a genuine
native order with `provider_id=NULL`; a malformed UUID returned `500` and created no correlated
order. A secondary-FHIR-store outage proved split state: Practitioner create returned `201` and
native direct read worked, forwarded search failed, and no search row appeared after recovery.

**DH-011H technical mechanism: NOT DONE / architecture decision required.** The smallest safe
current-architecture proposal is a native, unique OpenMRS Provider UUID → OpenELIS provider link
persisted atomically with provider creation, parallel to DH-011G2. An adapter-only map cannot close
the crash-after-native-commit gap. Full evidence: `docs/DH-011H1-PRACTITIONER-SPIKE.md`.

**DH-011H synthetic name:** `Pilot Test Clinician` is available as input only; it is not safely
mapped. **DH-011H real facility input:** waiting on staff names.

### DH-011I exact inventory result

Fresh native extraction corrected the old packet count: `clinlims.test` contains **189 rows**,

Docker container ultimately ran; the postgres CI job itself still uses `postgres:16-alpine`
unchanged.

**Four real defects found by actually running the code — none were visible from re-reading alone:**

1. **`LabOrderItemRecord` silently dropped the price snapshot** (`orders.py`) — the dataclass
   returned to callers never carried `selected_price_amount`/`selected_price_currency` at all,
   even though the ORM row had them; the very first SQLite pytest run failed on this immediately.
   Fixed: both fields added to the dataclass and populated in `_to_order_record`.
2. **Patient/practitioner source-identity uniqueness was scoped too broadly**
   (`UNIQUE(source_identity_system, source_identity_value)`, no organization) — proven live: two
   different organizations asserting the same `(system, value)` pair would have silently merged
   into one `PatientReference`/`PractitionerReference`, a cross-organization identity collision,
   not a hypothetical one. Fixed: uniqueness is now
   `(source_organization_id, source_system, source_identity_system, source_identity_value)` in
   both `models.py` and migration `0004`; `identity.py`'s conflict-lookup queries updated to match.
   New tests: `test_no_source_identity_collision_across_organizations_{patient,practitioner}`.
3. **`LabOrder.idempotency_key` was globally unique, and a key collision returned the existing
   order unconditionally** — two real bugs compounding: (a) a global unique key means two
   independent organizations' clients could collide on the same key value by accident, and the
   loser would have silently received the *other organization's order* back — a cross-tenant data
   leak, not a UX bug; (b) even within one organization, a resubmitted key with different
   patient/practitioner/requested-tests was returned as if it matched, silently handing back
   mismatched data instead of refusing. Fixed: uniqueness is now
   `(provider_organization_id, idempotency_key)`; a resubmission is only ever treated as a replay
   if patient, practitioner, and the exact requested test-ID set match exactly, otherwise a new
   `IdempotencyKeyConflict` is raised. `get_by_idempotency_key` signature changed accordingly
   (now requires `provider_organization_id`) — a real, intentional API-contract change, recorded
   here as required. New tests: `test_same_key_different_{patient,practitioner,test_set}_is_a_
   conflict*`, `test_same_key_different_provider_org_creates_two_independent_orders` (confirming
   org-scoping's *intended* effect — not a conflict, two legitimate independent orders).
4. **`CatalogRepository.set_price` raised a raw `IntegrityError` under real concurrent writes** —
   reproduced live against real PostgreSQL under 8-way concurrent contention (6 of 8 threads
   failed on the first attempt). Root cause: a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` that blocks on a row a
   concurrent winner has already superseded unblocks onto zero matching rows, not the winner's new
   row, so the loser wrongly believed no current price existed and collided on insert. Fixed:
   replaced with an unconditional `UPDATE ... WHERE superseded_at IS NULL` (never raises, matches
   however many rows are actually currently true) followed by a bounded (25-attempt) retry around
   the remaining insert-uniqueness race. Verified clean across 10 repeated real-PostgreSQL 8-way
   concurrent runs after the fix, 0 failures.

**Real PostgreSQL qualification, all live-executed and green** (`adapter/tests/integration/
test_dhex001r_postgres_qualification.py`, new file, gated behind `DHEX001R_PG_*` env vars,
skipped by default including in CI, matching this repository's existing live-integration-test
convention): 10 concurrent creates with the same idempotency identity → exactly 1 `LabOrder`, 1
`LabOrderItem` set, 1 `DoctorReview`, 1 `ResultDelivery` — no duplicates from the 9 losing
attempts; 10 concurrent creates with 10 different keys and identical payload → 10 independent
orders; 8 concurrent price updates on one offering → exactly 1 current price row survives (partial
unique index), 0 unhandled exceptions; an invalid state transition refused under a real row lock,
order status unchanged. Separately proven: fresh `alembic upgrade head` (0001→0004) on an empty
database; an existing pre-DH-EX-001 database (upgraded only to `0003_dead_letter_resolutions`,
with a real row inserted into `processed_messages`) upgrades cleanly to `0004_exchange_core` with
that row untouched; `alembic downgrade 0003_dead_letter_resolutions` cleanly drops all 12
`exchange_*` tables with the pre-existing row still intact; re-upgrading back to head succeeds.
Schema introspection on the live database confirmed every CHECK/UNIQUE/FK constraint compiles
exactly as `models.py` declares, including the corrected composite unique constraints. Five raw-SQL
negative/positive controls against `exchange_lab_results`' CHECK constraints (bypassing the ORM
entirely) confirmed the NUMERIC/TEXT mutual-exclusivity invariant is enforced by PostgreSQL itself,
not merely by application code.

**Transaction atomicity, proven by real fault injection** (added to `test_exchange_orders.py`, not
a new file): three tests patch `DoctorReview`, `ResultDelivery`, and `Session.commit` respectively
to raise mid-`create()`, after the point `LabOrder`+`LabOrderItem` rows would already have been
flushed to the database within that same uncommitted transaction. All three: zero trace of the
failed attempt afterward (`get_by_idempotency_key` raises `OrderNotFound`), and a retry with the
identical idempotency key immediately afterward produces exactly one complete aggregate with no
orphan rows. Note on scope: this implementation has exactly two flush points in its success path
(LabOrder+LabOrderItems together at one explicit `flush()`, then DoctorReview+ResultDelivery
together inside the final `commit()`), so "after LabOrder insert" and "after item insert" are the
same boundary here, not two — stated plainly rather than implying five distinct injectable points
that do not exist in this code.

**Audit writer guarantee restored, not weakened.** DH-EX-001 widened
`daher_adapter.audit.AuditWriter.append` from `AuditEvent` to `BaseModel` so `ExchangeAuditEvent`
could reuse it. Review found `ExchangeAuditEvent` was never actually wired to any repository call
in DH-EX-001 — no caller exists — so the widening weakened the writer's type guarantee for zero
current benefit. Reverted: `append` is `AuditEvent`-typed again, exactly as before DH-EX-001.
`ExchangeAuditEvent` remains defined (a forward-looking schema, still `extra="forbid"`) with an
updated docstring stating plainly that writer integration is deferred to whichever ticket builds
the first real Exchange-audit caller.

**Design findings reviewed, no code change made (Part G — eager `ResultDelivery`/`DoctorReview`
creation):** independent review confirmed this is a genuine, defensible tradeoff, not a bug.
Lazy creation (create `ResultDelivery` only "when a result becomes deliverable", `DoctorReview`
only "when a result exists to review") would require inferring that trigger point from something
adjacent to result completion — which is exactly what DH-EX-001 explicitly forbids ("delivery
status must never be inferred from `LabResult` completion"). Eager creation with PENDING rows for
orders that are later REJECTED/CANCELLED is a real, acknowledged cosmetic property (a "pending
review" list would need to join against order status to exclude them), not a data-integrity defect
— left as a documented consideration for whichever ticket builds the actual query/listing API, not
changed here.

**Org-type safety (Part L), reviewed, no gap found:** `LabOffering`/`LabSelection`/`LabOrder`
directly enforce PROVIDER/LAB type via `OrganizationRepository.require_type` at their own creation
points; `LabResult`'s lab identity is transitively safe because it can only be recorded against an
already-`require_type`-validated `LabSelection` (`WrongLabForResult` closes any mismatch); no
public repository method bypasses these checks. `PractitionerReference` has no organization-type
constraint at all, by design — DH-EX-001 never specified one, and neither did this review.

**Ruff/format/pytest, all real:** `ruff check src tests migrations scripts` clean, `ruff format
--check src tests migrations scripts` clean (69 files), full adapter suite **275 passed, 39
skipped** (the 39 are this repo's existing live-infra-gated integration tests plus the 4 new
`DHEX001R_PG_*`-gated ones — correctly skipped with no live Postgres env vars set, exactly the
existing convention). `pip check` clean.

**Files changed beyond DH-EX-001's original set:** `adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/{models,
identity,orders,catalog}.py` (the four fixes above), `adapter/src/daher_adapter/audit.py` (revert),
`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/{__init__,audit}.py` (docstring corrections),
`adapter/migrations/versions/0004_exchange_core.py` (matching constraint corrections), new
`adapter/tests/integration/test_dhex001r_postgres_qualification.py`, additions to
`test_exchange_orders.py`, `test_exchange_identity.py`, `test_exchange_selection.py`.

**READY FOR COMMIT: YES** — no BLOCKER/HIGH findings remain open; every gate this ticket's own
READY RULE names was checked against real execution, not assumption. **Not committed, not pushed**
— stopped for Liban's own review first, per this ticket's explicit instruction, independent of the
green result. No OpenMRS/OpenELIS connector touched, no poller activated, no real facility or
patient data used anywhere in this review.

### DH-CI-001 · Repair the pre-existing OpenMRS OMOD Maven reactor build failure · P0 ·
✅ DONE — CI hygiene only, no clinical/application logic changed

**Raised:** 2026-09-08/09, Liban, immediately after DH-EX-001C's exact-SHA CI run exposed the
pre-existing "OpenMRS narrow TestOrder module" job failure. **Human Decision Required: No** —
build-configuration-only correction, no product/clinical/architecture decision involved.

**Root cause.** The inherited `maven-parent-openmrs-module:2.2.0` `pluginManagement` binds
`maven-dependency-plugin`'s "Expand resources" execution (goal `unpack-dependencies`, unpacking the
sibling `daherendadmission-api` reactor artifact's `*.xml`/`*.properties` into the OMOD's
`target/classes`) to the `generate-resources` phase. Under a reactor-wide `mvn test` — this repo's
CI invocation, and the only place the OMOD's own tests ever actually run, since the real packaging
build in `openmrs-config/Dockerfile` uses `-Dmaven.test.skip=true package` — the sibling API module
has not been packaged into a JAR yet at that point in the lifecycle. This is the documented MDEP-98
pitfall. **Confirmed pre-existing, not a DH-EX-001 regression**: reproduced identically against the
parent commit `4dfaeef`'s own CI run before any fix was written. The actual OpenMRS tests
themselves always passed; the reactor died at `unpack-dependencies` afterward, before the OMOD's
own 27 tests were ever reached.

**Fix.** `openmrs-config/modules/daherendadmission/omod/pom.xml` only — rebound the "Expand
resources" execution (matched by id) from `generate-resources` to `prepare-package`, the last
standard lifecycle phase before `package`. Under `mvn test`, `prepare-package` is never reached, so
the execution cannot fail; under a full `mvn package`/`install` (the Dockerfile's real path), the
sibling API module is already packaged by the time OMOD reaches `prepare-package`, since Maven
completes each reactor module's full lifecycle before moving to the next dependent module. Both
properties live-verified, not assumed. Reproducing this locally required installing Maven + OpenJDK
8 into a previously-unused WSL2 Ubuntu instance; doing so also surfaced a real process hazard —
running `mvn test`/`package` locally triggers this project's `spotless:apply`/`license:format`
plugins in *apply* mode, silently reformatting ~24 tracked Java files as a side effect. Caught via
`git status` before treating any run as final, and reverted with `git restore` every time, twice.

**Evidence.** Local: full reactor `SUCCESS` (Parent/API/OMOD), 37/37 tests (API 10: `DaherTestOrder
ContractTest` 7/7, `DaherProxyPrivilegeExecutorTest` 3/3; OMOD 27: `CreateTestOrderServletTest`
6/6, `DaherExternalConfigurationInterceptorTest` 3/3, `EndMaternityAdmissionServletTest` 18/18), 0
failures/errors/skips — the 27 OMOD tests had never previously run through this CI job at all.
Package-regression control (`-Dmaven.test.skip=true package`, matching the Dockerfile) produced
`omod/target/daherendadmission-1.0.0.omod` with `moduleApplicationContext.xml` and `config.xml`
correctly unpacked. `git diff --check` clean; diff scope exactly one file, +46/-0.

**Committed and pushed:** `4f9c1d10dc4543aa785c0bee939108a339b45e61` ("fix(ci): make OpenMRS OMOD
test reactor lifecycle-safe"), parent `b1f8d85` (exact match, confirmed via `git rev-parse HEAD^`).
**Exact-SHA CI qualified:** run `34317829117`, `head_sha = 4f9c1d10dc4543aa785c0bee939108a339b45e61`,
conclusion `success`, **all 9 required jobs green** including "OpenMRS narrow TestOrder module"
(both its "Compile the complete module reactor and run every test" and "Refuse silent test loss"
steps green; job's own guard reports "OpenMRS module tests executed: 37"). No Java production or
test file changed, no CI workflow file changed, no Exchange code changed, no OpenELIS code changed,
no privilege/endpoint/clinical behavior changed, no poller activated, no real facility touched.

### DH-EX-002 · Organization onboarding, OIDC authentication, tenant isolation, minimal
`/exchange/v1` API · P0 · 🔨 IMPLEMENTED + SQLite/PostgreSQL-QUALIFIED · ⏳ NOT COMMITTED — awaiting
independent review

**Ticket:** DH-EX-002. **Base:** on top of DH-EX-001's qualified foundation (`0004_exchange_core`).
**Commit/push boundary:** explicitly **not committed, not pushed** — this entry documents
implementation returned for independent review, the same DH-EX-001 → DH-EX-001R → DH-EX-001C
sequence this ticket is expected to follow next.

**What was built.** Migration `0005_exchange_org_auth` (`exchange_identities`,
`exchange_organization_memberships`, `exchange_organization_role_assignments`, with matching FKs,
CHECK constraints, and UNIQUE constraints). `exchange/identity_auth.py`: OIDC bearer-token
validation via **PyJWT only** (`PyJWT[crypto]==2.13.0`, newly pinned, together with its
`cryptography`/`cffi`/`pycparser` transitive deps) — no hand-written cryptography, an explicit
algorithm allowlist that structurally excludes `alg=none`, and a `KeySource` protocol
(`JWKSKeySource` for production, `StaticKeySource`/`UnconfiguredKeySource` for tests and the
fail-closed default) so no test in this repository reaches the network. `exchange/membership.py`:
identity bootstrap and membership/role repositories, all insert-first-wins idempotent, enforcing
the provider/lab role matrix and refusing to attach a role to an inactive membership
(`MembershipInactive`). `exchange/authorization.py`: `AuthorizationService` — the sole place
`require_membership`/`require_role`/`require_org_admin`/`require_platform_admin` decisions are
made, implementing the anti-enumeration policy (no relationship → 404, has relationship but lacks
permission → 403, platform admin bypasses both except for a genuinely nonexistent org). Identity
and organization authentication/authorization are separate: Keycloak (OIDC issuer + subject)
authenticates; the Exchange database is the sole authority for organization membership and role —
no per-organization Keycloak realm role was created. `exchange/api.py`: five endpoints under
`/exchange/v1` (`GET /me`, `POST /organizations`, `GET /organizations/{id}`,
`GET /organizations/{id}/memberships`, `POST /organizations/{id}/memberships`), closed Pydantic
schemas throughout. `app.py`: the Exchange router is always mounted; when OIDC is unconfigured it
fails closed (401 on every request) via `UnconfiguredKeySource` rather than the adapter refusing to
start — `/health/live` and `/health/ready` are unaffected either way.

**Two real defects found and fixed before shipping** (caught by an independent-reviewer pass over
this same implementation, not by a pre-existing failing test): (1) a rejected multi-role
`POST .../memberships` request (e.g. `["ORG_ADMIN", "LAB_TECH"]` against a PROVIDER organization)
previously left a committed membership and a committed `ORG_ADMIN` grant behind before the 422 —
role validity is now checked against the organization-type matrix *before* the membership row is
created, so a rejected request commits nothing. (2) re-`POST`ing a membership that exists but is
`INACTIVE` previously returned a silent 200 with the requested roles attached, which would have let
an admin believe access was restored for someone deliberately deactivated — it now returns 409 and
attaches nothing; `OrganizationRoleAssignmentRepository.assign` independently refuses to attach a
role to an inactive membership regardless of caller.

**One real bug found only by running the code, not by reading it:** `exchange/api.py` originally
carried `from __future__ import annotations`. Combined with this module's nested-closure dependency
pattern (`get_principal` and friends are defined *inside* `build_exchange_router`, not at module
scope), FastAPI could not resolve `Depends(get_principal)` from the stringified annotation at
request time — every protected endpoint silently returned `422 {"detail": "principal required"}`
instead of running any authentication or authorization logic at all. This was not caught by code
review; it surfaced only once the HTTP test suite was actually executed. Fixed by removing the
future-annotations import from this one file (safe: the file uses only Python 3.10+ native union
syntax, and the target runtime is 3.13). Recorded here because it is exactly the class of bug this
repository's "distinguish written from verified from demonstrated" discipline exists to catch.

**Tests:** 82 new tests, all passing, added to the committed (SQLite-backed) adapter suite —
`test_exchange_token_validator.py` (19: the full authentication-negative matrix — missing/malformed
header, malformed/unsigned/`alg=none`/wrong-signature/wrong-issuer/wrong-audience/expired/future-nbf
/missing-sub/missing-exp/unresolvable-key tokens, all rejected; role/claim extraction),
`test_exchange_identity_membership.py` (19: identity bootstrap idempotency and exact-identity
scoping, the role matrix, inactive-membership refusal, and two 10-thread concurrency proofs — one
for identity bootstrap, one for membership creation, each asserting exactly one row and zero
escaped `IntegrityError`s), `test_exchange_authorization_service.py` (11: anti-enumeration,
cross-tenant isolation, platform-admin bypass), `test_exchange_api.py` (30: the full HTTP-level
matrix — platform-admin gating, org-admin scoping, role-escalation negative controls including the
two defects above, audit-log assertions including "never a bearer token in the log", no wildcard
CORS), `test_exchange_app_wiring.py` (3: the real `create_app()` assembly, proving the fail-closed
default and that health endpoints are unaffected). Full adapter suite: 357 passed / 39 skipped
(pre-existing, real-PostgreSQL-gated integration tests, unrelated to this ticket) — `ruff check` and
`ruff format --check` both clean across `src`, `tests`, and `migrations`.

**Real PostgreSQL 18 qualification** (`apt`-installed in a WSL2 sandbox, not Docker — see the
Keycloak note below for why): `alembic upgrade head` from a `0004`-only database reaches
`0005_exchange_org_auth` cleanly; `alembic downgrade 0004_exchange_core` was independently verified
to drop exactly the three new tables (`exchange_identities`,
`exchange_organization_memberships`, `exchange_organization_role_assignments`) and leave every
DH-EX-001 table intact; re-upgrade is clean. A standalone, not-committed 25-thread concurrency
script (matching the DH-EX-001R precedent of a real-database proof kept separate from the pytest
suite) proved exactly one row created and zero errors for both the identity-bootstrap race and the
membership-creation race against this real instance — not just SQLite. As with DH-EX-001R, this is
not claimed to be byte-identical to CI's own `postgres:16-alpine`.

**REAL KEYCLOAK QUALIFICATION = NOT RUN.** `docker pull` of a Keycloak image failed with a TLS
handshake timeout reaching the registry CDN, both unprivileged and with `sudo` — the identical
failure mode DH-EX-001R already recorded for this sandbox (Docker Hub/registry pulls unreliable
here). No mock-JWT test above is being represented as equivalent to a real Keycloak token issuance/
validation/tenant-isolation proof; every claim in this entry about token validation is proven
against a **locally generated RSA keypair** via `StaticKeySource`, never a real IdP.

**Keycloak realm config, prepared but not wired:** `keycloak/realm-config/dhealth-exchange-realm.json`
is new — a separate `dhealth-exchange` realm, one realm role (`dhealth-platform-admin`, matching
`Settings.exchange_platform_admin_role`'s default), one client (`dhealth-exchange-api`) with an
explicit audience-claim mapper, `registrationAllowed: false` (no public self-service signup),
brute-force protection mirroring the connector realm's already-established values
(`daher-realm.json`, untouched by this ticket). Session lifetimes are shorter than the connector
realm (`ssoSessionIdleTimeout` 1800s / `ssoSessionMaxLifespan` 14400s vs. the connector realm's
3600s/36000s) reflecting this ticket's explicit "short-lived tokens" instruction for a
cross-organization identity boundary; `accessTokenLifespan` is left at 300s, matching the connector
realm's already-established value rather than inventing a new number. This file is **not** wired
into `keycloak/reconcile-sso.sh` or `docker-compose.yml` and needs human security review before any
activation — it exists so the OIDC contract this ticket implements has a concrete target realm
shape to test/document against, per the ticket's explicit "prepare, stop short of changing
deployment topology" instruction.

**Audit is fail-open on the durability boundary, by omission, not by design decision — stated
plainly because the ticket requires it, not because it was mitigated.** Every mutation (`POST
/organizations`, `POST .../memberships`, each role assignment) commits its database write, then
calls `ExchangeAuditWriter.append`, which raises on any failure (disk full, permission error, a
short write) rather than swallowing it. Nothing catches that exception in `exchange/api.py`, so it
propagates as an uncaught 500 — but the mutation is already committed. The concrete failure this
produces: **a committed organization or membership with no audit line, surfaced to the caller only
as a 500 with no indication the write actually succeeded.** This was not changed in this ticket and
is not mitigated (no compensating transaction, no outbox pattern, no retry). Separately, two of the
six DH-EX-002 audit `event_type` values `exchange/audit.py` defines —
`membership_inactivated` and `role_removed` — have no HTTP call site in this ticket (no
deactivate-membership or remove-role endpoint was built) and are therefore untested; do not read
the six-value list as six values of equal coverage.

**Repo-wide CRLF line-ending flip — discovered during this ticket, blocks the next one, not caused
by DH-EX-002's own edits.** While preparing this work, `git status` showed ~344 tracked files across
the whole repository as modified with no code review would explain. Verified precisely: `git diff -w
--name-only` (ignore-whitespace) returns exactly the 8 files this ticket actually changed content
in — nothing else. Byte inspection of one such file confirms the mechanism: `git show
HEAD:README.md` ends lines in `0a` (LF); the working-tree copy now ends the same lines in `0d0a`
(CRLF). Something outside this ticket's own edits flipped the working tree's line endings from the
repository's LF convention to CRLF, tree-wide, at some point in this environment's history; the
cause was not identified and is out of this ticket's scope to fix. This session's own edits are
clean of it — the five pre-existing files this ticket modified
(`adapter/src/daher_adapter/{config,app,audit}.py`, `adapter/requirements.txt`,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and this documentation pass (`PROJECT_STATE.md`, `CURRENT_STATE.md`)
were explicitly normalized back to LF (`sed -i 's/\r$//'`) after editing, and every new file this
ticket created is pure LF from creation (confirmed: `grep -c $'\r'` returns 0 on all twenty files
this ticket touched). **This blocks DH-EX-002C** (or whatever ticket next runs `git add`): staging
this ticket's real changes today would also stage ~344 unrelated whitespace-only files unless that
ticket scopes `git add` to exactly the paths this entry lists. Fixing the flip itself (a
`.gitattributes` policy plus `git add --renormalize .`) is a repository-hygiene decision, not a
code change this ticket makes unilaterally — flagged for Liban, not resolved here.

**Real facility:** untouched. **Pollers:** inactive. **Not built in this ticket** (explicitly out
of scope, matching the ticket's own exclusion list): the lab-order API, Provider/Lab Portal UI,
patient links, WhatsApp, payments, email/invitation-based membership onboarding. **Known MVP
limitation, by design:** `POST .../memberships` attaches an existing identity by `identity_id`
(UUID) only — it performs a lookup, never a creation, and never accepts a raw `(issuer, subject)`
pair. The target person must authenticate at least once (e.g. call `GET /me`) and share their
`identity_id` out-of-band before an org admin can attach them; no invitation/lookup-by-email flow
exists yet.

DH-EX-002R entry below, superseding this line: that review has now happened.

### DH-EX-002R · Independent security review + runtime qualification of DH-EX-002 · P0 ·
✅ REVIEWED, ONE BLOCKER FIXED, ONE LATENT TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE BUG FOUND AND FIXED · ⏳ STILL NOT
COMMITTED — awaiting Liban's review

**Ticket:** DH-EX-002R, the DH-EX-001R-equivalent independent review step for DH-EX-002.
**Base:** unchanged, `e93e7cc17c01ba79e24b34524cb76d42cc4d928a` — still not committed, not pushed.

**BLOCKER found and fixed: the Exchange audit was fail-open, exactly as the DH-EX-002 handoff had
already disclosed.** DH-EX-002R's approved architecture decision: for organization creation,
membership creation, and role assignment, the mutation and its authoritative audit row now commit
or roll back together as **one database transaction**. New table `exchange_security_audit_events`
(folded into the still-uncommitted `0005_exchange_org_auth` migration, not a new `0006`, per this
ticket's own instruction not to invent artificial migration history for unreviewed work) — closed
schema (UUID FKs, CHECK-constrained short strings only, no free-text field, structurally incapable
of holding a token). New module `adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/security_audit.py`
(`ExchangeSecurityAuditRepository.record` — never opens or commits its own transaction, only
`session.add()`s onto a session the caller already owns). `OrganizationRepository.create`,
`OrganizationMembershipRepository.create`, and `OrganizationRoleAssignmentRepository.assign` all
gained an optional `session` parameter: when given, the caller owns the transaction and the
insert-or-fetch idempotency check runs inside a `SAVEPOINT` (`session.begin_nested()`) so a
duplicate-key hit unwinds only to the savepoint, never poisoning the caller's outer transaction;
when omitted, every existing caller (DH-EX-001's own code, this repo's other tests) is unaffected.
`exchange/api.py`'s two mutation endpoints now wrap their writes in
`with session_factory.begin() as session: ...`, which commits on success and rolls back
everything -- membership, every role assignment, and every audit row -- if anything inside raises,
including the audit insert itself. Authorization **refusals** (403/404, and the inactive-membership
re-POST 409) are explicitly excluded from this table by design (a refusal is not a mutation) and
stay in the existing best-effort file-based `ExchangeAuditWriter`, now wrapped so a refusal-audit
write failure can never turn an intended 403/404/409 into an accidental 500 -- access denial must
never depend on a database write succeeding, and now provably doesn't.

**Proven by failure injection, not just code review** (`test_exchange_audit_atomicity.py`, 3 new
tests): injecting a failure in the audit insert after organization creation leaves the DB with
zero new organizations and zero new audit rows; injecting a `Session.commit()` failure does the
same; injecting a failure on the *second* audit insert in a membership-creation-plus-role-grant
request (proving the whole multi-statement transaction unwinds, not just the one call that failed)
leaves zero new memberships, zero new role assignments, and zero new audit rows.

**A second, unrelated real bug was found while building that proof: SQLite/pysqlite silently broke
SAVEPOINT rollback semantics.** The very first version of the failure-injection test for the
membership+role case failed unexpectedly: the membership row survived a rollback that should have
erased it. Root-caused to a well-documented SQLAlchemy/SQLite gap -- the stdlib `sqlite3` DBAPI
manages its own implicit transactions underneath SQLAlchemy's, which breaks `Session.begin_nested()`
SAVEPOINT rollback unless disabled via SQLAlchemy's own documented workaround (`isolation_level =
None` on connect, an explicit `BEGIN` on begin). Verified reproducible in isolation, then verified
**absent against real PostgreSQL** (this repo's actual runtime driver, via psycopg) -- confirming
this was purely a test-environment gap, not a production correctness bug. Fixed in the **shared**
`adapter/tests/conftest.py` `engine` fixture (used by the whole adapter test suite, not just
Exchange tests), because leaving it broken would have silently invalidated any future ticket's
rollback-behavior test under this fixture, not just this one's. Full regression re-run after the
fix: **366 passed / 39 skipped, zero regressions** (was 360 before this fix's 3 new atomicity
tests were added; the fix itself changed no other test's outcome).

**Reproduced and reconfirmed all four previously-fixed bugs from the DH-EX-002 handoff**, each with
a permanent test: the multi-role atomicity fix (now additionally proven at the audit-row level --
zero `ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent` rows for a rejected request, not just zero membership/role rows);
the inactive-membership-reactivation 409; role-assignment refusing an inactive membership; and the
`from __future__ import annotations` / FastAPI nested-dependency 422 regression, now with a
permanently named regression test (`test_protected_routes_do_not_422_on_nested_dependency_resolution`).

### DH-EX-002 · FINAL CLOSURE — organization onboarding, OIDC authentication, tenant isolation ·
P0 · ✅ CLOSED / QUALIFIED (organization/auth/tenant-isolation foundation gate only — see scope
note below)

**Ticket:** DH-EX-002 (+ DH-EX-002R independent security/runtime review, combined into one commit).
**Implementation + review commit:** `dc3d13b7a8d6a53422091b56138718a73e096715`.
**Parent:** `e93e7cc17c01ba79e24b34524cb76d42cc4d928a` (DH-EX-001D's docs-closure commit).
**Exact CI run:** `34390897519` — `head_sha` exact match, conclusion `success`.
**CI:** 9/9 required jobs green (`adapter — ruff + pytest`, `provisioning — ruff + pytest`,
`ui — lint, typecheck, test, build`, `seed + form-safety suites`, `OpenMRS narrow TestOrder module`,
`static checks`, `compose interpolates and parses`, `oauth2login — patched identity tests`,
`openelis order-correlation patch — compiles`).
**Tests:** adapter suite 366 passed / 39 skipped, confirmed both locally and independently in CI's
own logs. `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean. Dependency consistency (`pip check`) clean.
**Migration:** `0005_exchange_org_auth` reaches head — `exchange_identities`,
`exchange_organization_memberships`, `exchange_organization_role_assignments`,
`exchange_security_audit_events`. Qualified: fresh `0001→0005`, `0004→0005`, downgrade `0005→0004`
(confirmed to drop exactly the four new tables, DH-EX-001's tables untouched), re-upgrade
`0004→0005` — all against a real, disposable PostgreSQL 18 instance. CI independently ran
`alembic upgrade head` against its own **`postgres:16-alpine`** service and confirmed `alembic
current == alembic heads == EXPECTED_HEAD == 0005_exchange_org_auth`. The local qualification
sandbox (PostgreSQL 18) and CI's actual database (`postgres:16-alpine`) are not claimed to be
identical -- CI independently proved migration/application compatibility on its own real 16 service,
not just on the newer local one.

**What DH-EX-002 established.** The DHealth Exchange **organization onboarding, authentication, and
tenant-isolation boundary**, on top of DH-EX-001's core domain: `ExchangeIdentity` (exact OIDC
`(issuer, subject)` key -- never email, name, or phone), `OrganizationMembership`
(`UNIQUE(organization_id, identity_id)`), `OrganizationRoleAssignment`
(`UNIQUE(membership_id, role)`), and `ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent` (the authoritative, transactional
audit table DH-EX-002R's review added). A minimal `/exchange/v1` HTTP API -- exactly these five
routes exist, no others: `GET /me`, `POST /organizations`, `GET /organizations/{id}`,
`GET /organizations/{id}/memberships`, `POST /organizations/{id}/memberships`. No lab-order API, no
pricing/selection API, no patient-link API, no Provider/Lab Portal exist yet -- those are explicitly
future tickets, not implied by this closure.

**Authentication model.** DHealth-native Exchange identities authenticate through OIDC; the stable
identity key is `(issuer, subject)` only, never email/name/phone. A valid, previously-unseen token
may create an `ExchangeIdentity` row on first use, and that alone grants **zero** organization
access -- membership is a separate, explicit grant. A prepared, dedicated `dhealth-exchange`
Keycloak realm (`keycloak/realm-config/dhealth-exchange-realm.json`) is the intended identity
provider, kept entirely separate from the historical connector realm (`daher-realm.json`, **not
modified by DH-EX-002**). Exchange platform-admin authority comes from exactly one validated realm
role, `dhealth-platform-admin` -- never from `ORG_ADMIN`, never from the connector realm's
`sys-admin`/`clinician`/`lab-tech` roles, and never from anything stored as an organization role.

**REAL KEYCLOAK QUALIFICATION = NOT RUN.** A disposable Keycloak image/runtime could not be obtained
in the local qualification sandbox -- registry pulls consistently failed with a TLS handshake
timeout (verified reproducible, both unprivileged and with `sudo`). The implementation was
qualified cryptographically against the real OIDC contract (RS256-only signature verification,
exact issuer, exact audience, expiration, `nbf`, required `sub`, unknown-signing-key refusal,
malformed-token refusal, JWKS-failure fail-closed, JWKS trust from configured application state
only -- never a token-supplied `jku`/`x5u`) using locally generated RSA keys and realistic Keycloak
`realm_access` claim shapes. **That is not equivalent to a live Keycloak integration test** and is
not represented as one anywhere in this record. Real Keycloak qualification remains a required
deployment/pilot gate, to be closed by a future ticket once a Keycloak runtime is available.

**Organization authorization and tenant isolation.** The Exchange database, not Keycloak, is the
sole authority for organization membership and role. Provider organizations may hold `ORG_ADMIN` or
`CLINICIAN`; lab organizations may hold `ORG_ADMIN` or `LAB_TECH`; platform admin is never an
organization role. Inactive memberships and inactive organizations are refused, not silently
bypassed. Qualified negative controls include: an unrelated clinic cannot read another clinic's or
lab's data; a lab cannot read a different lab's data; an `ORG_ADMIN` cannot manage another
organization or grant platform admin; `CLINICIAN`/`LAB_TECH` cannot manage membership; a provider
org cannot be assigned `LAB_TECH`; a lab org cannot be assigned `CLINICIAN`. Anti-enumeration
contract, applied consistently: an unrelated tenant/resource returns 404 (indistinguishable from
nonexistent); a member who lacks the required permission returns 403.

**Audit -- the blocker DH-EX-002R found and fixed before this commit, not after.** DH-EX-002's
initial implementation committed a security mutation, then wrote a filesystem audit line
separately -- if that second write failed, a real organization/membership/role change could exist
with no authoritative audit trail. DH-EX-002R corrected this **before any of it was committed**:
organization creation, membership creation, and role assignment now insert their authoritative
`ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent` row in the **same PostgreSQL transaction** as the mutation itself: if
the audit insert fails, the mutation rolls back with it. Proven by failure injection, not only code
review: an audit-insert failure, a `Session.commit()` failure, and a failure on the *second* audit
insert in a multi-statement request (membership + role together) each leave **zero** mutation and
**zero** audit row. Replays do not generate a false duplicate `*_created` event. Only the mutation
types this ticket actually exposes over HTTP are qualified this way -- there is no
deactivate-membership or remove-role endpoint yet, and none is claimed as qualified. Refusal
telemetry (403/404/409) is explicitly non-authoritative, best-effort, file-based, and cannot block
or depend on a database write succeeding. The historical connector `AuditWriter`
(`daher_adapter/audit.py`) remains separate and unchanged.

**Real bugs found and fixed before this became the committed state** (recorded here so this
closure entry alone gives an accurate picture, without requiring cross-referencing the DH-EX-002/
DH-EX-002R working entries above): (1) a multi-role membership request could previously commit a
partial membership/role grant before discovering one invalid role -- fixed by validating the whole
role set before any mutation begins; (2) re-`POST`ing an inactive membership could previously
reactivate it silently -- fixed to return a conflict/refusal instead; (3) role assignment
independently refuses an inactive membership regardless of caller; (4) a `from __future__ import
annotations` import combined with FastAPI's nested-dependency resolution caused every protected
route to return 422 before authentication ever ran -- fixed, and permanently regression-tested;
(5) the audit fail-open blocker described above; (6) a SQLite/pysqlite-specific `SAVEPOINT`
rollback gap in the shared test fixture (`adapter/tests/conftest.py`) was found while proving fix
(5) and corrected -- confirmed to be a test-infrastructure-only gap, real PostgreSQL never exhibited
it. None of these were ever the committed, deployed, or reviewed-as-safe state; all six were closed
before this ticket's commit.

**Concurrency.** Real PostgreSQL 18 (local qualification sandbox): 25 concurrent identical
`(issuer, subject)` first-seen attempts produce exactly one identity and zero errors; 25 concurrent
identical `(organization_id, identity_id)` membership attempts produce exactly one membership and
zero errors; 25 concurrent identical `(membership_id, role)` assignment attempts produce exactly one
role assignment and zero errors. CI's own PostgreSQL is `postgres:16-alpine`, not PostgreSQL 18 --
the two are not claimed identical; CI independently proved migration/application compatibility on
its actual 16 service via the exact-SHA run cited above.

**Real facility:** untouched. **Pollers:** inactive. **Connector realm:** unchanged
(`daher-realm.json`, `reconcile-sso.sh` not touched by DH-EX-002/DH-EX-002R). No file under
`openmrs-config/` or `openelis-config/` was touched.

**What this closure means, precisely.** DH-EX-002 closes the Exchange organization/authentication/
tenant-isolation **foundation**. It does **not** mean: the DHealth MVP is complete; a Provider
Portal order workflow exists; a Lab Portal exists; a patient secure link exists; a lab marketplace/
pricing UI exists; WhatsApp/SMS integration exists; a lab pricing API exists; a results workflow
exists; real Keycloak deployment is qualified; real organizations have been onboarded; real staff
accounts exist; an OpenMRS Exchange connector exists; an OpenELIS Exchange connector exists;
production deployment exists; or any pilot has begun. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §17 for the
architecture and `DECISIONS.md`'s ADR-042 for the underlying product-pivot decision, unchanged in
substance by this closure.

### DH-EX-003 · Lab directory, DHealth test catalog, lab offerings, current pricing, whole-order
eligibility · P0 · 🔨 IMPLEMENTED + SQLite/PostgreSQL-QUALIFIED · ⏳ NOT COMMITTED — awaiting
independent review

**Ticket:** DH-EX-003. **Base:** on top of DH-EX-002's qualified foundation
(`0005_exchange_org_auth`). **Commit/push boundary:** explicitly **not committed, not pushed** —
this entry documents implementation returned for independent review, the same
DH-EX-001→DH-EX-001R→DH-EX-001C / DH-EX-002→DH-EX-002R→DH-EX-002C sequence this ticket is expected
to follow next.

**What was built.** Migration `0006_exchange_lab_directory`, purely additive on top of `0005`: a
new `exchange_lab_directory_profiles` table (free-text `public_address` + optional paired
`latitude`/`longitude` with DB CHECK constraints enforcing both-or-neither and valid ranges, no
geocoding; `listed`/`accepting_orders` both default `false` — never auto-visible), plus a careful,
minimal generalization of DH-EX-002's `ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent` (not a replacement):
`organization_id` widened to nullable for platform-level mutations, new `resource_type`/
`resource_id` columns for polymorphic resource targeting, widened `event_type`/`outcome` CHECK
constraints. `exchange/directory.py` (new): `LabDirectoryProfileRepository`, insert-first-wins
upsert restricted to ACTIVE LAB organizations only. `exchange/catalog.py` (rewritten): DHealth test
catalog entries (HTTP creation always `is_synthetic=true` — no client request may submit
`is_synthetic=false`), lab offerings (insert-first-wins, a distinct `OfferingInactiveConflict` so a
re-POST against an existing inactive offering never silently reactivates it), and DJF-only current
pricing with optimistic concurrency (`expected_current_price_id` CAS token, `None` meaning "expect
no current price"; a documented same-value-replay exception treats an already-equal-value replay as
a safe `"unchanged"` no-op regardless of token; superseded price rows are never mutated, only
superseded — full price history preserved). `exchange/api.py`: new endpoints for catalog
(`GET/POST /catalog/tests`, platform-admin only for POST), lab directory (`GET /labs`,
`GET /labs/{id}`, `PUT /organizations/{id}/directory-profile`), offerings and pricing
(`GET/POST /organizations/{id}/offerings`, `PATCH .../offerings/{offering_id}`,
`POST .../offerings/{offering_id}/prices`, all org-admin gated with anti-enumeration 404s verified
via a new `_existing_offering_for_lab_or_404` helper), and `POST /marketplace/lab-options` — a
**read-only** query, gated behind a new non-org-scoped `require_any_active_membership` check
(platform admin bypasses; any other caller needs ≥1 ACTIVE membership anywhere), that returns which
listed/accepting-orders/ACTIVE labs can fulfil the **entire** requested set of tests and at what
total DJF price. This endpoint never writes a `LabSelection` row and never freezes a
`LabOrderItem` price — that remains a later ticket by explicit scope boundary.

**Whole-order eligibility is all-tests-only by construction, not by a filter applied after the
fact.** `find_whole_order_eligible_labs` is a 3-pass query specifically shaped to make a partial-lab
result structurally impossible even under a future refactor: (1) candidate labs via
`GROUP BY lab_organization_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT catalog_entry_id) == required_count` against
active offerings + active/synthetic catalog entries + current DJF prices; (2) filter candidates to
ACTIVE organizations with `listed=true` AND `accepting_orders=true`; (3) fetch the actual price
lines for surviving labs, defensively dropping any lab whose fetched line count does not exactly
equal the requested count. Verified against the ticket's exact four-lab scenario (Lab A offers all
three tests and is eligible from the start; Lab B offers two of three and is correctly excluded;
Lab C starts short one test, is excluded, then becomes eligible the moment its third offering is
priced, with no partial result ever observed in between; Lab D offers all three but has
`accepting_orders=false` and is excluded throughout) both in the SQLite pytest suite and
independently against real PostgreSQL.

**One real concurrency bug found only by running against real PostgreSQL, not by reading the code
or by SQLite testing — the most significant finding in this ticket.** The original `set_price`
implementation did a separate `SELECT` (discover the current price) followed by a separate
`UPDATE ... WHERE superseded_at IS NULL` (supersede it). Under PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED
isolation, each statement gets its own fresh snapshot, so multiple concurrent transactions could all
observe "no current price exists" before any of them committed — a 25-way same-price concurrency
qualification script caught this directly: `outcomes.count("created") == 1` asserted `4 == 1`, i.e.
four threads each wrongly believed they were the first to set the price. This was completely
invisible under the SQLite pytest suite because SQLite's coarse whole-database locking happened to
serialize the two statements enough to mask the race. Fixed by folding discover-and-supersede into
one atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE superseded_at IS NULL ... RETURNING` statement, with the same-value
replay exception handled by reverting the accidental supersede within the same transaction before
returning `"unchanged"`. Re-verified clean across 3 independent full re-runs of the real-PostgreSQL
qualification script after the fix (25-way same-price: exactly 1 `created`, 24 `unchanged`, 1
current row; 25-way different-price with a stale CAS token: exactly 1 `created`, 24 `PriceConflict`,
1 current row). Recorded here in full because it is exactly the class of bug this repository's real-
runtime-qualification discipline exists to catch — SQLite alone would have shipped it.

accepting_orders defaults, the three DB-level CHECK constraints exercised as raw-insert
`IntegrityError` negative tests), `test_exchange_catalog_dh_ex_003.py` (catalog/offering
idempotency and conflict semantics, price CAS semantics including the same-value-replay exception
and stale-token rejection, the exact ticket whole-order eligibility scenario, a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`

Full adapter suite: **429 passed / 39 skipped** (was 366 at the DH-EX-002
handoff; the 39 skipped are pre-existing real-PostgreSQL-gated integration tests, unrelated to this

`pip check` clean.

**Real PostgreSQL 18 qualification** (same WSL2 `apt`-installed sandbox as DH-EX-001R/DH-EX-002,
not Docker): `alembic upgrade head` from a `0005`-only database reaches
`0006_exchange_lab_directory` cleanly. `alembic downgrade 0005_exchange_org_auth` was verified in
**two** states, not one, because the first result alone would have overstated what was actually
proven: (1) against a freshly-migrated `0006` database with **no DH-EX-003 audit rows yet**, it
cleanly drops the new table and reverses the audit-table widening (CHECK constraints, nullable
`organization_id`, `resource_type`/`resource_id` columns), leaving every DH-EX-001/DH-EX-002 table
and row untouched, and re-upgrade is clean; (2) against a `0006` database seeded with DH-EX-003-
shaped audit rows (a `catalog_entry_created` row with `organization_id IS NULL`, exactly what
`POST /catalog/tests` produces — a genuinely platform-level mutation with no owning organization),
the downgrade **fails**, as it must: `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN organization_id SET NOT NULL`
raises `NotNullViolation` because a real NULL row now exists. This is not a bug — narrowing a
column that legitimately widened cannot be silently reversed once the wider shape has been used —
but it is a real, load-bearing limit on this migration that the first test alone would have hidden.
Postgres DDL is transactional here: the failed downgrade attempt left the database cleanly at
`0006_exchange_lab_directory` with zero partial schema change, independently confirmed via
`alembic current` immediately after the failure. **Stated plainly: `alembic downgrade
0005_exchange_org_auth` is only safe before any DH-EX-003 mutation (a platform-level catalog entry,
or any event/outcome the DH-EX-002 CHECK constraints didn't allow) has actually run — an operator
downgrading a live `0006` database must first confirm no such rows exist, or accept a manual data
migration.** A standalone, not-committed
qualification script (matching the DH-EX-001R/DH-EX-002 precedent of a real-database proof kept
separate from the pytest suite) additionally exercised the exact whole-order eligibility scenario
against real PostgreSQL (same result as SQLite: only Lab A eligible initially, Lab A + Lab C
eligible once Lab C's third offering is priced, never a partial-lab result) and the audit-atomicity
failure-injection case (an offering creation plus a deliberately-failing audit call inside one
`session.begin()` block: after the `RuntimeError` propagates, both the offering row count and the
audit row count are unchanged from before the attempt). As with DH-EX-001R/DH-EX-002, this is not
claimed to be byte-identical to CI's own `postgres:16-alpine`.

**REAL KEYCLOAK QUALIFICATION remains NOT RUN — unaffected by this ticket.** DH-EX-003 adds no new
authentication surface; it reuses DH-EX-002's existing OIDC/`AuthenticatedPrincipal` machinery
unchanged. The DH-EX-002 finding (Docker registry TLS handshake timeouts in this sandbox) was not
re-attempted and is not re-litigated here.

**Synthetic-catalog-only enforcement, checked at three independent layers.** (1) The HTTP request
schema `CatalogEntryCreateRequest` has no `is_synthetic` field at all — a client cannot submit
`is_synthetic=false` even if it tries, closed-Pydantic (`extra="forbid"`) rejects the unknown field;
(2) the endpoint handler hardcodes `is_synthetic=True` when calling `catalog.create_entry`,
independent of any request content; (3) the marketplace endpoint additionally validates every
requested `catalog_entry_id` is `is_synthetic=true` (422 if not) *before* running eligibility, and
`find_whole_order_eligible_labs` itself filters on `is_synthetic=true` in its candidate query, so a
non-synthetic entry could not leak through even if a future caller bypassed the endpoint-level
check. Covered by both a repository-level test
(`test_whole_order_eligibility_non_synthetic_catalog_entry_excluded`) and an HTTP-level test
(`test_marketplace_non_synthetic_catalog_entry_fails_closed`).

**Real facility:** untouched. **Pollers:** inactive. **Not built in this ticket** (explicitly out
of scope, matching the ticket's own exclusion list): order creation, patient links, any UI (Provider
Portal, Lab Portal, patient secure link), WhatsApp/SMS, payment/billing, connector code. The
marketplace endpoint is read-only by construction — it does not write `LabSelection` and does not
freeze a `LabOrderItem` price; that remains DH-EX-004's job. Pricing is DJF-only throughout — no FX/
currency conversion exists yet, so a future multi-currency order cannot be assembled from this
ticket's data alone without an explicit follow-up decision.

then — on approval — a combined DH-EX-003+DH-EX-003R commit/push/exact-SHA-CI ticket, following the

### DH-EX-003R · Independent marketplace/security/data-integrity review + runtime qualification of
DH-EX-003 · P0 · 🔨 REVIEWED + FIXED + SQLite/PostgreSQL-QUALIFIED · ⏳ NOT COMMITTED — awaiting
Liban's review

**Ticket:** DH-EX-003R, the DH-EX-001R/DH-EX-002R-equivalent independent review step for DH-EX-003.
**Base:** `a76455db8677815c4a32deee4fce592c7761dafb` (DH-EX-002D's docs-closure commit — confirmed
via `git rev-parse HEAD` before and after this review). **Not committed, not pushed** — same
boundary as DH-EX-003 itself.

**One BLOCKER found and fixed: `require_any_active_membership` never checked whether the
membership's own organization was ACTIVE.** An identity whose only membership was in a
**deactivated** organization retained standing, indefinite access to browse `GET /catalog/tests`,
`GET /labs`, and `POST /marketplace/lab-options` — network-wide reads that are not scoped to any
single organization, so none of the other `require_*` checks (which all check one specific
`organization_id`'s status) ever ran against it. The original docstring's reasoning ("an org's own
active/inactive status only matters for org-scoped actions") does not hold here: an organization is
deactivated specifically to cut off its access, and a network-wide read is still access. Fixed in
`exchange/authorization.py`: `require_any_active_membership` now requires an ACTIVE membership in
an organization that is *also* currently ACTIVE, checked per-membership via
`OrganizationRepository.get`. Verified at the HTTP layer, not just the authorization-service unit
level, by `test_active_membership_in_inactive_organization_cannot_browse_network` — access works
before deactivation, is refused (403) on all three network-read endpoints immediately after, while
`GET /me` stays unaffected (this is a browsing gate, not an authentication gate).

**Four HIGH findings, all fixed within DH-EX-003's already-approved architecture:**

1. **Mixed-currency total, not just a hypothetical race.** `find_whole_order_eligible_labs`'s pass
   (1) candidate query required `LabPrice.currency == "DJF"`, but pass (3)'s actual price-line
   fetch — the one whose amounts get summed into `total_amount` — never re-checked currency.
   `LabPrice.currency` is a plain code, not a hard enum, by design (for a future multi-currency
   lab), so any non-DJF current price reaching that column by any path other than this HTTP API's
   `Literal["DJF"]` request schema would have had its line silently included and summed into a
   response still labeled `"DJF"`. Fixed: pass (3) now re-checks every condition pass (1) already
   checked (`LabOffering.active`, `TestCatalogEntry.active`, `TestCatalogEntry.is_synthetic`,
   `LabPrice.currency == "DJF"`), not just offering-active. Proven with a repository-level test
   that deliberately sets a non-DJF price via direct repository call, bypassing the HTTP schema
   entirely (`test_whole_order_eligibility_non_djf_current_price_excluded`).
2. **`GET /catalog/tests` returned every row, unfiltered, to any authenticated network member —
   inactive and non-synthetic entries included — with no platform-admin distinction.** An ordinary
   lab/provider member could see a non-synthetic or inactive catalog entry as though it were
   selectable pilot inventory, purely because a row existed in the DB; DH-EX-003's own stated
   policy is the opposite. Fixed: `CatalogRepository.list_entries(active_synthetic_only=...)`, and
   `list_catalog_tests` now passes `active_synthetic_only=not principal.platform_admin` — ordinary
   members see ACTIVE+SYNTHETIC only, platform admin keeps the unfiltered inspection view. Proven
   by `test_catalog_list_hides_inactive_and_non_synthetic_from_ordinary_member`.
3. **`find_whole_order_eligible_labs`'s three passes are not automatically one coherent snapshot
   under PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED isolation**, which hands each statement its own fresh
   snapshot rather than sharing one across a transaction (the exact same class of gap `set_price`'s
   own docstring already documents, here in a different method). Careful analysis showed the
   existing self-healing design — every pass re-verifies its own conditions against fresh state,
   and the final exact-line-count check drops rather than partially emits a lab that stopped
   qualifying mid-query — already prevented any partial-lab or fabricated-eligibility result from a
   race. What it did not guarantee was that the response's one `as_of` timestamp actually
   corresponded to one true database snapshot, or eliminate every theoretical staleness edge case.
   Fixed by running the whole read under `REPEATABLE READ` on PostgreSQL specifically (a per-Session
   isolation-level override set before the first statement executes; SQLite has no equivalent named
   level and does not need one for a single-connection test run, so the override applies only when
   the bound dialect is `postgresql`). Also strengthened the final defensive check from a line
   *count* comparison to an exact requested-*set* comparison (structurally redundant today given
   `LabOffering`'s `UNIQUE(lab_organization_id, catalog_entry_id)` constraint, but made explicit
   rather than relying on that constraint implicitly, per the review's own "requested A,B but
   returned lines A,A must never be accepted" challenge). Verified against real PostgreSQL two ways:
   (a) confirmed `SHOW transaction_isolation` actually reports `repeatable read` inside the
   overridden session; (b) a dedicated stress script ran 4 concurrent reader threads against
   `find_whole_order_eligible_labs` for 3 seconds while a 5th thread continuously toggled an
   offering's active state — 616 reads completed under active concurrent mutation, zero
   inconsistent results (no partial line sets, no mixed currency), zero errors.
4. **Migration `0006`'s downgrade could hit a raw, unfiltered `NotNullViolation` mid-migration** if
   any DH-EX-003 platform-level audit row (`organization_id IS NULL`) existed — honest evidence, not
   a bug, but not yet an intentional operator-facing contract either (the DH-EX-003 handoff itself
   flagged this precisely). Fixed: `downgrade()` now runs an explicit pre-check, before any DDL,
   for any `exchange_security_audit_events` row incompatible with `0005`'s narrower shape (NULL
   `organization_id`, a DH-EX-003 `event_type`, or an `'updated'`/`'unchanged'` `outcome` —
   `resource_type`/`resource_id` need no separate check, since every row carrying either is, by
   construction, also a DH-EX-003 `event_type`). If any exist, it raises a new
   `DowngradeBlockedByAuditHistory` with an explicit, operator-readable message and makes zero
   schema changes — it never deletes audit rows and never fabricates a placeholder
   `organization_id` to force compatibility. Verified against real PostgreSQL in both states: (a) a
   freshly-migrated `0006` database with no DH-EX-003 rows downgrades to `0005` cleanly, and
   re-upgrades cleanly; (b) the same database reseeded with one DH-EX-003-shaped row refuses
   immediately with the new explicit error, and `alembic current` / a direct row-count/schema query
   afterward confirm the database is still exactly `0006`, byte-for-byte unchanged (transactional
   DDL — the refusal happens before any `ALTER`/`DROP` statement runs).

**Three MEDIUM/LOW findings, also fixed:**

- `LabDirectoryProfileRequest.public_address` only enforced `min_length=1`, accepting a
  whitespace-only string as though it were a real address — for a mandatory, non-nullable field
  with no "draft, no address yet" state modeled anywhere in the schema. Fixed with a
  `model_validator` requiring `public_address.strip()` to be non-empty, matching the
  `code.strip()`/`display_name.strip()` convention already used elsewhere in this package.
- `LabPriceSetRequest.amount` had no `max_digits`/`decimal_places` constraint, so a value with more
  than 2 decimal places or more than 10 integer digits reached the database rather than being
  refused at the schema boundary — `exchange_lab_prices.amount` is `Numeric(12, 2)`. Fixed by
  adding `max_digits=12, decimal_places=2` to the Pydantic `Field`, matching the DB column exactly;
  both now 422 cleanly. Proven by `test_price_amount_precision_and_scale_are_enforced`.
- Two disclosed audit-coverage gaps from the DH-EX-003 handoff — `lab_directory_profile_updated`
  never exercised via HTTP at all, `lab_offering_status_changed` never exercised on its
  successful-mutation path — are now closed:
  `test_directory_profile_update_and_replay_audit_sequence` (create → real update → no-op replay,
  asserting the no-op reports `outcome="unchanged"`, never a false `"updated"`) and
  `test_offering_status_update_full_sequence_audit` (ACTIVE→INACTIVE→ACTIVE→no-op, same false-
  positive-outcome check). The cross-tenant refused-PATCH test was also strengthened to assert zero
  `lab_offering_status_changed` rows survive the 404, not just the status code.

**Additional coverage added, not fixing a defect but closing disclosed test gaps from the DH-EX-003
handoff and this review's own challenge list:** `test_lab_tech_cannot_manage_offerings_profile_or_price`
(a LAB_TECH's ACTIVE-but-non-ORG_ADMIN membership must refuse every lab-management mutation — a
real permanent regression test, not previously exercised for any DH-EX-003 endpoint);
`test_catalog_create_failure_leaves_zero_mutation_and_zero_audit_row`,
`test_directory_profile_failure_leaves_zero_mutation_and_zero_audit_row`,
`test_offering_status_change_failure_leaves_zero_mutation_and_zero_audit_row`,
`test_price_change_failure_leaves_zero_mutation_and_zero_audit_row` (audit-atomicity failure
injection for the four mutation classes the DH-EX-003 handoff had proven for offering-creation
only); `test_marketplace_price_change_never_rewrites_an_existing_order_snapshot` (the ticket's
explicit price-snapshot-non-regression scenario — DH-EX-001's `LabOrderItem`/`LabSelection` tables
already exist, so this was directly testable, not merely structurally argued as the DH-EX-003
handoff had claimed); real-PostgreSQL concurrency proofs for catalog-entry creation and lab-offering
creation (25-way each, exactly 1 `created`, 1 row, 0 errors — not previously exercised against real
Postgres, only SQLite).

**Tests:** 12 new tests added to the committed (SQLite-backed) adapter suite (441 passed / 39
skipped, up from 429 at the DH-EX-003 handoff) — `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` both clean
across `src`, `tests`, `migrations`; `pip check` clean.

**Real PostgreSQL 18 qualification, re-run in full after every fix above** (same WSL2 sandbox):
the full `pg_dh_ex_003_qualification.py` script (25-way same-price and different-price
concurrency, the exact whole-order eligibility scenario, audit-atomicity failure injection) passed

incompatible-refuses-cleanly) verified as described above; the REPEATABLE READ coherence stress
test (616 reads under concurrent mutation, 0 inconsistent results) passed; catalog-entry and
lab-offering 25-way creation concurrency both passed. None of this is claimed byte-identical to
CI's own `postgres:16-alpine`, matching every prior ticket's same caveat.

**REAL KEYCLOAK QUALIFICATION remains NOT RUN** — unaffected by this review; no new authentication
surface was added or touched.

**Real facility:** untouched. **Pollers:** inactive. **No file under `openmrs-config/` or
`openelis-config/` touched. No connector code touched.**

**Files changed beyond DH-EX-003's original set:** none new — every fix above is inside the same 18
files DH-EX-003 already touched (`git status` confirms the identical 13 modified + 5 new file list,

**READY FOR COMMIT: YES** per this ticket's own gate — no BLOCKER/HIGH finding remains open, all six

generalized (nullable `organization_id` for platform-level mutations, polymorphic
`resource_type`/`resource_id`), not replaced, to cover these six new mutation event types, all now
proven by a positive HTTP test.

retained standing, indefinite access to browse the catalog/directory/marketplace, because

membership status only, never the membership's own organization status. Fixed before any of this

whole-order query's pass-3 line fetch; `GET /catalog/tests` returning every row unfiltered to any
network member with no platform-admin distinction; the three-pass eligibility query's snapshot
coherence under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED, closed by running the whole read under `REPEATABLE READ`
— proven both by confirming `SHOW transaction_isolation` actually reports `repeatable read` and by

downgrade, which could previously hit a raw `NotNullViolation` mid-migration, now runs an explicit

**Migration `0006_exchange_lab_directory`, purely additive on `0005_exchange_org_auth`, and
CONDITIONALLY reversible — stated precisely, not as a bare "downgrade works".** `alembic upgrade
head` from `0005` reaches `0006` cleanly; `0006 → 0005` succeeds cleanly and re-upgrades cleanly
**only while no DH-EX-003 platform-level audit history exists that cannot fit `0005`'s narrower
shape** (a NULL `organization_id`, a DH-EX-003 `event_type`, or an `'updated'`/`'unchanged'`
`outcome`). Once such a row exists — for example, one `catalog_entry_created` audit row from a
platform-level catalog mutation, which by definition has no owning organization —
`downgrade()` detects this **before any DDL** and refuses with an explicit
`DowngradeBlockedByAuditHistory` message rather than deleting the audit row, fabricating a
placeholder organization, or silently rewriting audit ownership to force the schema to narrow. This

row-count and schema query afterward confirm the database is still exactly `0006`, byte-for-byte
unchanged (transactional DDL — the refusal happens before any `ALTER`/`DROP` runs). This is an
intentional fail-safe, not a migration defect, and not equivalent to "downgrade is unconditionally
safe."

**Ticket:** DH-EX-004. **Base:** on top of DH-EX-003's qualified foundation
(`0006_exchange_lab_directory`). **Commit/push boundary:** explicitly **not committed, not

**What was built.** Migration `0007_exchange_order_api`, purely additive on top of `0006`: widens
`ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent`'s closed `event_type`/`resource_type` CHECK constraints to permit

created or dropped, since `LabOrder`/`LabOrderItem`/`DoctorReview`/`ResultDelivery` already exist
