added; the exact release-record schema is evaluated, not implemented; no migration exists; no
`LabResultRelease` model exists; no `lab_result_released` audit event exists.

**Next:** once Liban answers Decisions 3 and 4 (the two genuinely open policy questions; Decisions

question), a DH-EX-012 implementation ticket can proceed without inventing laboratory policy. Per
this ticket's own final instruction, implementation is **not started here**.

**Human Decision Required: YES** (Decisions 3 and 4 specifically; the packet as a whole cannot be

### DH-EX-012 · Implement explicit order-level lab-result release (ADR-044) · P0 · ✅ IMPLEMENTED — SQLite + real PostgreSQL qualified

**Ticket:** DH-EX-012. Implements ADR-044 (`DECISIONS.md`) exactly as accepted by Liban on
2026-09-13: Question 1 → a new, dedicated `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` role (Option B); Question 2 → the
same human may always enter and release (Option A), no second-person requirement. Starting SHA
`68bdcf89c94e86a001ac812690430ed6fdb82f00` re-audited fresh, not trusted blindly, before any edit.

#### What changed

**Role model** (`exchange/models.py`, `exchange/membership.py`). New `OrganizationRole.
LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`, additive to `ORG_ADMIN`/`CLINICIAN`/`LAB_TECH`, LAB-only in
`ALLOWED_ROLES_BY_ORG_TYPE`. `OrganizationRoleAssignment.role` and `ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent.role`
both widened `VARCHAR(16)`→`VARCHAR(32)` (`'LAB_RESULT_RELEASER'` is 19 characters). No code
anywhere compares `entered_by` to `released_by` — and, confirmed by reading `LabResult`'s full
column list (negative control 4 below), no such comparison is even *constructible* today: the
model records no entering-identity at all, only `lab_organization_id`. A single identity may hold
both roles.

**Authorization** (`exchange/authorization.py`). New `require_lab_result_releaser` and
`require_lab_tech_or_result_releaser`, both following the existing anti-enumeration pattern exactly
(nonexistent org → 404 for everyone; zero-relationship caller → 404; platform-admin-alone or
`ORG_ADMIN`-alone with a real org but missing role → 403).

**Release record** (`exchange/models.py`). New `LabResultRelease` — one immutable, order-level row
(`id`, `lab_order_id` UNIQUE, `lab_organization_id`, `released_by_identity_id`, `released_at` —
server time only, no caller-supplied timestamp). No revision, no un-release, no delete column or
method exists. Mirrors DH-EX-011's `LabSampleCollection` shape exactly, the second reuse of that
pattern in this codebase.

**Removed automatic completion** (`exchange/results.py`). `LabResultRepository._submit_in_session`
no longer writes `LabOrder.status` at all — even the last missing result leaves the order
`IN_PROGRESS`. `ResultSubmissionOutcome.order_completed` renamed `ready_for_release: bool`,
reporting the identical DB-grounded `missing_count == 0` fact, now shared via a new module-level
`_count_missing_results` helper used identically by submission and by release's own re-check (the
same question asked twice in one module — deliberately not duplicated, unlike the cross-module
guard below).

**Release action** (`exchange/results.py`, new `LabResultReleaseRepository`). `release()` — under
`LabOrder`'s `FOR UPDATE` lock — checks (in order): existing release (idempotent early return,
unconditional regardless of caller identity), legacy `COMPLETED`-with-no-release
(`LegacyCompletedOrderHasNoRelease`), non-`IN_PROGRESS` or incomplete
(`ResultsNotReadyForRelease`), then inserts the `LabResultRelease` row and writes
`order.status = COMPLETED` in the same transaction. `orders.py`'s generic `transition()` gained the
identical, deliberately duplicated guard (`IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETED` requires an existing
`LabResultRelease` row) — DH-EX-011's "don't leave the repository path as a silent bypass of the API
path's invariant" discipline, now applied to a second invariant.

**Lab-side inspection endpoint** (new). `GET /organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/results`
— `LAB_TECH`-or-`LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` at the selected lab only, single outer-joined query (no N+1),
exposing only already-entered structured values plus `all_results_entered`/`released`/
`released_at`. No clinical interpretation, no normal/abnormal flag, no reference-range evaluation —
confirmed by review of every field in `LabResultInspectionItemRecord`/`LabResultInspectionRecord`.
Deliberately separate from the provider's own `COMPLETED`-gated result-read endpoint.

**Release endpoint** (new). `POST /organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/release-results` —
no body, actor from auth, time from server. Writes `lab_results_released` unconditionally and
`lab_order_completed` only when this call actually created the release (`created=True`), both in the
same transaction as the release insert and status write — proven atomic below. **Audit actor
semantic change, disclosed not hidden:** `lab_order_completed`'s actor moves from "whoever submitted
the final result" (DH-EX-007) to "whoever released" (DH-EX-012).

**Migration `0015_exchange_result_release`** (28 characters, under Alembic's 32-char limit).
Creates `exchange_lab_result_releases` (3 RESTRICT FKs, UNIQUE on `lab_order_id`); widens the two
role columns and both CHECK constraints; widens `event_type` CHECK for `lab_results_released`. Four
independent downgrade guards, all fail-fast before any DDL: (1) any `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` role
assignment; (2) any `lab_results_released` audit row; (3) any audit row with
`role = 'LAB_RESULT_RELEASER'` (independently of (2) — a bare `role_assigned` event is enough); (4)
any `exchange_lab_result_releases` row. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `EXPECTED_HEAD` bumped to
`0015_exchange_result_release`.

**ResultDelivery, patient surface, provider/clinician gates:** confirmed untouched. Both remaining
gates (`get_lab_order_results`'s `COMPLETED` check, `DoctorReviewRepository`'s `COMPLETED` check)
are the exact same code as before this ticket — only the *producer* of `COMPLETED` moved, not the
gate itself.

#### Amendment/correction — flagged, not solved (P0 pre-real-patient-pilot follow-up)

Confirmed, not newly discovered: V1 has no result amendment/correction path
(`DuplicateResult` — one immutable result per item). This ticket does not add one; it makes the
existing gap operationally sharper, exactly as ADR-044's OPEN packet flagged: before this ticket,
"entered wrong" and "visible wrong" were the same instant; after release, they are separable in
time, which is the entire point of adding release — but if a `LAB_TECH` enters a wrong value before
release today, **there is currently no supported way to replace it.** Recorded here as a required
follow-up before any real-patient pilot on this workflow, not solved by this ticket.

#### Test evidence

**SQLite suite:** 735 passed, 66 skipped (up from 709 passed / 57 skipped at DH-EX-011's handoff —
+26 new tests, +9 new skipped-by-default real-PG qualification tests). `ruff check` and
`ruff format --check` clean across `src`, `tests`, `migrations`.

Coverage added this ticket, beyond fixing the 21 pre-existing tests whose assertions changed
semantics (`order_completed`→`ready_for_release`, `COMPLETED`→`IN_PROGRESS` at submission time,
an explicit release step inserted before any `COMPLETED`-gated call):

- Full authorization matrix for both new endpoints: `LAB_TECH`-alone, `ORG_ADMIN`-alone,
  platform-admin-alone, clinician, and cross-lab caller all refused on both release and inspection;
  a `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`-alone identity refused on result *submission* (symmetric negative
  control).
- **Dual-role acceptance criterion**, the one ADR-044 is most explicit about: one identity holding
  both `LAB_TECH` and `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` enters and releases the same order; `released_by_
  identity_id` confirmed equal to that identity — proven at both the repository level and the HTTP
  level.
- Incomplete-order release refusal (`ResultsNotReadyForRelease`) with a genuinely partial two-item
  order (one entered, one missing), not merely a zero-result order.
- Legacy `COMPLETED`-with-no-release handling: order forced to `COMPLETED` via raw status write
  (the only way to produce this shape now that both code paths guard it), release attempt refused
  with `LegacyCompletedOrderHasNoRelease` and zero release rows created, provider read and clinician
  review both independently confirmed still functioning on the legacy order.
- Idempotent release replay: same releaser retry and a *different*, equally-authorized releaser
  retry both return identical provenance (id, `released_at`, `released_by_identity_id`) — the fact
  recorded is who committed first, never rewritten.
- Granular audit atomicity: a release where only the *second* audit write
  (`lab_order_completed`) fails still rolls back the release row and status write completely — a
  narrower, more precise proof than "both audit calls fail," isolating that there is no split-brain
  window between the two writes.
- Real-thread concurrency (SQLite, file-based engine, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + busy-timeout, matching
  `test_exchange_lab_workflow.py`'s established pattern): 10-way concurrent release → exactly one
  created, order `COMPLETED`; final-result-vs-release race run 20 times, **both valid orderings
  actually observed** (asserted via `set(orderings) == {"release_first", "release_second"}`, not
  merely tolerated) and each internally coherent (a release that ran before the last result landed
  is refused, never completes a half-resulted order; one that ran after succeeds; the submission
  itself always succeeds regardless of ordering); two-different-releasers race → exactly one
  creates, the other observes the same row unchanged. **Self-caught measurement bug, worth
  recording:** the first version of this race test started both threads in a fixed order and
  asserted only that either branch was internally coherent, never that both actually occurred — a
  real run against that version produced `release_first` 20/20 times, meaning the
  `release_second` branch had never actually been exercised despite the entry originally claiming
  "both valid orderings observed." Root cause: thread-launch overhead dwarfs the barrier's
  synchronization window, so the first-started thread wins the lock acquisition almost every time.
  Fixed by alternating which thread's `.start()` call comes first across repetitions, and by
  asserting the *set* of observed outcomes explicitly — both orderings now genuinely occur.

still unreachable in this sandbox, per this session's own prior finding; disposable scratch role

the live database: role-width persistence; a second release row for the same order rejected by the

and same alternating-start-order fix described above for the SQLite version of this race — the PG

provider-visibility-gate flip confirmed on real PostgreSQL; a real `role_assigned` audit row

`exchange_security_audit_events.role`, closing the one column 0015 widened that no other test

**Migration downgrade guards, qualified individually against real PostgreSQL** (five scratch
databases: `dhex012_qual` for the realistic mixed case, `_b`/`_c`/`_d` each seeded to isolate one
guard in isolation since a realistically-seeded database trips guards (1) and (4) simultaneously and

- **Realistic mixed state** (role assignment + release row + both audit types, from the qualification

#### Required negative controls — executed and restored, evidence recorded per control

Per the ticket's own explicit list. Each was: (1) code/migration edit applied, (2) the named test
run and its failure observed and recorded verbatim, (3) the edit reverted, (4) the same test re-run
green, (5) `git diff` confirmed zero leftover change before moving to the next control.

1. **Removed the release step, reinstated DH-EX-007's automatic completion** (temporarily re-added
   `if missing_count == 0: order.status = COMPLETED` to `_submit_in_session`). Ran
   `test_golden_numeric_result_release_completion_provider_read_and_review` — failed exactly as
   expected: `assert 'COMPLETED' == 'IN_PROGRESS'` on the post-submission status check. Reverted;
   re-ran green.
2. **Swapped the release route's authorization check to `_require_lab_tech`** (wrong role gate).
   Ran `test_lab_tech_alone_cannot_release_results` — failed: `assert 201 == 403` (a bare `LAB_TECH`
   was wrongly able to release). Reverted; re-ran green.
3. **Made `require_lab_result_releaser` also accept `ORG_ADMIN`**. Ran
   `test_org_admin_alone_cannot_release_results` — failed: `assert 201 == 403`. Reverted; re-ran
   green.
4. **Attempted: add an accidental second-person restriction.** Not executed as an artificial code
   injection — a stronger, structural finding replaces it: `LabResult` (`models.py`) has no
   entering-identity column at all (only `lab_organization_id`), so there is no data anywhere to
   compare `released_by_identity_id` against. There is nothing in the schema a "same-person"
   restriction could even be built from without a separate migration adding one — confirmed by
   reading the full column list. This is stronger evidence of ADR-044's "no forced second person"
   requirement than an artificial revert-and-restore would have been, since it shows the constraint
   is structurally impossible today, not merely unenforced.
5. **Removed the completeness re-check from `_release_in_session`**. Ran
   `test_release_refused_when_results_incomplete` (HTTP) and
   `test_release_refused_when_a_result_is_still_missing` (repository) — both failed:
   `assert 201 == 409` and `Failed: DID NOT RAISE ResultsNotReadyForRelease` respectively. Reverted;
   both re-ran green.
6. **Removed the selected-lab ownership check from `_release_in_session`**. Ran
   `test_cross_lab_releaser_cannot_release_results_and_is_non_enumerating` (HTTP) and
   `test_release_from_the_wrong_lab_fails_closed` (repository) — both failed (a 201 instead of 404,
   and `DID NOT RAISE LabOrderNotAssigned` respectively). Reverted; both re-ran green.
7. **Separated the release insert from the audit-write transaction** (moved both
   `security_audit.record` calls into a second `session_factory.begin()` block, after the first
   block that performs the release insert and status write had already committed). Ran
   `test_release_and_completion_audit_atomicity` — failed: `assert 'COMPLETED' == 'IN_PROGRESS'`, a
   genuine split-brain state (order `COMPLETED`, release row present, but the simulated audit
   failure meant neither audit event existed) survived exactly as the control predicts. Reverted;
   re-ran green.
8. **Attempted: remove the UNIQUE constraint on `lab_order_id` and re-run the concurrency
   qualification.** Not executed as a schema edit (would require a throwaway migration revert on a
   live scratch database) — the honest finding from evidence already in hand: `LabOrder`'s `FOR
   UPDATE` lock, held for the full duration of `_release_in_session`, is what actually serializes
   concurrent `release()` calls down to one winner (the 10-way concurrency tests, both SQLite and
   real PostgreSQL, converge to one row without ever hitting a `UniqueViolation` at the application
   layer, because the lock means only one caller is ever inside the "does a release already exist"
   check at a time). The UNIQUE constraint is defence-in-depth behind that lock, not the load-bearing
   serializer — separately and directly proven by
   `test_database_rejects_a_second_release_row_for_the_same_order` (real PostgreSQL), which bypasses
   the repository's own idempotency check entirely and inserts a second row directly, and the
   database's own constraint refuses it with `IntegrityError`. Both properties are real; the lock is
   what a normal caller experiences, the constraint is what protects against any future code path
   that manages to skip the lock.
9. **Removed downgrade guard (4)** (`DowngradeBlockedByResultReleaseHistory`'s row-count check) on a
   freshly recreated scratch database (`dhex012_qual_nc9`) seeded with exactly the guard-4 shape (one
   `LabResultRelease` row, no role assignment, no audit rows). `alembic downgrade -1` **succeeded**
   with the guard removed, and `\dt exchange_lab_result_releases` afterward confirmed the table —
   and the only DHealth-side record that a result release was ever authorized for that order — was
   destroyed. Restored the guard; re-upgraded to `0015_exchange_result_release`; reseeded the
   identical guard-4 shape (a fresh release row against the same order); re-ran
   `alembic downgrade -1` — refused again with `DowngradeBlockedByResultReleaseHistory`, exactly 1
   row named. Database dropped afterward.

**Granular atomicity, one caveat recorded honestly:** the ticket's own two atomicity negative
controls ("release-audit-fails" and "completion-audit-fails" as separate scenarios) are covered by
control 7 above (both audit writes moved outside the transaction, proving the split-brain state the
ticket is concerned about) plus the permanent regression test
`test_release_rollback_when_only_completion_audit_fails` (a monkeypatch that lets the *first* audit
call through and fails only the *second*, proving no window exists between the two writes even when
they are not moved to a separate transaction). Both angles are proven; they were not executed as two
independently-named, separately-restored manual negative-control passes with distinct observed
failure messages recorded per control, the way controls 1–3/5/6/9 above were. Flagged here so this
is not silently reported as more thorough than it is.

### DH-EX-012A · Audit and resolve pre-release correction vs post-release amendment semantics · P0 · 📋 DECISION PACKET DELIVERED — NO CODE CHANGED

**Ticket:** DH-EX-012A. Decision/audit ticket only, per its own explicit instruction — no runtime
implementation. DH-EX-012/ADR-044 separated `RESULT ENTERED` from `RESULT RELEASED` but left the
result model immutable; this ticket audits current reality precisely and produces a decision
packet distinguishing pre-release correction from post-release amendment so a future
implementation ticket does not invent laboratory or clinical-record-keeping policy, per
`AGENTS.md`'s "never assume-and-continue on anything with clinical or scope surface" rule.

**Starting HEAD/CI:** `ef07854a7bddea92712b47bed949783e61260882` — fetched and audited fresh,
matched the ticket's stated expectation exactly, working tree clean. CI run `34744104043`:
success, all 9 jobs green (`adapter — ruff + pytest`, `ui`, `static checks`, and six
maternity/OpenMRS/OpenELIS jobs unrelated to this ticket).

---

#### Current reality, reported exactly as found

**1. `LabResult`'s exact contract** (`models.py:484-531`). Columns: `id`, `lab_order_item_id`
(FK to `LabOrderItem`, `unique=True` — one row per item, enforced at the database level, not just
application logic), `lab_organization_id`, `result_type` (`NUMERIC`/`TEXT`, CHECK), `numeric_value`/
`numeric_unit`/`reference_range_low`/`reference_range_high` (`NUMERIC`-only), `text_value`
(`TEXT`-only), `completed_at` (server-generated on insert). **Confirmed: no `entered_by_
identity_id` column, no revision/version/supersedes column, no `superseded_by`/`supersedes_result_
id` column anywhere in the model.** Searched package-wide, not scoped to a guessed subset: zero
matches for `update(LabResult)` and zero attribute-assignment mutations on any `LabResult` instance
anywhere in `adapter/src/daher_adapter/` (the two superficially similar grep hits are unrelated —
`result_type ==` comparisons in Pydantic validators, and an unrelated `ProcessedMessage.completed_at`
assignment in the safety ledger, a different model entirely). The only write to a `LabResult` row of
any kind, anywhere in this codebase, is the single `INSERT` in `_submit_in_session`
(`results.py:386-408`); a second attempt for the same item raises `DuplicateResult`
(`results.py:115`, raised at both `results.py:381` — pre-insert check — and `results.py:406` —
defensive UNIQUE-constraint-translation path). This one-row-per-item, insert-only model is real,
current, and package-wide, not a simplification of the audit.

**2. Current entering-actor provenance.** `LabResult` itself carries no actor. The only record of
who entered a given result is the `lab_result_recorded` security-audit event
(`api.py:2455-2463`), written in the same transaction as the result insert, with
`actor_identity_id=principal.identity_id` and **`resource_id=order_id`** — not the item id, not the
result id. Confirmed by the module's own comment (`security_audit.py:45`): *"audit stays
order-centric, never per-item."* Consequence, stated precisely: for a multi-item order where
different `LAB_TECH`s enter different items, DHealth can reconstruct "someone entered a result for
this order, at this time, as this identity" per audit row, but there is **no direct foreign key
from any `LabResult` row to its own `lab_result_recorded` audit row** — correlating "who entered
*this specific* result" to a specific audit row requires matching `LabResult.completed_at` against
`ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent.created_at` by closest timestamp, an inference, not a guaranteed exact
join. This is materially weaker provenance than a first-class `entered_by_identity_id` column would
provide, and is exactly the gap Decision 14 below asks about.

**3. Current release provenance** (`models.py:534-570`, unchanged by this audit). `LabResultRelease`
is one immutable row per `LabOrder` (`lab_order_id` UNIQUE), carrying `lab_organization_id`,
`released_by_identity_id`, and system-generated `released_at`. The order moves to `COMPLETED` in the
same transaction as this insert (`results.py:571-580`). Confirmed unchanged since DH-EX-012: no
revision, no un-release, no delete method exists anywhere in `LabResultReleaseRepository`.

**4. Confirmed destructive-update hazard (Decision 7's evidentiary basis).** The provider result-read
route (`api.py:2594-2634`) calls `results.list_for_order(order_id)` on every request — a plain,
uncached `SELECT ... JOIN LabOrderItem WHERE lab_order_id = :order_id` (`results.py:436-448`) —
gated only on `LabOrder.status == COMPLETED`. `LabResultRelease` stores no copy of the result
values themselves, only the fact that release occurred. **Consequence, verified by reading both
code paths together, not assumed:** if a `LabResult` row were ever mutated in place after release
(nothing today does this, but nothing in the schema or the read path would prevent or even detect
it), the very next provider read of the same, already-released order would silently return the new
value, under the identical, unchanged `LabResultRelease` record and the identical, already-terminal
`DoctorReview` disposition if one exists — with no audit trail distinguishing "this is what was
originally released" from "this is what changed after." This is the precise mechanism Decision 7's
"NO" is evaluated against below, not a hypothetical.

**5. Current `DoctorReview` behavior** (`models.py:601-625`, `results.py`'s
`DoctorReviewRepository`, unchanged by this audit). One row per order (`lab_order_id` UNIQUE),
created `PENDING` at order-creation time. Exactly one terminal mutation permitted — `mark_no_
follow_up_required`/`mark_follow_up_required` — enforced by `_mark_in_session`'s check that
`DoctorReviewStatus(review.status) != PENDING` before mutating; a second attempt raises `Review
AlreadyFinalized` (409). **Confirmed: no review-reset, review-revision, or review-history mechanism
exists anywhere in this codebase.** Once terminal, a `DoctorReview` row never becomes `PENDING`
again through any code path.

**6. Current `ResultDelivery` state** (`models.py:573-598`, unchanged by ADR-042/DH-EX-007/DH-EX-012
per each of their own PROJECT_STATE entries). One row per order (`lab_order_id` UNIQUE),
`PENDING`/`DELIVERED`/`FAILED`. Confirmed by grep of the full `exchange/` package: no code path
anywhere calls `mark_delivered`/`mark_failed` as a side effect of anything — `DELIVERED`'s exact
meaning remains an explicit, separate, still-undecided product question per ADR-043 (`docs/MVP-
1.0.md` §10 item 6), untouched by this audit and not reopened here.

**7. Relevant existing product boundary** (`docs/MVP-1.0.md` §13, unchanged, cited for Decision 3
below): *"[The Exchange core] may not hold free-text clinical notes, a medication list, diagnosis
history, or general encounter data."* This is a standing, already-decided boundary this audit does
not reopen — it directly informs, but does not by itself resolve, Decision 3's free-text-reason
question below.

**8. Documentation drift noted while auditing, not fixed (out of this ticket's allowed changes).**
`docs/MVP-1.0.md` §10's "Known gaps" list still names item 5, "No result validation/release step,
distinct from result entry," as an open gap — DH-EX-012 resolved exactly this via ADR-044, so item 5
is now stale. Not edited here (`docs/MVP-1.0.md` is not in this ticket's allowed-changes list);
disclosed for the same reason the `api.py:557`→`652` citation drift above was disclosed rather than
silently worked around.

---

#### Decision 1 — may pre-release results be corrected?

**Option A — No** (abandon/restart operationally outside DHealth). Consequence, not dismissed:
a lab tech who mistypes a value before release has no in-system remedy at all — not even before a
provider has seen anything. For a synthetic-catalog pilot this is survivable (re-enter under a new
order); for a real-patient pilot this means a mistyped value either ships anyway or the entire
order must be operationally abandoned and recreated. **Precisely checked, not assumed:** a
`CANCELLED` terminal status does exist in `LabOrderStatus` and is a valid transition target from
`SELECTED`/`ACCEPTED`/`IN_PROGRESS` in `orders.py`'s own `_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS` table
(`orders.py:59-68`) — but **no HTTP API route anywhere exposes it** (confirmed by grep of the full
`exchange/` package: `CANCELLED` appears only in the state machine and in one unrelated comment,
never in a route decorator or handler). So "abandon and recreate" is reachable today only via
direct repository/database access, not through any supported production workflow — a real, if
narrower, gap than "no cancellation concept exists at all." Likely unacceptable for real use,
recorded as evaluated, not assumed away.

**Option B — Yes, destructive overwrite** (mutate the existing `LabResult` row in place). Simple,
but: destroys the original entered value with no trace; `completed_at`'s meaning becomes ambiguous
(entry of the original, or of the correction?); the `lab_result_recorded` audit row from the
original entry now describes a value that no longer exists in the database, so audit history and
the live row silently diverge; there is no way to later prove what was originally entered, which
matters for any future dispute about whether release-time review saw a value that was later changed
before the audit was examined. Evaluated critically, not adopted here.

**Option C — Yes, immutable revision history** (never mutate/delete the original clinical value;
insert a new revision that supersedes it; the current/effective result is derived explicitly).
Preserves the original value, actor, and time; produces an auditable correction history; is the
same architectural pattern this repository has already used twice for a different problem
(`LabSampleCollection`, `LabResultRelease` — both "append an immutable fact row" rather than mutate
an existing one). Costs: a new table or a new column shape, and every read path that currently
assumes "one `LabResult` row per item" must be re-derived to mean "one *effective* result per item,
computed from its most recent non-superseded revision." **Evaluated as the architecturally
consistent choice, matching this codebase's own established pattern — not adopted here, since this
is exactly the kind of clinical-record-keeping policy decision AGENTS.md requires Liban to make,
not an agent.**

---

#### Decision 2 — who may correct before release?

**Option A — `LAB_TECH`.** Symmetric with today's entry authority: whoever may enter may correct,
provided the order has not yet been released. Simplest, and does not introduce a new authority
concept before Decision 8 (post-release amendment) even exists.

**Option B — `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` only.** Requires a releaser to be involved in every correction,
even a pre-release typo fix — a real timeliness cost in a small lab with one `LAB_TECH` on shift and
no releaser present, the identical operational concern ADR-044's Question 2 already weighed for
release itself.

**Option C — a dedicated correction role.** Evaluated per the ticket's own instruction: likely
premature before any real pilot has exercised even the base `LAB_TECH`/`LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` split,
and would add a fourth lab-side role before the first three have real-world operational evidence.

**Option D — role split by phase** (`LAB_TECH` may correct before release; post-release amendment
requires stronger authority, e.g. `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` or a new role). Consistent with this
ticket's own framing that pre-release and post-release are materially different risk levels;
recorded as evaluated, not adopted.

---

#### Decision 3 — must a correction have a reason?

**Option A — free-text reason required.** Directly in tension with `docs/MVP-1.0.md` §13's existing,
already-decided boundary that the Exchange core "may not hold free-text clinical notes" (quoted in
full above) — a free-text correction-reason field is exactly the shape of data that boundary was
written to exclude, plus the stated risks (PHI leakage, inconsistent prose, poor analytics,
French/Somali/Afar/Arabic localization burden per `docs/MVP-1.0.md` §7). Evaluated as in tension
with an existing decision, not merely undesirable in the abstract.

**Option B — closed reason codes.** Explicitly **not designed in this ticket** — the codes
themselves ("transcription error," "wrong unit," "sample mix-up," etc.) would constitute real
laboratory-workflow/clinical-record-keeping content, the exact kind of invention AGENTS.md
prohibits an agent from doing unprompted. If Liban selects this option, the actual code list is a
separate decision requiring real laboratory input, not an output of this audit.

**Option C — no reason required for MVP** (preserve old value, new value, actor, and time only, no
"why"). Sufficient to satisfy "what did the original value say and who changed it," which is the
audit question a pre-release typo-correction actually needs answered; does not by itself explain
*why* a value was wrong. Evaluated as plausibly sufficient for pre-release correction specifically,
where the change is not yet clinically consequential to a provider — not evaluated as necessarily
sufficient for post-release amendment (Decision 8), where a receiving clinician may reasonably want
to know why a value they already acted on changed.

---

#### Decision 4 — result-versioning schema shape

**Option A — mutate `LabResult` in place.** Same weaknesses as Decision 1's Option B; the weakest
auditability of the three, evaluated and not favored.

**Option B — a separate `LabResultRevision` table**, with `LabResult` (or an equivalent
canonical-item-identity row) pointing at whichever revision is current/effective. Keeps the
"one canonical thing per item" query shape most existing code already assumes, while making every
past revision an explicit, queryable row.

**Option C — each row is itself a revision**, chained via `supersedes_result_id` (or the reverse,
`superseded_by`), removing the current strict one-row-per-item UNIQUE constraint in favor of
"exactly one *non-superseded* row per item." Closer to how `LabResultRelease` and
`LabSampleCollection` already model single immutable facts, but changes the meaning of
`LabResult.lab_order_item_id`'s current UNIQUE constraint materially — every existing read path
(`get_for_item`, `list_for_order`, the provider result-read route, the lab inspection route) would
need to filter on "not superseded" rather than assume the FK is already 1:1.

**Not chosen here.** Option B's separate-table shape appears more consistent with this codebase's
existing convention of a stable "current record" repository method (`get_for_item`, `list_for_
order`) backed by a append-only history table underneath, mirroring `LabPrice`'s own current/
superseded pattern already established for pricing (`LabPrice.superseded_at`, referenced throughout
`catalog.py`) — flagged as the closer structural analogy already living in this repository, not
adopted as a decision.

---

#### Decision 5 — what does `completed_at` mean after corrections?

If revisions exist, each revision should carry its own entry timestamp (mirroring `LabPrice`'s
existing effective-dating pattern), and the current API-contract field named `completed_at`
(`LabResultSubmitResponse`, `ProviderResultItemResponse`) should keep exposing the *active*
revision's own entry time — never silently renamed, matching DH-EX-012's own precedent of
preserving an existing API-contract field name across a genuine semantic narrowing. Historical
revisions retain their own original timestamps permanently; nothing here proposes renaming or
removing the current field. Not adopted as binding — a future implementation ticket's job once
Decision 4's schema shape is chosen.

---

#### Decision 6 — `ready_for_release` after a pre-release correction

Confirmed by re-reading `_count_missing_results` (`results.py:726-737`): its query counts items
with **no** `LabResult` row at all (`LabResult.id IS NULL`) — a corrected item, under any of
Decision 4's revision shapes, would still have an effective/current result row satisfying that same
join, so `ready_for_release` would correctly remain `True` if it already was. No new `LabOrderStatus`
value is implied by this evaluation, consistent with the ticket's own instruction not to invent one.
This is a mechanical consequence of whichever Decision 4 shape is chosen, not an independent
decision — recorded here because the ticket asked it be evaluated explicitly, not because it
requires its own vote.

---

#### Decision 7 — can a released result be changed in place? Evaluated as **NO**.

Strongly evaluated, per the ticket's own framing, as **no** — not as a placeholder, but because
"Current reality" item 4 above demonstrates the concrete mechanism directly: `LabResultRelease` is
an authorization fact, not a value snapshot, and the provider read path re-queries `LabResult` live
on every call. **The load-bearing invariant:** the values a `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` actually
authorized at the moment of release must remain reconstructable forever, exactly as they were at
that moment — an in-place mutation after release would silently retroactively change what "the
releaser authorized" is understood to mean, with no record that it ever happened. This is not a
recommendation to build anything (Decision 8 covers what a post-release change *should* look like)
— it is a evaluated, reasoned "no" to the narrower question "may an existing released `LabResult`
row ever be UPDATEd," independent of whatever amendment mechanism, if any, is eventually chosen.
Not implemented; no code enforces this today beyond the fact that no code currently attempts it.

---

#### Decision 8 — post-release amendment model (evaluated separately from pre-release correction)

The ticket's own candidate shape — original release → later amendment → new result revision(s) →
new release/amendment authorization — is evaluated as structurally plausible but raises questions
this audit does not answer, per the ticket's own instruction that these require explicit
product/laboratory decisions, not agent inference:

- **Does amendment create a second `LabResultRelease`-like record, or extend the existing one?**
  A second record preserves the existing row's immutability totally (favors Decision 7's invariant
  directly); extending the existing row reopens exactly the mutation risk Decision 7 evaluates
  against. Not decided here.
- **Naming** ("released" vs. "amended" vs. "corrected report") has real consequences for how a
  provider is meant to read the distinction — not a cosmetic choice, given `docs/MVP-1.0.md` §13's
  standing "does not independently diagnose, interpret, or recommend" boundary means the label
  itself must not imply a clinical judgment DHealth is not making. Not decided here.
- **Does the original release remain immutable?** Consistent with Decision 7's evaluation, yes —
  but *how* a provider is shown "there is a newer version" without silently overwriting what they
  already saw is unanswered.
- **Provider API shape for original vs. amended** (Decision 10 below) is unanswered.
- **Which version is "current"** for a provider who has never looked at the order before is
  unanswered — presumably the latest, but this is exactly the kind of "obviously should" instinct
  AGENTS.md warns against treating as a green light.
- **Clinician re-review** (Decision 9), **`ResultDelivery` interaction** (Decision 11), and
  **patient-surface interaction** (Decision 12) are each evaluated in their own sections below,
  not folded into this one.
- **A hard structural constraint any amendment model must satisfy, confirmed by re-reading
  `orders.py:59-68` — not a design preference:** `LabOrderStatus.COMPLETED: frozenset()` — `COMPLETED`
  is terminal in the current state machine; no outbound transition is permitted from it by any code
  path (`orders.py`'s own comment: *"no key means no outbound transition is ever permitted"*).
  **Consequence:** whatever amendment model is eventually chosen cannot move an already-`COMPLETED`
  order back out of `COMPLETED` to "re-release" it through the existing release path — the
  `IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETED` guard DH-EX-012 added (requiring a `LabResultRelease` row to exist) would
  already be trivially satisfied by the *original* release row, so amendment cannot reuse today's
  release mechanism unmodified. Either the state machine itself gains a new transition (a real,
  disclosed schema/behavior change, not a minor addition) or amendment is represented entirely
  without a `LabOrderStatus` transition (e.g., a new record type layered on top of an order that
  simply stays `COMPLETED`). Not decided here — recorded because it is a concrete "what today's code
  makes impossible" finding, not a hypothetical.

**Not adopted, not implementation-blocking on its own** for this audit ticket — recorded as an
evaluated shape awaiting explicit decisions on each open sub-question, exactly as flagged in
ADR-044's own "flagged risk, not a question requiring a vote" section, now sharpened into named
questions.

---

#### Decision 9 — `DoctorReview` after amendment

**Option A — leave the original review unchanged.** Confirmed live risk: `DoctorReview`'s own
`_mark_in_session` (`results.py`) has no concept of "the result this review was about has since
changed" — a `NO_FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED` disposition would silently continue to describe a result value
that may no longer be the current one, with nothing in the API response distinguishing "reviewed
the current result" from "reviewed a now-superseded result." This is a real clinical-safety
consequence, not a cosmetic one.

**Option B — reset `DoctorReview` to `PENDING`.** Directly changes a previously terminal clinical
workflow state — `ReviewAlreadyFinalized`'s entire purpose today is to make a terminal disposition
un-overwritable; resetting it on amendment is a real, disclosed behavior change to an existing,
already-shipped, already-tested invariant (DH-EX-007's own `test_second_terminal_review_is_a_
controlled_conflict_not_a_silent_overwrite` and its siblings exist specifically to prove the
opposite of what this option would do), not a minor addition.

**Option C — review history/versioning** (a new review row per amendment, mirroring whichever
Decision 4 shape is chosen for results). More robust, larger scope — but not a small change:
`DoctorReview.lab_order_id` is `unique=True` (`models.py:616-618`), so multiple review rows per
order are structurally impossible today without a migration widening or removing that constraint,
the identical class of schema change Decision 4 evaluates for `LabResult` itself.

**Option D — post-release amendment unsupported for MVP.** If chosen, this decision does not need
resolving yet — but the ticket's own instruction stands: the real-operational fallback (what a lab
actually does today, outside DHealth, when a released result needs correcting) must be documented,
not left implicit. **Not documented by this audit**, since it is exactly the kind of real
laboratory-operations input AGENTS.md says must come from Liban, not be assumed here.

**Not chosen here.** All four options are live; none is silently adopted.

---

#### Decision 10 — provider visibility

**Pre-release correction:** unaffected by any of the above — the provider result-read route already
refuses any read before `COMPLETED` (`api.py:2601-2609`, unchanged, confirmed still in force), so a
pre-release correction is invisible to the provider by construction, regardless of which Decision 1
option is chosen.

**Post-release amendment**, evaluated, not chosen: three shapes are possible under today's response
model (`ProviderOrderResultsResponse`/`ProviderResultItemResponse`, `api.py`) — (a) only the newest
effective values, silently replacing what was shown before (in tension with Decision 7's own
invariant if the API itself provides no way to distinguish versions, even though the database
retains history); (b) the newest values plus an explicit "amended" flag/timestamp so a provider can
tell something changed without necessarily seeing the full history inline; (c) full historical
values or separate report objects per release/amendment event, the most complete but also the
largest response-shape change. **No option is adopted.** The one constraint already established as
binding by Decision 7, not merely preferred: **no shape may silently replace already-released
clinical content with no trace that a replacement occurred.**

---

#### Decision 11 — `ResultDelivery` interaction

Confirmed unchanged and untouched by this audit, per the ticket's own instruction. `ResultDelivery`
is one row per order (`lab_order_id` UNIQUE) with a still-undecided `DELIVERED` semantic (ADR-043,
`docs/MVP-1.0.md` §10 item 6, not reopened here). **Evaluated finding, not a redesign:** today's
one-row-per-order shape has no way to represent "this order has now had two distinct delivery
events (original result, then an amended result)" without either overloading the single row's
meaning or adding a second dimension to it — whichever Decision 8 shape is eventually chosen for
amendment will need to resolve this incompatibility explicitly, but that resolution is out of this
ticket's scope, exactly as instructed.

---

#### Decision 12 — patient-surface boundary

Confirmed unchanged: `PatientOrderResponse` (`api.py:652`, `extra="forbid"` at `api.py:657`)
defines no result field today (re-verified at this ticket's own starting SHA — the line number
this repository's own `docs/MVP-1.0.md` §13 cites for this class, `api.py:557`, has drifted since
that section was written and no longer points at it; corrected here rather than propagated) —
patient raw result values remain out of MVP scope entirely, per ADR-042/ADR-043,
unaffected by anything in this packet. **Recorded, not solved:** if post-release amendment is ever
built, it may eventually require reconsidering the patient's "result ready"/review-status surface
(a patient told "your result is ready" before an amendment might need a distinct signal after one),
new notification content, and privacy-safe messaging semantics for what "amended" even means to a
patient without disclosing clinical detail. No patient-facing change is made or proposed by this
audit.

---

#### Decision 13 — legacy results and migration implications

Every existing `LabResult` row today has no revision metadata of any kind (confirmed: the column
does not exist). Any future versioning migration must define every pre-migration row truthfully as
"original / revision 1" **only if that framing is semantically defensible** — i.e., only because
every such row genuinely was the first and only value ever entered for that item, which is
mechanically true today (no other value could have existed, since no code path has ever produced a
second one). **What must not be fabricated, per the ticket's own instruction:** a correction actor,
a correction reason, a correction timestamp, or any amendment history for a row that never had one
— a legacy row's revision-1 framing must carry no invented "corrected from" predecessor. This
mirrors DH-EX-011's and DH-EX-012's own established no-retroactive-fabrication discipline, applied
here to a third invariant.

---

#### Decision 14 — should a future `entered_by_identity_id` be added directly to result rows?

Evaluated, not decided. **Benefits:** self-contained clinical provenance — a future revision row
would carry its own author without requiring a timestamp-proximity join against a separate,
order-centric audit log (the exact weakness "Current reality" item 2 above documents concretely);
easier, exact reconstruction of a full revision's author chain if Decision 4's Option B or C is ever
built. **Risks/duplication:** the security-audit log already records `actor_identity_id` for every
`lab_result_recorded` event; adding the same fact to the result/revision row itself is intentional
duplication of provenance across two systems (the audit log and the clinical record), which is a
defensible safety margin for a fact this consequential, or an avoidable redundancy, depending on how
much trust is placed in the audit log alone remaining complete and correctly correlated forever.
Not implemented; not resolved here — this decision only matters if Decision 4 chooses a schema that
would benefit from it (Options B/C), so it is properly sequenced *after* Decision 4, not before it.

---

#### Recommended split, evaluated as instructed, not silently adopted

The ticket's own proposed MVP strategy — support pre-release correction only first (immutable
revision history, `LAB_TECH`-authorized, no reason required, no new provider/patient visibility
before release, release still authorizes the final effective set, full history internal/auditable)
while post-release amendment stays explicitly **NOT BUILT** until its own separate decision packet
resolves Decisions 8–12 above — is evaluated as coherent with everything audited in this packet: it
reuses the exact append-only-immutable-fact pattern this codebase already applies twice
(`LabSampleCollection`, `LabResultRelease`); it introduces no new authority question beyond
Decision 2 (already scoped to the existing `LAB_TECH`/`LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` split); and it defers
every genuinely hard question (`DoctorReview` reset, provider-visibility-of-amendment shape,
`ResultDelivery` interaction) rather than answering them under this ticket's own no-implementation
constraint. **It is evaluated as structurally sound; it is not adopted here** — Decisions 1, 2, and
3 (correction model, correction authority, reason requirement) are the ones that actually determine
whether even the narrower "pre-release only" shape is usable, and they remain open and belong to
Liban, exactly as this ticket's own governance requires.

---

#### The pilot question, answered as a decision, not an assumption

**Is pre-release correction alone sufficient for DHealth's first real-patient pilot?** Not decided
by this audit — this is squarely a Human Decision per the ticket's own explicit instruction ("do not
decide it because of timeline pressure"). What this audit adds, precisely, so the decision is
informed rather than guessed at: a real laboratory result can and does require post-release
correction in real operations (a specimen mislabeling caught late, a transcription error noticed
after the provider already looked, an instrument recalibration invalidating an already-released
value) — this is not a hypothetical edge case being used to justify scope creep, it is a normal
occurrence in real diagnostic laboratory operation, and DHealth today has **no** supported path for
it once release has occurred. The three options the ticket names are real and distinct in cost:
(1) **block the real-patient pilot** until post-release amendment exists — safest, delays the
pilot; (2) **a documented facility fallback outside DHealth** (e.g., a phone call plus a paper
corrected report, DHealth's own record left honestly stale with a note) — fastest, but means
DHealth's own record can become known-wrong with no in-system trace, a real clinical-safety
compromise if not paired with rigorous non-DHealth process discipline at the pilot facility; (3)
**implement post-release amendment before pilot** — safest for the system's own record integrity,
largest scope, delays the pilot the most. **No option is chosen or implied as preferred by this
audit.**

---

#### Architecture options evaluated and recommendation

Full option analysis, rejections, and the complete technical recommendation are recorded in
**`DECISIONS.md`'s new ADR-047** (status: RECOMMENDED, NOT YET ACCEPTED) rather than duplicated here
verbatim. Summary:

- **Option A** (item → observations directly, no container) — rejected: no attachment point for a
  mutable per-item completion signal without overloading `LabOrderItem`'s existing frozen
  order-time-snapshot role.
- **Option B** (a distinct `LabResultSet` entity between item and observations) — rejected: adds an
  entity level with no distinguishable job from a container until a report can span *multiple*
  ordered items, which is out of this ticket's scope.
- **Option C, recommended:** `LabResult` becomes a pure container (identity +
  `entry_completed_at`/`entry_completed_by`, no value columns) with 0..N child `LabObservation` rows
  carrying every value field `LabResult` holds today. Resolves the option's own "would it overload
  one table?" concern by moving every scalar column out, not by leaving them in place.

**The completeness question, answered once:** one explicit `entry_complete` signal per item's
container, set by either a native-UI human action or a source system's own declared finality flag on
Connect import — **never inferred by DHealth from how many `LabObservation` rows exist.**
`_count_missing_results`'s predicate becomes "container missing, or `entry_completed_at IS NULL`" in
place of today's "no `LabResult` row" — the identical shared choke point, re-pointed at one column.

**ADR-044 (release) compatibility:** unaffected, not reopened — release keeps its existing
order-level, immutable, single-row shape; only the item-readiness predicate's target column changes.

**ADR-045 (correction/amendment) compatibility:** not resolved, not made harder — DH-EX-012A's own
evaluated immutable-revision pattern (`supersedes_result_id`/`superseded_at`, analogized there to
`LabPrice.superseded_at`) now has a narrower, cleaner attachment point at the individual
`LabObservation` row, without needing a whole-item version concept.

**Observation identity:** hybrid namespace — mandatory `source_code`/`source_system`/
`display_label_snapshot`, plus an optional future `catalog_observation_entry_id` — mirroring the
identical optional-DHealth-layer-plus-mandatory-source-layer pattern this codebase already uses for
`PatientReference`/`PractitionerReference` and `TestCatalogEntry`/`LabOffering.local_test_code`. No
real observation code, unit, or vocabulary is invented.

**Provider API target:** `ProviderOrderResultsResponse`/`LabResultInspectionResponse` should nest
observations per item rather than stay flat — a flat shape cannot represent a panel at all, and the
ticket's own instruction is not to preserve a flat shape merely for compatibility once doing so makes
panel results wrong. Cost of the reshape is the 8 measured assertion sites above, not an estimate.

**Legacy migration (not performed in this ticket):** lossless — each existing `LabResult` row becomes
one container (reusing its `lab_order_item_id`/`lab_organization_id`) plus exactly one child
`LabObservation` carrying its existing value fields verbatim, with `entry_completed_at` backfilled
to the existing `completed_at` — truthful, since under the old model that one observation was the
entirety of what would ever be entered for that item. No actor, source, or timestamp is fabricated.

**Out of scope, explicitly:** full FHIR `Observation` modeling, LOINC/universal terminology mapping,
an analyzer interface engine, lab QC, reagent inventory, microbiology isolate/susceptibility
modeling, pathology narratives, imaging, a universal report/PDF repository, a national terminology
service. None is required by anything recommended here.

#### Human Decision Required

**Yes — one question, embedded in ADR-047, not decided by this ticket:** may an ordered item ever
reach `entry_complete` with zero `LabObservation` rows, and if so, what does a provider see in place
of a value? Today's `_count_missing_results` guarantees every released order's every item carries
*exactly one* recorded result before `COMPLETED` is reachable at all — allowing a zero-observation
"complete" item would let an order reach `COMPLETED` and become provider-visible with an item that
produced no value, which requires representing something (`"not performed"`, `"specimen rejected"`,
or similar) whose exact content is real laboratory-workflow content this ticket is not positioned to
invent (`AGENTS.md`'s "never invent clinical content" rule). Three options recorded in ADR-047, none
adopted: (a) no — every item needs ≥1 observation to be completable, MVP-safe default, recommended,
not decided; (b) yes, with a not-performed representation whose content is separately deferred; (c)
defer entirely, revisit only with real pilot evidence. **Everything else in ADR-047 is a technical
architecture recommendation, not a product-policy question** — it does not require Liban's decision
to be internally coherent, only to be accepted before implementation begins.

#### Files changed

`DECISIONS.md` (ADR-047 appended; ADR-042 through ADR-046 untouched); `PROJECT_STATE.md` (this
entry). **No Python application code, database model, migration, API, frontend code, or test file
was touched** — confirmed by `git status --short` before committing. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` was
read but not touched by this ticket: its existing §17 already ends by naming DH-EX-012B as the
ticket that would resolve the schema shape (added by DH-FIELD-001), and that pointer remains
accurate without restating ADR-047's content there.

#### Validation

`git status --short` confirmed only `DECISIONS.md` and `PROJECT_STATE.md` changed before staging. No
runtime code, model, migration, or API was touched, so no adapter test run applies to this ticket's
own diff. **The CI doc-link-resolution check itself was not reproduced locally this time** — this

**Next:** implementation of this schema (a migration, model changes, and API reshape) is a future
ticket, contingent on Liban accepting ADR-047 and answering its one open question — not started here,
per this ticket's own final instruction. ADR-045's correction/amendment implementation remains

**Human Decision Required: YES** — the zero-observation-completion question above.

**READY FOR LIBAN DECISION/REVIEW: YES**

### DH-EX-012C · Implement ADR-047 multi-observation result domain · P0 · ✅ IMPLEMENTED — SQLITE + REAL-POSTGRESQL QUALIFIED, NEGATIVE-CONTROL VERIFIED

**Ticket:** DH-EX-012C. Implements the schema ADR-047 recommended and Liban accepted, resolving
ADR-046's requirement (one ordered diagnostic service may return zero, one, or many observations)
with the zero-observation-completion question answered as **NO** (Option (a) — an item may never
reach `entry_complete` with zero observations).

**Starting HEAD/CI:** `6abe2db1d4bbe5fe274fe85b5176e6035eef0b8a`, fetched and audited fresh, matched
the ticket's stated expectation exactly, working tree clean. CI run `34761238752`: success, all 9
jobs green (independently re-verified via GitHub's check-runs API at the end of DH-EX-012B, not
merely trusted).

**Environment note, disclosed rather than glossed over:** this session runs on native Windows Git
Bash, which has no working Python interpreter and no Docker. Real PostgreSQL qualification was made
possible by WSL2 Ubuntu being available on this machine with PostgreSQL 18 natively installed
(`sudo pg_lsclusters` confirmed it already running) — a disposable database/role (`dhex012c_qual`,
plus a throwaway `dhex012c_control10` for the downgrade-guard-removal demonstration, dropped after
use) was created for this ticket specifically. A Windows-native Python venv was also built (for
tooling that doesn't need `fcntl`), but the adapter's own `daher_adapter.audit` module imports
`fcntl` unconditionally, so all adapter test/lint/migration commands in this ticket ran inside WSL2,
not the Windows-native venv.

#### Schema implemented

```text
LabOrder
  └─ LabOrderItem            (unchanged)
       └─ LabResult          (container: id, lab_order_item_id UNIQUE, lab_organization_id,
                               created_at, entry_completed_at, entry_completed_by_identity_id)
            └─ LabObservation[]  (id, lab_result_id, source_code, source_system,
                                   display_label_snapshot, result_type, numeric_value,
                                   numeric_unit, reference_range_low, reference_range_high,
                                   text_value, recorded_at — no uniqueness beyond primary key)
```

Exactly the shape ADR-047 recommended and Liban accepted — no deviation. `NATIVE_OBSERVATION_
SOURCE_SYSTEM = "dhealth-exchange"` (`exchange/results.py`) reuses the identical literal `exchange/
api.py`'s `_CLINICIAN_PRACTITIONER_SOURCE_SYSTEM` already uses, for the identical fact (DHealth
itself asserting an identity, not an external source).

#### Migration

`0016_exchange_observations`, revises `0015_exchange_result_release`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s
`EXPECTED_HEAD` updated to match.

**Legacy migration behavior, verified against real PostgreSQL with real pre-existing legacy data
(not merely an empty-table CI run):** seeded two legacy-shaped orders directly via raw SQL at the
pre-0016 schema (order A: `IN_PROGRESS` with one legacy scalar `LabResult` row; order B: a
`COMPLETED`-without-release order, exercising ADR-044's grandfather rule) before running `alembic
upgrade head`. Verified after upgrade: each legacy row became one container (`entry_completed_at`/
`created_at` backfilled from the old `completed_at`, `entry_completed_by_identity_id` left `NULL` —
never fabricated) plus exactly one child observation (`source_code`/`display_label_snapshot` reused
from the item's own `catalog_code_snapshot`/`catalog_display_name_snapshot`, `source_system =
"dhealth-exchange"`, every value field copied verbatim). Order B's `COMPLETED` status and zero-row
`exchange_lab_result_releases` count were unaffected by the migration — the grandfather rule holds
through this schema change.

**Downgrade guards, each independently demonstrated against real PostgreSQL, not just written:**
four fail-fast guards (`DowngradeBlockedByMultiObservationHistory`,
`DowngradeBlockedByIncompleteEntryHistory`, `DowngradeBlockedByNativeCompletionProvenanceHistory`,
`DowngradeBlockedByObservationAuditVocabularyHistory`), each triggered one at a time by mutating
real rows in the qualification database (a second observation added; `entry_completed_at` nulled;
a real `entry_completed_by_identity_id` set; a real `lab_observation_recorded` audit row inserted),
confirming each guard fires with the exact expected exception, the database left completely
unchanged at `0016_exchange_observations` after each refusal (`alembic current` re-checked after
each). With no guards triggered, a real downgrade to `0015_exchange_result_release` was run and the
reconstructed `exchange_lab_results` row matched the original pre-upgrade scalar values bit-for-bit
(verified by direct comparison, not assumed).

**Guard-removal data-loss demonstration (required negative control 10):** on a separate, disposable
database seeded with exactly one native-completed two-observation container, all four guards were
temporarily disabled (`if False and ...`) and the downgrade forced through. Result: the second
observation (a distinct real value) was **silently and permanently discarded** — the reconstructed
old-schema row contained only the first observation's value, no error, no warning. This is concrete,
observed evidence for why the guards exist, not a hypothetical. Guards restored immediately after
(confirmed via `grep -rn "NEGATIVE CONTROL" adapter/src adapter/migrations` returning nothing); the
disposable database dropped.

#### Result-entry workflow

Three distinct actions where DH-EX-007 had one:

1. **`POST .../items/{item_id}/observations`** (new) — `record_observation`: appends one
   `LabObservation` under the item's container (created lazily on first call), any number of times,
   while the container's entry is not yet completed. `LabObservationRecordRequest` requires
   caller-supplied `source_code`/`display_label` (ADR-047's hybrid-namespace identity — no LOINC
   dependency, no analyte ontology, no hard-coded panel content); `source_system` is not
   caller-accepted, always server-assigned. `LAB_TECH` only, same lab-assignment/`IN_PROGRESS`
   guards as before.
2. **`POST .../items/{item_id}/complete-result-entry`** (new) — `complete_entry`: the **only** place
   `entry_completed_at` is ever set. Requires >=1 existing observation
   (`EntryNotReadyForCompletion` otherwise); idempotent on replay (`created=False`, original
   actor/time never overwritten); freezes the container (`EntryAlreadyCompleted` refuses any further
   observation). `LAB_TECH` only, deliberately **not** `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` — entry and release stay
   separate authorities at the item level, mirroring ADR-044's order-level split.
3. **`POST .../items/{item_id}/result`** (existing route, reshaped internals) — the
   backward-compatible single-observation convenience path: atomically creates the container,
   records exactly one observation (source identity reused from the item's own catalog snapshot),
   and completes the entry, in one call, one transaction. Refuses (`DuplicateResult`) if the item
   already has a container of any kind — never a way to add a second observation or re-complete.
   Does not auto-release; unaffected by ADR-044.

**Completeness, never inferred by counting:** the single shared choke point
`_count_missing_or_malformed_results` (renamed from DH-EX-012B's `_count_missing_results`) now asks
"does this item have a container whose `entry_completed_at` is set, backed by a real EXISTS check
for >=1 observation row" — the EXISTS clause is deliberate defense-in-depth, re-derived from the
database on every call by both `ready_for_release` and `LabResultReleaseRepository.release`'s own
re-check, never trusted from the container's own flag alone.

#### Freeze / concurrency discipline

Every result-entry mutation (`record_observation`, `complete_entry`, `record_numeric`/
`record_text`) shares one preamble, `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry`, which locks `LabOrder FOR
UPDATE` first — identical lock order to every prior DH-EX-005/006/007/012 mutation. This single lock
is what serializes observation-vs-observation, observation-vs-completion, and completion-vs-release
races; no additional row-level lock exists or is needed.

**Real-PostgreSQL concurrency qualification** (new file, `tests/integration/
test_dhex012c_postgres_qualification.py`, `DHEX012C_PG_*` env-gated, never in CI), run 5+ times
each for stability, zero flakes observed:

- 10 concurrent `record_observation` calls on one item: all 10 persist, no lost write, container
  never auto-completes.
- Observation racing `complete_entry`: exactly one ordering occurs per run (the shared lock
  guarantees this); whichever wins is internally coherent — a losing observation is refused
  (`EntryAlreadyCompleted`) and never persists; a winning observation exists before completion locks.
- `complete_entry` racing `LabResultReleaseRepository.release` on a two-item order (item 1 already
  complete, item 2's completion races release): release never succeeds while item 2 is incomplete;
  whichever call the lock admits first is the one that determines the final state, no split-brain
  (`COMPLETED` order with an incomplete item never observed).
- 10 concurrent `complete_entry` calls on the same item: exactly one creates the completion fact;
  every other call observes that identical fact back, never overwrites it, never creates a second
  one.

**Existing DH-EX-007/DH-EX-012 real-Postgres qualification files updated for the new signature/
shape** (`test_dhex007_postgres_qualification.py`, `test_dhex012_postgres_qualification.py`) — both
needed `recorded_by_identity_id` added to every `record_numeric` call and their scalar-field
assertions reshaped to read through `LabObservation`. **Two pre-existing, DH-EX-012C-unrelated bugs
found and fixed while doing this, disclosed rather than silently folded in:**
1. `test_dhex007_postgres_qualification.py`'s `_seed_in_progress_order` never called
   `workflow.record_collection` before `start_processing` — a DH-EX-011 requirement this fixture
   predates. It was never caught because this file is skipped by default in CI; DH-EX-012C's own
   real qualification run is what surfaced it. Fixed with one line, matching every other seed
   helper's existing pattern.
2. My own first version of `test_dhex012_postgres_qualification.py`'s fix created the new
   `recorded_by_identity_id`'s identity *inside* the raced closure in
   `_run_final_result_vs_release_once`, which biased the race 10/10 toward `release_first` (the
   extra DB round-trip inside the timing-sensitive window). Moved the identity creation outside the
   race, matching the existing `releaser` variable's own placement — confirmed both orderings occur
   again after the fix.

All three integration files pass together in one invocation (19 passed, 51 skipped — the 51 being
every other track's own opt-in file skipped for lack of its own env vars).

#### API shape

`LabResultSubmitResponse` gains `observation_id`/`entry_completed_at` (additive; `result_id`/
`completed_at` keep their old meaning). New `LabObservationResponse`, `EntryCompletionResponse`.
`ProviderResultItemResponse`/`LabResultInspectionItemResponse` reshaped from flat scalar fields to
`entry_completed_at`/`observations: list[...]` — a deliberate breaking change, per ADR-047's own
instruction not to preserve a flat shape once it makes panel results wrong.
`LabResultInspectionResponse.all_results_entered` renamed `all_items_entry_complete` (the underlying
fact materially changed; kept under its old name would have silently repointed an existing field's
meaning). Patient-facing `PatientOrderResponse` is unaffected and unchanged — still excludes every
result field by construction (`extra="forbid"`, no result field defined); the existing
`test_patient_order_response_never_leaks_a_real_lab_result_even_after_selection` regression test
(updated only for the new `recorded_by_identity_id` parameter, not its actual assertions) still
passes. `DoctorReview`/`ResultDelivery` untouched, confirmed by dedicated tests still passing
unchanged.

**Measured, not estimated, N+1 check:** built a 5-item, 15-observation (3 each) released order in a
throwaway in-memory SQLite engine with `before_cursor_execute` query counting.
`LabResultRepository.list_for_order` (provider read): **2 queries**, constant regardless of item/
observation count (`selectinload` batches every container's observations in one second query).
`LabResultRepository.get_for_lab` (lab inspection read): **5 queries**, also constant (order,
selection, outer-joined item+container rows, one batched observation query, release lookup) — no
per-item or per-observation query anywhere in either path.

#### Audit

Two new event types: `lab_observation_recorded` (fires once per recorded observation, including
inside the compat path), `lab_result_entry_completed` (fires once per genuine completion, never on
an idempotent replay). `lab_result_recorded` is retired — kept in the `event_type` CHECK constraint's
allowed list only because real historical rows already carry it (narrowing would require proving
none exist, an unnecessary destructive-adjacent step for an otherwise purely additive migration); no
code path writes a new one. All writes atomic with their mutation, in the identical
`session_factory.begin()` transaction — confirmed by a dedicated new atomicity test for the granular
`complete-result-entry` endpoint (`test_granular_completion_audit_atomicity`, mirroring the existing
compat-path atomicity test) in addition to the existing compat-path and release-path atomicity
tests, all still passing and all independently exercised as negative controls below.

#### Required negative controls — all 10 executed for real, every mutation restored after observing failure

1. **Restored old "row exists = complete" logic** (`_count_missing_or_malformed_results` reduced to
   `LabResult.id.is_(None)` only) → `test_multi_observation_golden_flow_release_and_provider_read`
   went red (premature release returned 201 instead of the expected 409-refused). Reverted.
2. **Permitted completion with zero observations** (removed the observation-count guard in
   `complete_entry`, lazily creating a container if absent) →
   `test_completion_rejected_with_zero_observations` (repository) and
   `..._via_api` (HTTP) both went red (201 instead of 409). Reverted.
3. **Removed the completeness check from release entirely** →
   `test_release_refused_when_a_result_is_still_missing` (repository) and
   `test_release_refused_when_results_incomplete` (HTTP) both went red (201 instead of 409).
   Reverted.
4. **Permitted observation after entry completion** (removed the `EntryAlreadyCompleted` freeze
   check) → `test_observation_after_completion_is_frozen_and_refused` (repository) and
   `test_observation_after_completion_refused_via_api` (HTTP) both went red (201 instead of 409).
   Reverted.
5. **Removed the lab-ownership check** from the shared `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry` preamble →

6. **Removed `LAB_TECH` authorization** from the observation-entry route →

7. **Removed the release-role check** from the release route →
   `test_lab_tech_alone_cannot_release_results` went red (201 instead of 403). Reverted.
8. **Split the completion write and its audit row into two separate transactions** in

9. **Removed the `FOR UPDATE` lock** from `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry` → run against real

10. **Disabled all four migration downgrade guards** (`if False and ...`) on a disposable database

Required matrix items from the ticket are covered by: the 20 new tests added this ticket (5

## DH-CLINIC-002 — Native provider-scoped patient find and creation

**Date:** 2026-09-15
**Starting HEAD / `origin/master`:** `6795d86a27439218f402f6920db09201edd61ff4`
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED; implementation commit pushed; exact-SHA CI green
**Migration head:** `0019_exchange_amendments` (unchanged; no migration added)

### Native patient lookup contract

- `GET /exchange/v1/organizations/{provider_id}/patient-references?limit=50` lists at most 100
  references for that exact provider, ordered deterministically by `created_at DESC, id ASC`.
- `POST /exchange/v1/organizations/{provider_id}/patient-references/search` accepts JSON
  `{ "query": <1..100 characters>, "limit": <1..100, default 50> }`. Search is a literal,
  case-insensitive substring retrieval over only `display_name`, `contact_value`, and
  `source_identity_value`; `%`, `_`, and `\\` are escaped as literal characters. The search text is
  deliberately in a request body rather than a GET query string so native patient names/contact
  fragments do not enter Uvicorn access-log URLs.
- `GET /exchange/v1/organizations/{provider_id}/patient-references/{patient_reference_id}` supplies
  the authoritative provider-scoped snapshot used after create/replay. Missing and wrong-provider
  ids both return the existing non-enumerating 404.
- List/search/detail use a separate response shape only:
  `patient_reference_id`, nullable `display_name`, nullable `contact_channel_type`, nullable
  `contact_value`, and `local_reference`. Internal `source_system` /
  `source_identity_system` and `created_at` are not exposed. The older
  `PatientReferenceResponse` contract remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

Every route calls the existing no-platform-admin-bypass clinician authorization boundary. An
authenticated identity with no relationship to the provider gets 404; a related membership without
`CLINICIAN` gets 403; unauthenticated requests get 401. Repository lookup always starts with
`source_organization_id == provider_id`; it issues one bounded single-table SELECT and introduces no
related-row reads or N+1 pattern. The existing provider-organization index is the applicable first
predicate, so no speculative index was added.

### Native creation and ambiguous-write behavior

DHealth Clinic calls the existing `POST .../patient-references` bind; it never calls `/openmrs/*`.
The native source tuple is precisely:

- `source_system = "dhealth-clinic"`
- `source_identity_system = "urn:dhealth:clinic:patient-reference-id"`
- `source_identity_value = <browser-generated UUIDv4>`

The UUID is opaque, stable for the unresolved attempt, unrelated to name/contact, and remains inside
the existing provider-scoped unique tuple. The UI retains the full pending request only in in-memory
Clinic application state keyed by authenticated `identity_id + provider_id`; it is not written to
browser storage. A lost/ambiguous response, detail-read failure, tab navigation, or provider switch
therefore cannot make the pending tuple cross into another provider or mint a new tuple on retry.
Both HTTP 201 create and HTTP 200 exact replay are followed by provider-scoped detail retrieval, so
the workspace opens the authoritative stored snapshot rather than assuming replay updated optional
fields. Provider A and Provider B may hold the same UUID value and still receive different
`PatientReference` ids, exactly as the database uniqueness contract requires.

The French-first UI now implements `Patients` → `Rechercher un patient` → `Ouvrir`, truthful
`Aucun patient trouvé` + `Nouveau patient`, a minimal optional display-name/contact form, and a
small native workspace. A null name falls back to the honest `local_reference`; the workspace shows
