### DH-EX-013 · Immutable pre-release observation correction (ADR-045 Questions 1–3) · P0 · ✅ IMPLEMENTED — SQLITE + REAL-POSTGRESQL QUALIFIED, NEGATIVE-CONTROL VERIFIED

**Ticket:** DH-EX-013. Implements ADR-045's Questions 1–3 exactly as accepted (see DECISIONS.md's
ADR-045 addendum): a supported, non-destructive workflow for correcting an entered
`LabObservation` **before** order release. Post-release amendment (Questions 4–5) is explicitly out
of scope — deferred to DH-EX-014 — and remains forbidden here, unchanged from ADR-045's own already-
established "no in-place mutation of an already-released result" conclusion.

**Starting HEAD/CI:** `c3c8646927fe5866730417eb6a2c6c5fbd447400` (DH-EX-012C), fetched and audited
fresh, working tree clean before this ticket began. All 9 CI check runs on that SHA independently
re-verified `success` via GitHub's check-runs API, not trusted from the ticket prompt.

**Environment note (unchanged from every prior ticket this session):** Windows Git Bash has no
working Python interpreter (`daher_adapter.audit` imports `fcntl` unconditionally) and no Docker.
All adapter test/lint/migration/qualification work ran inside WSL2 Ubuntu against its native
PostgreSQL 18 install and the adapter's existing `.venv`.

#### Schema implemented

Three new columns on `LabObservation`, no new table:

```text
LabObservation
  ├─ recorded_by_identity_id      FK → exchange_identities, nullable (legacy rows stay NULL,
  │                                 never fabricated; every new observation from this ticket
  │                                 forward — ordinary entry AND correction — sets it)
  ├─ supersedes_observation_id    FK → exchange_lab_observations.id, nullable, self-referential,
  │                                 UNIQUE (at most one successor per predecessor)
  └─ superseded_at                nullable DateTime — NULL means effective; non-NULL means this
                                    row has been corrected and superseded
```

**Effective rule, stated once and enforced everywhere:** `superseded_at IS NULL`. An explicit
relational fact, never inferred from `recorded_at` ordering. A `CHECK` constraint
(`ck_exchange_lab_observations_no_self_supersede`) forbids an observation from superseding itself.

#### Migration

`0017_observation_revisions`, revises `0016_exchange_observations`. **Naming note:** the originally
planned revision id `0017_exchange_observation_revisions` (35 characters) exceeded Alembic's own
`alembic_version.version_num` `VARCHAR(32)` column — this was not caught by inspection, it was
caught by actually running the migration against real PostgreSQL and observing a genuine
`psycopg.errors.StringDataRightTruncation`/`DataError`. Renamed to `0017_observation_revisions` (26
characters) everywhere (migration file, `models.py` docstring reference, `.github/workflows/
ci.yml`'s `EXPECTED_HEAD`). No legacy data migration loop is needed — the three new columns simply
default `NULL`, which truthfully represents every pre-existing observation.

**Downgrade guards, each independently demonstrated against real PostgreSQL:**
`DowngradeBlockedByCorrectionHistory`, `DowngradeBlockedByObservationActorProvenanceHistory`,
`DowngradeBlockedByObservationCorrectionAuditVocabularyHistory` — each triggered one at a time by
seeding the exact real condition it guards (a correction chain; a real `recorded_by_identity_id`;
a real `lab_observation_corrected` audit row), confirmed to fire with the exact expected exception
and leave the database unchanged at `0017_observation_revisions` after each refusal.

**Guard-removal data-loss demonstration (required negative control 10), on disposable database
`dhex013_control10`:** with all three guards disabled and a real two-version correction chain
present (original value 5.1, corrected value 5.9), the forced downgrade did **not** delete either
row — a more subtle failure than DH-EX-012C's equivalent demonstration. Both the original and
corrected values survived as two independent, structurally identical rows in the flat 0016 schema,
with the supersession relationship silently discarded and no remaining way to tell which value was
ever authoritative. Documented precisely as this distinct, arguably worse failure mode (looks fine,
silently wrong) rather than described as simple deletion. Guards restored immediately after; the
disposable database dropped.

#### Correction workflow

- **`POST .../items/{item_id}/observations/{observation_id}/correct`** (new) —
  `correct_observation`: locks the parent `LabOrder` `FOR UPDATE` (the same shared preamble already
  used by `record_observation`/`complete_entry`/the compat path), verifies the observation belongs
  to the addressed item/order/lab, refuses (409, `StaleObservationVersion`) if the target is already
  superseded, then in one nested transaction inserts a new effective observation
  (`supersedes_observation_id` = predecessor) and marks the predecessor `superseded_at`. `LAB_TECH`
  only (ADR-045 Question 2 — matches entry authority, `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` not required). No reason
  field accepted or stored (ADR-045 Question 3). Deliberately does **not** check
  `LabResult.entry_completed_at` — correction is permitted whether or not entry is already complete,
  and never clears that field.
- **Refuses after release, by construction, not by a bolted-on extra check:** the same
  `LabOrder`-locked `IN_PROGRESS` gate in `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry` that already refuses a new
  `record_observation` call after `COMPLETED` refuses `correct_observation` identically — one shared
  mechanism, not two independent ones that could drift apart.
- **`GET .../items/{item_id}/observations/history`** (new) — `get_correction_history`: returns every
  observation that has ever existed under the item's container, superseded and effective alike,
  ordered oldest to newest. The one place a lab-authorized caller may see historical
  (non-effective) values at all. `LAB_TECH` or `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`; never exposed to any
  provider-facing or patient-facing route.
- **Zero-effective-observation safety:** argued from the transaction shape, not covered by a
  dedicated test — a correction always inserts exactly one new effective row in the same transaction
  it marks exactly one predecessor superseded, so net effective count is unchanged by construction.
  No test asserts this directly; it follows from `correct_observation`'s code shape, not from
  independent verification.
- **Chain integrity enforced at the database, not only in application code:** a full `UNIQUE`
  constraint on `supersedes_observation_id` is the concurrency backstop behind the `LabOrder FOR
  UPDATE` lock — confirmed necessary, not redundant, by negative control 4 (see below). No partial
  index was needed: PostgreSQL treats every `NULL` as distinct under `UNIQUE`, so the never-corrected
  majority of observations (`supersedes_observation_id IS NULL`) are left unconstrained by it.

#### Read-path changes

- `get_for_item`, `list_for_order`, `get_for_lab` (lab inspection) all now filter observations to
  `superseded_at.is_(None)` — effective-only. Release and provider visibility are unaffected in
  every other respect: release still sees exactly the effective set at the moment of release,
  post-release provider re-queries still return only what was effective at release time (DH-EX-012A's
  original re-query-safety concern is unaffected because release never freezes a snapshot — it
  simply reads live effective rows, which is exactly what "no superseded row is ever effective"
  guarantees stays correct after release too, since nothing can be corrected post-release).
- `_count_missing_or_malformed_results`'s completeness check now requires an *effective* observation
  to exist — a container whose only observation was corrected away still correctly counts as having
  content, via its new effective successor.
- Lab inspection (`get_for_lab`) gained `has_correction_history: bool` per item — `True` iff any
  observation under that container has ever been superseded — computed via one batched query, not
  N+1.
- `LabObservationResponse` now includes `recorded_by_identity_id`, `supersedes_observation_id`,
  `superseded_at` on every observation returned anywhere.

#### Audit

New `lab_observation_corrected` security-audit event type, added to
`ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent`'s `event_type` CHECK constraint and `SecurityEventType` Literal.
Recorded in the **same transaction** as the correction/supersession write — verified atomic by
negative control 9 (see below), not merely asserted.

#### Required negative controls — the ticket's own 10, executed against real code in that order, every mutation reverted and re-verified green afterward

1. **Replace revision creation with destructive UPDATE → immutable-history tests must fail.**
   Replaced `correct_observation`'s insert-new-row-plus-mark-predecessor-superseded logic with an
   in-place `UPDATE` of the existing observation's value column, no new row, no `superseded_at`.
   Confirmed red: all three immutable-history tests failed (the destructive path also left the method
   returning `None` where a `LabObservationRecord` was expected — a second, independent symptom of
   how wrong this path is). Reverted, re-passed.
2. **Permit correction after release → post-release refusal test must fail.** Removed the
   `IN_PROGRESS` status check from the shared `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry` preamble. Confirmed
   red: `test_correction_after_release_refused` failed — a correction succeeded (`201`) against an
   already-`COMPLETED`/released order instead of being refused. Reverted, re-passed.
3. **Remove effective-observation check → stale-observation correction test must fail.**
   **Genuine defense-in-depth finding, not a fabricated failure:** removing the application-level
   `if predecessor.superseded_at is not None: raise StaleObservationVersion` check did **not** turn
   the stale-correction tests red, because the database-level `UNIQUE` constraint on
   `supersedes_observation_id` independently catches the identical case via `IntegrityError` →
   `StaleObservationVersion` translation, in both SQLite and PostgreSQL. Reported exactly as
   observed, not forced red artificially — a second, independent layer already covers this case
   on its own. Reverted.
4. **Remove sibling-revision uniqueness/concurrency defense → concurrent correction test must
   expose dual effective revisions.** Removing the DB `UNIQUE` constraint **alone** was insufficient
   — the `LabOrder FOR UPDATE` lock still fully serialized every correction attempt, so no exposure
   occurred. Only after removing **both** the lock and the constraint together did real corruption
   appear: 5/5 runs against real PostgreSQL, 10 concurrent correction attempts on the same
   observation all succeeded, producing 10 sibling revisions superseding one predecessor — exactly
   the dual-effective-revisions failure this control requires. Both defenses restored; the corrupted
   qualification database (`dhex013_qual`) could not have the constraint re-added over corrupted
   data and was recreated from scratch.
5. **Include superseded observations in provider read → effective-only test must fail.** Removed
   the effective-only filter from the provider-facing read path. Confirmed red: the golden-flow
   test's post-release provider-observation-count assertion failed (both the superseded and
   effective observation were returned). Reverted, re-passed.
6. **Include superseded observations in lab current inspection → test must fail.** Removed the
   effective-only filter from the lab-inspection read path (`get_for_lab`). Confirmed red:
   `test_correction_golden_flow_history_and_release`'s `len(item_line["observations"]) == 1`
   assertion failed (`2 == 1`, both the original and corrected value visible). Reverted, re-passed.
7. **Remove LAB_TECH authorization → auth test must fail.** Removed the `_require_lab_tech` call
   from the correction route. Confirmed red: both `test_clinician_cannot_correct_or_view_history`
   and `test_releaser_alone_cannot_correct` failed (a `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`-only token successfully
   corrected an observation, `201` instead of the expected `403`). Reverted, re-passed.
8. **Remove lab ownership check → cross-lab test must fail.** Removed the
   `selection.lab_organization_id != lab_organization_id` check from `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry`'s
   shared preamble. Confirmed red: both `test_wrong_lab_cannot_correct_or_view_history_and_is_non_enumerating`
   (HTTP layer) and `test_cross_lab_correction_refused` (repository layer) failed — a lab could
   correct an observation belonging to a different lab's order entirely. Reverted, re-passed.
9. **Split correction/audit transaction → atomicity test must detect inconsistent correction.**
   Moved the audit-event write into its own separate `session_factory.begin()` block, after the
   correction's own transaction had already committed. Confirmed red: `test_correction_audit_atomicity`
   failed — when the audit write was made to fail (monkeypatched), the correction had already
   committed on its own (`original_row.superseded_at` was a real timestamp, not `None` as the test
   requires). Reverted, re-passed — confirming the single shared `session_factory.begin()` block is
   load-bearing, not cosmetic.
10. **Remove downgrade guard → real PostgreSQL control must demonstrate correction history loss.**
    Satisfied by the migration guard-removal demonstration above (`dhex013_control10`): with all
    three downgrade guards disabled and a real two-version correction chain present, the forced
    downgrade did not delete either row, but did silently discard the supersession relationship
    between them — both the original and corrected values survived as two indistinguishable rows,
    with no remaining way to tell which one had ever been authoritative. This is real, observed
    correction-history loss, not merely asserted to be prevented.

`grep -rn "NEGATIVE CONTROL" adapter/src adapter/tests adapter/migrations` returns nothing —
every control fully reverted before proceeding.

#### Test matrix coverage

~13 new repository-level tests (`test_exchange_results.py`) and ~10 new HTTP-level tests
(`test_exchange_results_api.py`) cover: numeric correction, text correction, unit/reference-range
change without mutating the original, a three-version correction chain, stale-superseded-correction
refused, correction permitted after entry completion but before release, correction refused after
release, cross-lab correction refused (both layers), correction on an observation from a different
item refused, the full golden flow (correct → history shows both versions → lab inspection shows
effective-only with `has_correction_history` → release ships only the effective value → provider
sees only the effective value), auth matrix (clinician and lone releaser both refused), non-
enumerating cross-lab 404s for both correction and history, correction/audit atomicity, and patient-
bearer tokens never seeing correction or history endpoints. Plus 4 new real-PostgreSQL concurrency
tests: concurrent corrections of the same observation (exactly one winner), correction-vs-release
race (release never ships a stale value), concurrent corrections on independent observations (both
succeed independently), correction-vs-ordinary-add (the post-release freeze applies identically to
both actions).

#### Validation

`ruff check`/`ruff format --check` on `src tests migrations scripts`: clean. Full SQLite suite:

### DH-EX-014D · Post-release amendment + clinician re-review architecture decision audit · P0 · 📋 DECISION PACKET DELIVERED — NO CODE CHANGED

**Ticket:** DH-EX-014D. Audit/decision packet only, per its own explicit instruction — no runtime
implementation, no migration, no API, no model, no test change. Resolves ADR-045's Questions 4–5 and
its own named amendment-model sub-questions into a linked, RECOMMENDED-not-ACCEPTED architecture
(`DECISIONS.md`'s new **ADR-048**), without implementing any of it.

**Starting HEAD/CI:** `8328d2e400217837aae6cca8cf17fde7e54dea47` (DH-EX-013's own doc-follow-up
commit), fetched via `git fetch origin master` and audited fresh — parent confirmed `05ebe22...`
(DH-EX-013's implementation commit), working tree clean before this ticket began. CI run
`34777867014` independently re-verified via GitHub's check-runs API (not trusted from the ticket
prompt): 9/9 jobs `success`. Both values matched the ticket's own stated expectation exactly.

**Migration head confirmed:** `0017_observation_revisions`, `down_revision` chain traced to
`0016_exchange_observations` with no forks — matches the ticket's stated expectation.

#### Current-state evidence, re-audited directly from code, not from a prior ticket's summary

- `LabResultRelease` (`models.py:670-706`): one immutable row per order, no revision/un-release/
  delete method anywhere in `LabResultReleaseRepository`. Stores no reference to which
  `LabObservation` rows were effective at release time — an authorization fact, not a value
  snapshot.
- `get_lab_order_results` (`api.py:3018-3071`): gated only on `order.status == COMPLETED`; queries
  `results.list_for_order` live on every call, which itself filters to `superseded_at IS NULL`.
  **No binding exists between a specific release and the specific observations it authorized.**
- `correct_observation`/`_lock_order_and_item_for_entry` (`results.py:589-745`, `1326-1360`,
  DH-EX-013, unchanged): the same `LabOrder FOR UPDATE` + `IN_PROGRESS` gate that serializes
  concurrent corrections is exactly what makes correction refuse once `COMPLETED`.
  **`uq_exchange_lab_observations_supersedes_observation_id` is a full, unconditional `UNIQUE`
  constraint — at most one successor may ever supersede a given observation, permanently.** This is
  the single most consequential existing constraint for any amendment design; full analysis in
  ADR-048 §3.
- `orders.py:57-66`: `_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[COMPLETED] == frozenset()` — confirmed genuinely
  terminal, re-verified directly, not assumed from a prior audit.
- `DoctorReview` (`models.py:737-761`): `lab_order_id` is `unique=True` **at the database level** —
  Question 4's Option C is therefore a real migration, not an application-code-only change. No
  review-reset/revision/history mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase.
- `ResultDelivery` (`models.py:709-734`): one row per order; confirmed by grep that no code path
  anywhere calls `mark_delivered`/`mark_failed` as a side effect of anything.
- `PatientOrderResponse` (`api.py:657-667`): `extra="forbid"`, no result field of any kind —
  confirmed unaffected by anything in this audit.
- `_require_lab_tech`/`_require_lab_result_releaser`/`_require_lab_tech_or_releaser`
  (`api.py:1238-1287`): three independent, already-shipped authorization primitives. A future
  "`LAB_TECH` prepares, `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` releases" amendment flow requires **zero new
  authorization primitives**.
- `security_audit.py:24-99`: `event_type` is a DB-enforced `CHECK`, widened per migration with a
  downgrade guard keyed to existing rows (exactly DH-EX-013's own `0017_observation_revisions`
  pattern for `lab_observation_corrected`). `resource_type` needs no widening — `"lab_order"` is
  already the established convention reused by every per-item-but-order-scoped event; this asymmetry
  makes a future audit-vocabulary migration smaller than it might first appear.

#### Risk statement (required acceptance criterion 2/7)

A concrete, verified sequence, not a hypothetical: release with observation V2 effective (5.1) →
provider reads 5.1 → clinician calls `mark_no_follow_up_required`, `DoctorReview` becomes terminal
→ if DH-EX-013's `IN_PROGRESS` gate were simply removed, a later correction to 5.9 would insert V3
superseding V2 → the same, unchanged `LabResultRelease` row still says "released," the same,
unchanged `DoctorReview` row still says `NO_FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED`, and the very next
`GET .../results` call — unmodified — silently returns 5.9 instead of 5.1, with nothing anywhere
distinguishing "originally released and reviewed" from "changed since, unreviewed." This is the
literal, verified behavior of today's code under that one naive change, not a worst-case guess — see
ADR-048 §2 for the full statement.

#### Architecture alternatives evaluated (required acceptance criterion 8/25: at least three)

**Model 1 — release manifest**: an immutable release-version row plus immutable membership rows
naming exactly `(item, observation_id)` per release. **Model 2 — result-set/version entity**: a new
first-class aggregate underneath the order that observations/releases/reviews all bind through —
evaluated as disproportionately heavy for what current evidence demonstrates is needed. **Model 3 —
amendment episode + release manifest**: a workflow row (`PREPARING`→`RELEASED`) whose release step
produces exactly Model 1's manifest, while `LabResultRelease` itself is never mutated, replaced, or
reinterpreted — remains permanently "release #1." A fourth option (a self-referential supersession
chain on `LabResultRelease` itself, mirroring `LabObservation`'s own pattern) was considered and
rejected: `LabResultRelease` is explicitly documented and tested today as immutable with no revision
mechanism of any kind, and retrofitting one would risk every existing release read path far more than
a new, purely additive table does.

**Recommended (not accepted): Model 3** — full reasoning, and answers to every one of the ticket's
lettered sub-questions (A–P) and the required data-model comparison (entities, keys, cardinalities,
immutability, reconstruction of release #1 vs #2, review #1 vs #2 binding, migration impact, legacy
compatibility, concurrency impact, API complexity), live in `DECISIONS.md`'s new **ADR-048**, not
duplicated here in full.

#### The one finding this audit adds beyond what DH-EX-012A/ADR-045 already established

DH-EX-012A's own packet evaluated the amendment-model sub-questions in the abstract; this audit adds
one concrete, verified, load-bearing constraint neither DH-EX-012A nor ADR-045/046/047 could have
named, since it did not exist until DH-EX-013 shipped it: the full `UNIQUE` constraint on
`supersedes_observation_id` means an amendment design that lets a `LAB_TECH` "prepare" a correction
(inserting a real successor row) and later **discard** it without releasing permanently blocks any
future correction of that same predecessor, since rows are never deleted. Two structurally different
resolutions exist (immediate-permanent insert, mirroring DH-EX-013's own no-undo philosophy exactly;
or a staged/discardable draft, requiring a future relaxation of the existing constraint to a partial
index) — recorded as Human Decision 3 in ADR-048 §19, not silently resolved by this audit, since it
carries real operational-workflow consequences AGENTS.md's "obviously should" guard applies to
directly.

### DH-EX-014A · Immutable release-version manifest + versioned DoctorReview foundation · P0 · ✅ IMPLEMENTED — SQLITE + REAL-POSTGRESQL + CI QUALIFIED, NEGATIVE-CONTROL VERIFIED

**Ticket:** DH-EX-014A. Implements ADR-048's Model 3 architecture (accepted by Liban this ticket,
appended to ADR-048) as an **immutable versioning foundation only** — a release-version manifest and
a version-aware `DoctorReview`. It does **not** implement post-release amendment preparation or
release; no amendment endpoint, no observation mutation past `COMPLETED`, and no `version_number > 1`
row is creatable by anything in this ticket. DH-EX-014B (amendment preparation/release) remains
required, and remains a real-patient-pilot blocker per Liban's own Decision 3.

**Starting HEAD/CI:** `932455bbb812289268c032b0f9f8491ba6e8e9ce` (DH-EX-014D's own audit commit),
fetched and audited fresh — working tree clean before this ticket began. CI run `34778951953`
independently re-verified via GitHub's check-runs API: 9/9 jobs `success`. Both matched the
ticket's own stated expectation exactly.

#### The load-bearing invariant, proven from code before relying on it

Every `LabObservation`-mutating code path in the package — `record_observation`,
`correct_observation`, and the single-observation convenience path (`_submit_in_session`) — is
gated, without exception, on `_lock_order_and_item_for_entry`'s `LabOrder`-locked `IN_PROGRESS`
check (confirmed by grepping every `LabObservation(` construction site and the sole
`.superseded_at =` assignment in the package: exactly three construction sites, one mutation site,
all three behind the identical gate). Once `LabResultReleaseRepository.release` moves an order to
`COMPLETED`, no code path anywhere can create, mutate, or supersede an observation belonging to it.
**Therefore the currently-effective observation set for an already-released order is, today,
exactly and provably the set that was effective at the moment of release** — proven, not assumed,
and this is exactly why the migration's backfill (below) is reconstruction, never fabrication.

#### Schema

```text
LabResultRelease (unchanged, immutable, exactly as ADR-044 shipped it)
      ↓ (Version 1 only, lab_result_release_id UNIQUE)
LabResultReleaseVersion (id, lab_order_id, version_number, lab_result_release_id, created_at)
      ↓
LabResultReleaseManifestEntry (release_version_id, lab_order_item_id, lab_observation_id)

DoctorReview (lab_order_id no longer UNIQUE; new nullable release_version_id)
```

`exchange_release_versions`: `UNIQUE(lab_order_id, version_number)`; a `CHECK` enforces version 1
is always release-bound (`lab_result_release_id IS NOT NULL`) and every later version is not (since
DH-EX-014B's amendment episodes will bind differently — that table is deliberately not created
here). `exchange_release_manifest_entries`: `UNIQUE(release_version_id, lab_observation_id)` — a
single item may carry more than one manifest entry (a panel), matching ADR-047's own "do not impose
one observation per item" rule; binds by immutable `LabObservation.id` only, no clinical scalar
value ever duplicated. `exchange_doctor_reviews`: `uq_exchange_doctor_reviews_lab_order_id` dropped;
new `release_version_id` column with a plain `UNIQUE` (sufficient alone for "one review per non-NULL
version," since every SQL dialect this codebase targets treats `NULL` as distinct under `UNIQUE` —
the identical insight `0017`'s `supersedes_observation_id` constraint already relies on) plus a
genuine partial unique index on `lab_order_id` scoped to `release_version_id IS NULL` (the one
legacy/unbound row per order).

#### Migration

`0018_exchange_release_versions`, revises `0017_observation_revisions`. **Table/constraint naming
note:** the originally planned table names (`exchange_lab_result_release_versions`,
`exchange_lab_result_release_manifest_entries`) produced constraint identifiers exceeding
PostgreSQL's 63-character limit (`uq_exchange_lab_result_release_manifest_entries_version_
observation` at 67 characters) — caught by actually running the migration against real PostgreSQL,
not by inspection. Renamed to `exchange_release_versions`/`exchange_release_manifest_entries`
throughout (model, migration, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `EXPECTED_HEAD`), bringing every
constraint name comfortably under the limit.

**Original-release backfill**, seeded via the real repository layer at the pre-0018 schema in a
temporary git worktree at the parent commit (the current ORM models already reflect the new schema,
so seeding "pre-migration" data requires the pre-migration application code, not merely a pre-
migration database) — four scenarios, verified against real PostgreSQL: (1) an explicit release
with one DH-EX-013 pre-release correction — verified the manifest names the *corrected* observation
id, never the superseded original; (2) an explicit release with a two-observation panel item —
verified both manifest entries present; (3) a grandfathered `COMPLETED`-without-`LabResultRelease`
order (raw SQL status write, matching DH-EX-012C's own precedent for simulating this otherwise-
unreachable legacy shape) — verified zero version/manifest rows created; (4) an unreleased
`IN_PROGRESS` order with its default `PENDING` review — verified untouched. `DoctorReview` status/
`reviewed_at`/`reviewed_by_practitioner_reference_id` preserved verbatim for the terminal-review
scenario, never reset or fabricated.

**Second, independent backfill validation** (beyond the four seeded scenarios above, added after
advisor review): the still-existing `dhex012c_qual` and `dhex013_qual` real-PostgreSQL databases
from DH-EX-012C's and DH-EX-013's own qualification runs — real released-order data produced by
prior tickets' actual code paths, not seeded for this ticket — were confirmed already at
`alembic_version = 0018_exchange_release_versions` (`SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version`,
observed directly), and both tickets' own qualification suites (`test_dhex012c_postgres_
qualification.py`, `test_dhex013_postgres_qualification.py`) were re-run against them: **8 passed,
0 failures**, confirming the backfill logic holds against genuine historical data, not only against
this ticket's purpose-built fixtures.

**Downgrade guards, each independently demonstrated against real PostgreSQL:**
`DowngradeBlockedByAmendmentReleaseVersionHistory` (any `version_number > 1` row) and
`DowngradeBlockedByMultipleReviewsPerOrderHistory` (any `lab_order_id` with more than one review
row) — neither can trigger against this ticket's own reachable states (no amendment mechanism
exists to produce either condition), both exist to protect **future** DH-EX-014B history from an
accidental downgrade run much later. A real downgrade with neither condition present was run and
the pre-0018 shape was reconstructed exactly (both new tables dropped, `release_version_id` column
and its two constraints dropped, `UNIQUE(lab_order_id)` restored) — verified byte-for-bit against
the original `DoctorReview` status values, not assumed.

**Guard-removal data-loss demonstration (required negative control 10):** on a disposable clone of
the backfilled qualification database, a simulated `version_number = 2` row (with its own manifest
entry) was inserted, both guards disabled, and the downgrade forced through. Result: both new
tables were dropped entirely — **all evidence that a second (amendment) version had ever existed
vanished with no trace**, and the surviving `DoctorReview` row (status `NO_FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED`)
reverted to the flat pre-0018 shape, now silently appearing to describe the order's only-ever
version, with no way to tell it had actually been reviewed against different content than what a
provider might see after a real future amendment. Guards restored immediately after (confirmed via
`grep -rn "NEGATIVE CONTROL"` returning nothing); the disposable database dropped.

#### Release transaction, now atomic across four things

`LabResultReleaseRepository.release` (`results.py`), inside the same `LabOrder`-locked transaction
that already re-checks completeness, now also: computes the exact effective observation set across
every item (identical query shape to `list_for_order`'s own effective-only read); creates
`LabResultReleaseVersion` (`version_number=1`, bound to the just-inserted `LabResultRelease`);
inserts one manifest entry per effective observation; and binds the order's one existing, still-
unbound `PENDING` review row to the new version (never creates a second review row). All four
commit together or none do — the release insert, version, manifest, and review-binding are in the
identical session/transaction, verified by extending the pre-existing
`test_release_and_completion_audit_atomicity` test with explicit assertions that no version,
manifest, or review-binding survives when the transaction is forced to fail.

#### Reads

- **Provider read** (`get_lab_order_results`, `api.py`): branches on whether the order has a release
  version. If it does, reads the exact, immutable manifest — never live current-effective state —
  and the response gains `release_version_id`/`release_version_number`/`is_amendment` (all three
  `None` together only for a grandfathered order, `is_amendment` always `False` in this ticket).
  If it does not (a grandfathered order), falls through to the **unchanged legacy path**
  (`list_for_order`) — the two branches are deliberately kept separate, never merged into one
  conditional expression, per the ticket's own explicit instruction.
- **Historical manifest reads never filter by the observation's current `superseded_at`** — a
  manifest entry names an exact id and resolves it regardless of whether a (not-yet-existing)
  future amendment has since superseded it. Verified directly: since no code path in this ticket
  can actually reach that future state, a dedicated test forces it (`superseded_at` set directly on
  a manifested observation, bypassing every real code path) and confirms the manifest read still
  resolves it unchanged.
- **Lab pre-release inspection** (`get_for_lab`) is completely untouched — it continues reading live
  current-effective observations, which is correct for a screen inspecting what is *about to be*
  released, a different semantic from historical reconstruction. Not accidentally made to read a
  manifest. **Precision on how this is verified**: no test distinguishes "reads live" from "reads
  manifest" for this path, because in every state this ticket's own code can reach, the two reads
  return identical content (a released order's effective observations are, by the load-bearing
  invariant above, exactly what got manifested at release time) — so there is no reachable state in
  which the two semantics would visibly diverge yet. Verified instead by non-modification
  (`get_for_lab`'s source is byte-identical to before this ticket, confirmed via `git diff`) plus
  the pre-existing inspection tests continuing to pass, not by a differentiating test. A genuinely
  differentiating test becomes possible, and should be added, once DH-EX-014B can produce a state
  where live-effective and last-manifested content actually differ.
- New `DoctorReviewRepository` methods resolve "the current review for an order" by explicit
  `version_number` ordering (`coalesce(version_number, 0) DESC`, the one legacy/unbound row sorting
  lowest), never by `reviewed_at` or any other timestamp — `get_for_order`'s existing signature is
  unchanged (order-oriented, internally version-aware), plus new `get_for_release_version` and
  `get_history_for_order` for DH-EX-014B's future use.
- New release-version repository reads: `get_latest_release_version`, `get_release_version_history`,
  `get_release_version`, `get_manifest_for_order`, `get_manifest_for_version` — **two logical
  queries** regardless of item/observation count (one version-lookup `SELECT`, one batched joined
  manifest `SELECT`), matching this module's own established no-N+1 discipline. **Measured, not
  just reasoned about** (ticket's own explicit requirement): a new test
  (`test_get_manifest_for_order_query_count_does_not_scale_with_item_count`) hooks SQLAlchemy's
  `before_cursor_execute` event and counts SQL statements for `get_manifest_for_order` against a
  1-item/1-observation order versus a 5-item/10-observation order, asserting the counts are
  **identical** (3 cursor executions measured for both — the two logical `SELECT`s above plus one
  `BEGIN`, which `conftest.py:33-35`'s explicit-transaction SQLite/pysqlite workaround emits per
  test-fixture session and which real PostgreSQL's driver does not; the statement list was printed
  and inspected directly, not inferred) rather than asserting a hardcoded magic number — so the
  test
  goes red if a future change introduces a per-item or per-observation query, not merely if today's
  exact count changes for an unrelated reason.

#### API surface

New `GET .../organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/release-versions` (`LAB_TECH`/
`LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`, reusing `get_for_lab`'s existing non-enumerating tenant check purely for its
own tenant-check side effect) — the foundation read a future "Version 1 / Version 2 / Version 3" UI
will use once DH-EX-014B can produce more than one version; returns an empty list for a
grandfathered order, never a fabricated one. No amendment-preparation or amendment-release endpoint
exists anywhere. `security_audit.py` is **unchanged** — audited and concluded no new event type is
warranted, since creating a release-version/manifest is part of the existing `lab_results_released`
transaction and carries no independent semantic value the existing event doesn't already capture.

#### Required negative controls — all 10 executed against real code, every mutation reverted and re-verified green

1. Provider read forced back to live effective state (manifest branch disabled) → the golden-flow
   test's `release_version_id is not None` assertion went red. Reverted, re-passed.
2. Historical manifest read filtered by current `superseded_at` → the dedicated historical-read
   test went red (the manifested item disappeared entirely once its observation was forced
   superseded). Reverted, re-passed.
3. Original release omitted the last item's observation from the manifest (`effective_rows[:-1]`)
   → the multi-item manifest test went red (one item missing). Reverted, re-passed.
4. Manifest entries paired with the wrong item (rotated by one across a two-item order) →
   the cross-item integrity test went red (observation id mismatched its expected item).
   Reverted, re-passed.
5. Order-scoping filter removed from the release query (`LabOrderItem.lab_order_id == order_id`
   deleted) → the cross-order integrity test went red (a different order's item leaked into the
   manifest). Reverted, re-passed.
6. **Genuine multi-layer defense-in-depth finding, not a fabricated failure:** removing the new
   `uq_exchange_release_versions_order_version` constraint alone did not expose a race (the
   `LabOrder FOR UPDATE` lock plus the idempotent-replay early-return already fully serialize
   release attempts). Removing **both** that constraint and the lock together still did not produce
   duplicate versions — instead, 9 of 10 concurrent attempts raised an unhandled `IntegrityError`
   against DH-EX-012's own pre-existing `uq_exchange_lab_result_releases_lab_order_id` constraint
   (unrelated to this ticket), which remained fully sufficient on its own to prevent duplication,
   just without `release()`'s own graceful idempotent-replay translation. Reported exactly as
   observed. Both defenses restored; re-verified stable across 3 repeated runs.
7/8. **Atomicity, combined:** attempting a genuine mid-method premature `session.commit()` (to
   simulate "release exists without its manifest") does not silently partially commit under this
   codebase's `session_factory.begin()` context-manager convention — it raises `InvalidRequestError`
   immediately, since the context manager refuses further operations on a session whose managed
   transaction has already been closed. This is itself a real, disclosed finding: the convention
   makes a silent partial-commit bug structurally impossible to introduce here, not merely unlikely.
   The pre-existing `test_release_and_completion_audit_atomicity` (extended this ticket with
   explicit version/manifest/review-binding assertions) already proves the required outcome — a
   failure anywhere in the transaction rolls back everything, verified without needing to force an
   artificial split.
9. `uq_exchange_doctor_reviews_release_version_id` removed from the model → a dedicated test
   inserting two `DoctorReview` rows bound to the same release version, expecting `IntegrityError`,
   went red (`DID NOT RAISE`). Reverted, re-passed.
10. Both downgrade guards disabled, forced downgrade on a disposable clone with simulated
   `version_number = 2` history → real, observed silent semantic loss (see "Guard-removal
   data-loss demonstration" above). Guards restored; the pre-existing DH-EX-013/012C guard-removal
   precedent followed exactly.

`grep -rn "NEGATIVE CONTROL" adapter/src adapter/tests adapter/migrations` returns nothing — every
control fully reverted before proceeding.

#### Test matrix coverage

13 new repository-level tests (`test_exchange_results.py`) and 8 new/extended HTTP-level tests
(`test_exchange_results_api.py`) cover: single-observation Version 1 manifest, panel-item manifest,
multi-item manifest, pre-release-corrected-observation manifest uses the effective id, exact
manifest reconstruction, grandfathered order has no version/manifest (and release on it still
raises `LegacyCompletedOrderHasNoRelease`), unreleased order has no version, pending review binds
to Version 1 on release, review marked after release is bound and readable by version, review
history for the one-row case, release-version history ordering, release replay creates no second
version/manifest, historical manifest read ignores current `superseded_at`, manifest integrity
(cross-item, cross-order), duplicate-review-per-version database rejection, provider read version
metadata (explicit-release and grandfathered), release-version-history endpoint auth (lab tech/
releaser allowed, clinician denied, cross-lab non-enumerating, grandfathered returns empty),
extended release/completion audit atomicity, and patient-bearer boundary (no release-version/
manifest leakage). Plus 4 new real-PostgreSQL concurrency tests: original-release race (exactly one
version/manifest/bound review), correction-vs-release race re-qualified against the manifest,
concurrent-reader-never-observes-a-partial-manifest, and a version-scoped review race.

#### Validation

`ruff check`/`ruff format --check` on `src tests migrations scripts`: clean. Full SQLite suite:
**787 passed, 78 skipped** (up from DH-EX-013's baseline 766/74 — 21 net new tests, including the
query-count measurement control added after advisor review). Real-PostgreSQL, all five relevant
qualification files run together in one final pass for stability: `test_dhex007_postgres_qualification.py`

`test_dhex013_postgres_qualification.py` (4), `test_dhex014a_postgres_qualification.py` (4) —
**27 passed, 0 failures**. The new concurrency file re-run 4 times total (1 initial + 3 repeats),

- **Post-release amendment remains required before the first real-patient pilot** (Decision 3) —

**Human Decision Required: NO** — this ticket implements the six ADR-048 decisions Liban already

### DH-EX-014B · Post-release amendment preparation/release · P0 · ✅ IMPLEMENTED — SQLITE + REAL-POSTGRESQL QUALIFIED, 12 NEGATIVE CONTROLS VERIFIED

**Ticket:** DH-EX-014B. Implements post-release amendment preparation and release under ADR-048
Model 3 (accepted by Liban in ADR-048 §19 items 1–6). Resolves the required real-patient-pilot
blocker on post-release amendments.

**Recovery, Hardening & Continuity:**
Taken over from an interrupted session, followed by a dedicated closure and hardening pass.
No work was discarded, reset, or restarted. The implementation was audited against runtime reality,
hardened against query scaling regressions and lineage corruption, qualified across the full
PostgreSQL concurrency matrix, and verified against all 12 negative controls.

**Implementation & Domain Architecture:**
- **Schema & Migration (`0019_exchange_amendments`):**
  - Table: `exchange_amendments` (`id`, `lab_order_id`, `lab_organization_id`, `base_release_version_id`,
    `started_by_identity_id`, `started_at`, `released_by_identity_id`, `released_at`, `status`).
  - Identifiers: `started_by_identity_id`, `released_by_identity_id`. No `prepared_by_user_id`.
  - Zero reason requirement: no `reason` column in schema, no reason field in API request payload,
    adhering strictly to ADR-048 Decision 5 (no fabricated clinical reason taxonomy for MVP).
  - Partial unique index: `uq_exchange_amendments_one_preparing_per_order` on `(lab_order_id)` WHERE
    `status = 'PREPARING'`, guaranteeing at the database level that at most one active amendment
    preparation episode can exist per order.
  - Foreign keys: `exchange_lab_observations.amendment_id` and `exchange_release_versions.amendment_id`
    referencing `exchange_amendments.id`.
  - Check constraint: `ck_exchange_release_versions_v1_bound_to_release` on `exchange_release_versions`
    guaranteeing V1 is bound to `lab_result_release_id` with `amendment_id IS NULL`, and V > 1 is bound
    to `amendment_id` with `lab_result_release_id IS NULL`.
  - Downgrade guards: fail-closed with `DowngradeBlockedByAmendmentHistory` if any amendment exists,
    and with `DowngradeBlockedByAmendmentAuditVocabulary` if amendment security audit events exist.
- **Lifecycle & Endpoints (`results.py`, `api.py`):**
  - `POST /exchange/v1/organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/amendments` (`start_lab_order_amendment`):
    `LAB_TECH` only, requires order `COMPLETED`, no request body.
  - `POST /exchange/v1/organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/amendments/{amendment_id}/items/{item_id}/observations/{observation_id}/correct` (`correct_lab_order_amendment_observation`):
    `LAB_TECH` only, supersedes observation with immutable new row attributed to the amendment.
  - `POST /exchange/v1/organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/amendments/{amendment_id}/release` (`release_lab_order_amendment`):
    `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` only (403 if tech-only), requires at least one observation change (`AmendmentNotReadyForRelease`),
    creates new `LabResultReleaseVersion` (e.g. Version 2), creates immutable manifest (`LabResultReleaseManifestEntry`),
    marks amendment `RELEASED`, and creates fresh `PENDING` `DoctorReview` bound to the new version.
  - `GET /exchange/v1/organizations/{provider_id}/orders/{order_id}/release-versions` (`get_lab_order_release_version_history`):
    Clinician-read returning version history with reviews.
  - `GET /exchange/v1/organizations/{provider_id}/orders/{order_id}/release-versions/{release_version_id}` (`get_provider_release_version_content`):
    Clinician-read returning exact immutable manifest observations and review disposition for that version.
  - `POST /exchange/v1/organizations/{provider_id}/orders/{order_id}/release-versions/{release_version_id}/review/no-follow-up-required` and `.../follow-up-required`:
    Clinician endpoints to review explicit release version.
- **Provider History Query Scaling (N+1 Elimination):**
  - Added `LabResultReleaseRepository.get_release_version_history_with_reviews(order_id)`: single joined
    query on `DoctorReview.release_version_id == LabResultReleaseVersion.id`.
  - Added batch fetch `DoctorReviewRepository.get_for_release_versions(release_version_ids)`.
  - Statement count verified: repository method uses exactly 1 SELECT statement constant for 1 vs 5
    versions; API endpoint `GET /release-versions` executes exactly 7 SELECT statements (auth,
    membership, order, relationship) and 15 total statements, constant across 1 vs 4+ versions.
- **Lineage Integrity Defense:**
  - Added `AmendmentReleaseIntegrityError` (HTTP 409 Conflict) in `results.py:2105-2115` and `api.py:3433`.
  - Refuses release fail-closed if any effective observation at release time is not present in the base
    release manifest and is not attributed to the amendment being released.
- **Clinician Review Ambiguity Guard:**
  - `DoctorReviewRepository.record_review` enforces `ExplicitReviewVersionRequired` (HTTP 409 Conflict)
    for unversioned review mutations once Version > 1 exists, preventing clinicians from accidentally
    reviewing an unseen version.

**Real-PostgreSQL Concurrency Matrix (10/10 PASSED on native PostgreSQL 18 in WSL):**
- Baseline tests 1–6:
  - `test_concurrent_amendment_start_yields_one_preparing_episode`: 8 concurrent starters -> exactly 1 wins, 7 conflict.
  - `test_concurrent_corrections_yield_one_effective_successor`: 6 concurrent corrections -> exactly 1 successor.
  - `test_concurrent_amendment_release_is_one_version_one_review_one_manifest`: 6 concurrent releasers -> exactly 1 V2, 1 review.
  - `test_correction_racing_release_manifest_matches_the_winner`: correction racing release -> manifest matches winner.
  - `test_review_and_amendment_release_race_never_reviews_unseen_version`: review racing release -> V1 review never touches V2.
  - `test_reader_never_observes_partial_amendment_manifest`: concurrent readers never see partial manifest.
- Concurrency Matrix Scenarios A–D:
  - **Scenario A (`test_concurrent_independent_observation_corrections_both_succeed`):** concurrent corrections to
    different order items under the same amendment episode both commit successfully without lock collisions.
  - **Scenario B (`test_second_amendment_start_racing_first_amendment_release_sequences_properly`):** second amendment
    start racing first amendment release sequences properly (either refused if start runs before release completes,
    or succeeds against newly minted V2 base).
  - **Scenario C (`test_sequential_amendment_chain_through_version_three`):** sequential amendment chain V1 -> V2 -> V3

## DH-CLINIC-001 — Native DHealth Clinic foundation

**Date:** 2026-09-15
**Branch:** `master`
**Status:** COMPLETED
**Author:** Primary Agent & `dhealth_advisor`
**Reviewed By:** Senior Independent Advisor (`dhealth_advisor`)

### Summary & Goal

Established the native **DHealth Clinic** frontend application foundation and clean typed Exchange client boundary under `ui/src/features/clinic/` and `ui/src/api/exchangeClient.ts`.

This ticket delivers the native Clinic surface without breaking, modifying, or repurposing the existing OpenMRS connector maternity stack (all 19 pre-existing test files and 236 tests continue to pass without modification).

### Delivered Architecture & Components

1. **Typed Exchange Client Boundary (`ui/src/api/`):**
   - [`ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts`](ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts): Strongly typed models for `ExchangeIdentity`, `ExchangeMembershipSummary`, `ExchangeMeResponse`, `LabOrderSummary`, `LabOrder`, `ProviderOrderResults`, `ProviderReleaseVersionHistory`, `PatientReferenceResponse`, and related Enums.
   - [`ui/src/api/exchangeClient.ts`](ui/src/api/exchangeClient.ts): Direct client for DHealth Exchange endpoints (`/exchange/v1/me`, `/organizations/{id}/orders`, `/organizations/{id}/orders/{order_id}`, `/organizations/{id}/orders/{order_id}/results`, `/organizations/{id}/orders/{order_id}/release-versions`, `/organizations/{id}/patient-references`).
   - Normalizes FastAPI error responses (`{ detail: string | Array<{ msg: string }> }`) into typed `ExchangeApiError` instances with semantic codes (`UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `SERVER_ERROR`, `NETWORK_ERROR`).
   - Includes `mapExchangeErrorToCode` adapter for design system `ErrorState`.
   - **Zero calls to `/openmrs/*`** from the Exchange client boundary.

2. **Native Clinic Application Shell & State (`ui/src/features/clinic/`):**
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicContext.ts`](ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicContext.ts) & [`ClinicProvider.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicProvider.tsx): Provider organization context with automatic identity bootstrap via `/me`. Enforces Finding F-08: filters strictly for active provider organizations with active clinician roles (`organization_type === 'PROVIDER'`, `organization_status === 'ACTIVE'`, `membership_status === 'ACTIVE'`, `roles.includes('CLINICIAN')`). Truthful states for `loading`, `ready`, `unauthenticated`, `no_clinics`, and `error` without mock fallback.
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicShell.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicShell.tsx) & [`ClinicShell.module.css`](ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicShell.module.css): French-first responsive navigation with accessible tabs (`Accueil`, `Patients`, `Ordres de laboratoire`, `Résultats`), active clinic selector badge, and app mode switcher.
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicApp.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/ClinicApp.tsx): Top-level Clinic application component managing active navigation tabs.

3. **Clinic Pages:**
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicHomePage.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicHomePage.tsx): Summary cards for *Ordres actifs* (pending, accepted, in-progress), *Résultats disponibles* (completed), and *À revoir* (truthful navigation to results tab). Avoids N+1 query storms by deriving counts directly from provider orders list.
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicPatientsPage.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicPatientsPage.tsx): Truthful patient boundary explanation pending DH-CLINIC-002; zero calls to OpenMRS and zero fabricated patient names.
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicOrdersPage.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicOrdersPage.tsx): Provider orders table displaying status badges, order priority, timestamps, test counts, and opaque patient reference tokens (`patient_reference_id` UUIDs).
   - [`ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicResultsPage.tsx`](ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicResultsPage.tsx): Lists completed orders and allows drill-down into order-scoped `/results` to view released observations, reference ranges, abnormal flags, and lab comments.

4. **Integration & Connector Stack Preservation:**
   - [`ui/src/design-system/AppShell.tsx`](ui/src/design-system/AppShell.tsx): Added optional `headerActions` slot to allow seamless app switching.
   - [`ui/src/App.tsx`](ui/src/App.tsx): Preserves default OpenMRS maternity workflow. Adds mode toggle to switch between OpenMRS Maternity and native DHealth Clinic. All existing 236 OpenMRS maternity tests pass without regression.

### Patient Workflow Audit for DH-CLINIC-002

An audit of the Exchange backend API (`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`) revealed the following constraints for native patient management:
- **Available endpoint:** `POST /organizations/{provider_id}/patient-references` exists to bind/register a patient reference token.
- **Missing endpoints:**
  - No patient search endpoint (cannot search by name, phone, birth date, or external identifier).
  - No patient list endpoint (no `GET /organizations/{provider_id}/patient-references`).
  - No patient detail endpoint (no `GET .../patient-references/{id}`).
- **Response payload limitation:**
  - `POST .../patient-references` returns `PatientReferenceResponse(id=..., source_organization_id=..., source_system=..., source_identity_system=..., source_identity_value=...)` (no `created_at` or patient profile representation).
  - It does NOT return `display_name`, `phone_number`, or contact channels in the response model.
- **Architectural laws:**
  - The Exchange is an interoperability hub, not a centralized national patient registry.
  - `PatientReference` is strictly scoped to a provider organization; there is no global patient registry and no fuzzy matching across clinics.
- **Requirement for DH-CLINIC-002:**
  To implement native provider-scoped patient finding and registration, DH-CLINIC-002 should either:
  1. Add a provider-scoped patient lookup/list endpoint to the Exchange API: `GET /organizations/{provider_id}/patient-references?query=...` with strict provider authorization.
  2. Include `display_name` in the patient reference retrieval model so clinicians can identify patients within their own clinic.

### Infrastructure & Keycloak Notes for SPA

- **Reverse Proxy Routing:**
  In local development and production (`caddy/Caddyfile` and Vite dev server `vite.config.ts`), requests to `/exchange/v1/*` must be routed to the Exchange backend service (`http://exchange:8000` or `http://localhost:8000`), alongside existing `/openmrs/*` reverse proxy rules.
- **Keycloak Client Configuration:**
  Direct browser authentication for the SPA requires a public Keycloak client configured with PKCE (e.g., client ID `dhealth-clinic-ui`, standard flow with PKCE, valid redirect URIs).

### Independent Advisor Review (`dhealth_advisor`)

- Phase 3 independent architecture and plan review performed by `dhealth_advisor` (conversation `536af9f4-776e-42af-989e-b3581d192006`).
- Phase 3 Findings & Dispositions:
  - **F-01 (CORS & Caddy/Vite Routing):** RESOLVED. Base URL made configurable via `baseUrl` option and `VITE_EXCHANGE_BASE_URL`. Documented proxy requirements.

  - **F-06 (FastAPI Error Parsing):** RESOLVED. Handled `{ detail }` string and array structures and provided `mapExchangeErrorToCode`.
  - **F-07 (A11y Navigation Collision):** RESOLVED. Disjoint accessible names (`Navigation DHealth Clinique` vs `Navigation principale`).
  - **F-08 (Multi-Provider Filter):** RESOLVED. Filtered memberships for `organization_type === 'PROVIDER'`, active statuses, and `CLINICIAN` role.
  - **F-09 (TypeScript Compiler Constraints):** RESOLVED. Used `import type` and `const` string unions.
- Phase 6 Independent Review (`dhealth_advisor` conversation `14cce7fd-d8bd-4abc-95bb-58c263a19d70`):

## DH-CLINIC-002A — Native Clinic contract and patient-safety hardening

**Date:** 2026-09-15
**Starting HEAD / `origin/master`:** `e0eaef9a1b54577918cd5a9c5c342e151d746657`
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED + LOCALLY VERIFIED + FULL UI SUITE (307 passed) + ADVISOR APPROVED + CI-QUALIFIED (exact-SHA run 35016425683: 9/9 jobs passed)
**Migration head:** `0019_exchange_amendments` (unchanged; no migration added)  
**Exact CI Commit SHA:** `b8879122268f36c60e67185d81ec7c3374b3adf3`
**GitHub Actions Run ID:** `35016425683` (https://github.com/brittLiban/d-health/actions/runs/35016425683)

### Summary of Changes & Contract Hardening

1. **Order-Status Contract Alignment:**
   - Reconciled `LabOrderStatus` in `ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts` with backend Pydantic/FastAPI schemas:
     `AWAITING_LAB_SELECTION | SELECTED | ACCEPTED | IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED | REJECTED | CANCELLED`.
   - Removed invented statuses (`PENDING_SELECTION`, `LAB_ASSIGNED`, `SUBMITTED`).
   - Updated `ClinicOrdersPage.tsx` with truthful French labels and design-system status tones for all 7 genuine statuses.

2. **Result Observation & Review State Contract Alignment:**
   - Corrected `DoctorReviewStatus` in `ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts` and `ClinicResultsPage.tsx` to exact backend strings:
     `PENDING` (*"À examiner"*), `NO_FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED` (*"Sans suite requise"*), `FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED` (*"Suivi clinique requis"*).
   - In `ClinicResultsPage.tsx`, review status is now read from release version summaries (`GET /release-versions`), not order results (where it does not exist).
   - Reconciled observation rendering to genuine backend fields (`catalog_display_name_snapshot`, `catalog_code_snapshot`, `display_label_snapshot`, `numeric_value`, `numeric_unit`, `reference_range_low`/`high`, `text_value`). Removed invented phantom fields (`abnormal_flag`, `value_coded`, `value_boolean`).
   - Safely handled grandfathered orders where `release_version_number === null` by displaying *"Résultats initiaux"* rather than rendering `"Version null"`.

3. **Patient Creation Error Classification:**
   - In `ui/src/api/exchangeClient.ts`, HTTP 400 is now explicitly mapped to `VALIDATION_ERROR` (previously defaulted to `SERVER_ERROR`).
   - Implemented `isDefinitiveExchangeError` (classifies 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 as definitive) and `isAmbiguousExchangeError` (classifies status 0 network drops and 5xx as ambiguous).
   - Definitive failure: clears pending state from storage and memory, presents sanitized error message, leaves form fields editable, and mints a fresh client UUID on next submission without claiming duplicate-safe replay.
   - Ambiguous failure: retains opaque identity tuple in storage and memory, and presents safe retry option reusing the exact client-minted identity.

4. **Persist-Before-POST & Fail-Closed Durability (Zero PHI):**
   - In `ui/src/features/clinic/pendingPatientStorage.ts`, browser storage holds strictly technical identifiers:
     `source_system`, `source_identity_system`, `source_identity_value`, `created_at`, and `confirmed_patient_reference_id` (post-bind). STRICTLY ZERO PHI (no names, phones, or demographics).
   - Scoped strictly to authenticated user identity and active provider (`${userId}:${providerId}`).
   - Durability is a prerequisite for POST: `setStoredPendingPatient` writes and reads back to verify before POST. Unreadable or unwritable storage fails closed (blocks mutation and displays safe error).
   - No destructive TTL: unresolved identities are retained indefinitely until authoritatively resolved by the server to prevent accidental duplicate patient creation.
   - Discard action eliminated: unresolved attempts must be resumed/reconciled with the server, never casually discarded into a fresh UUID.
   - Logout intentionally retains this scoped non-PHI record so that logging out does not destroy the only key needed to prevent duplicate patient creation on subsequent login.

5. **Mutation vs. Detail Read Separation:**
   - Decoupled Phase A (mutation via bind POST) from Phase B (authoritative detail retrieval via GET).
   - Once Phase A returns successfully, the patient reference is confirmed independently of whether Phase B succeeds.
   - Subsequent GET failure (definitive 403 or transient 503/network) enters a confirmed/read-recovery state (*"Patient créé : La création est confirmée, mais la fiche patient ne peut pas être ouverte pour le moment."*).
   - Recovery retry executes GET only (`client.getPatientReference`); it cannot repeat the bind POST.
   - Verified across an explicit 2x2 created/replay x definitive/transient GET failure matrix.

6. **Provider-Switching Isolation:**
   - A POST initiated under Provider A that resolves after switching to Provider B remains strictly scoped to Provider A.
   - Provider B UI never consumes or displays Provider A's pending or confirmed state.
   - Switching back to Provider A restores the confirmed reference and scoped read retry.

7. **Decimal Wire Contract Alignment:**
   - FastAPI/Pydantic returns Decimal fields (`numeric_value`, `reference_range_low`, `reference_range_high`) as JSON strings.
   - Asserted in backend API test (`test_exchange_results_api.py`) that Decimal fields are JSON strings preserving exact precision (allowing PostgreSQL `NUMERIC` scale formatting e.g. `"13.5000"`).
   - Frontend types (`exchangeTypes.ts`) model them as `string | null` and test fixtures match.

8. **Mandatory Patient Display Name in Native Clinic UI:**
   - In `ClinicPatientsPage.tsx`, patient creation requires non-blank `displayName.trim()`. Form validation blocks submission client-side with *"Le nom affiché est obligatoire."*
   - Phone (`contactValue`) remains optional.
   - Exchange backend API contract remains untouched (background connector/import flows can still bind references without display names).

9. **Fail-Closed Corrupted Pending Patient Storage (Zero Silent Deletion):**
   - In `pendingPatientStorage.ts`, when a scoped pending patient key exists in `localStorage` but cannot be safely parsed (malformed JSON, invalid field types, missing required source identity value, or untrusted schema), the storage layer throws `PendingPatientStorageReadError`.
   - Absolutely never deletes, clears, or resets corrupted storage entries; the raw record remains intact for safe/manual recovery.
   - `ClinicPatientsPage` treats this condition as unreadable storage (`storageUnreadable`): renders safe server error banner without leaking raw technical contents or PHI, disables *"Nouveau patient"* button, closes creation form, disables submit, and ensures `bindPatientReferenceWithOutcome` is never called (0 mutation POSTs) and no fresh UUID is minted.
   - Distinguishes strictly between truly absent keys (`localStorage.getItem(key) === null` -> returns `null` normally) and corrupted keys (throws fail-closed error).

### Negative Controls Executed

1. **NC 1: Bypass storage verification before POST (frontend)**
   - Property: Mutation POST must not execute if durable storage write/read-back verification fails.
   - Mutation: In `ClinicPatientsPage.tsx`, commented out `return` on `setStoredPendingPatient` failure.
   - Result: RED (`AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` in `ClinicPatientsPage.test.tsx`).
   - Restored: GREEN.

2. **NC 2: Created bind + GET failure can retry POST (frontend)**

   - Result: RED (`AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times` in `ClinicPatientsPage.test.tsx`).

   - Mutation: In `ClinicPatientsPage.tsx`, second `bindPatientReferenceWithOutcome` call injected in `handleRetryConfirmedRead`.
   - Result: RED (`AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times` on replay test).
   - Restored: GREEN.

4. **NC 4: Destructive TTL (frontend)**

   - Restored: GREEN.

   - Result: RED (`Error: expect(element).not.toBeInTheDocument()` finding button in `ClinicPatientsPage.test.tsx`).

6. **NC 6: Provider-A confirmation attaches to current Provider B (frontend)**

   - Restored: GREEN.

7. **NC 7: localStorage read exception treated as "no record" (frontend)**
   - Property: `localStorage.getItem` throwing must fail closed, not pretend there is no pending record.
   - Mutation: In `pendingPatientStorage.ts`, caught read exception and returned `null`, and made `canReadPendingPatientStorage` return `true`.
   - Result: RED (error banner not rendered; "Nouveau patient" button not disabled in `ClinicPatientsPage.test.tsx`).
   - Restored: GREEN.

8. **NC 8: Wrong Decimal frontend wire representation (frontend & contract)**
   - Property: Decimal observation values are JSON strings, not JavaScript numbers.
   - Mutation: In `exchangeClient.test.ts`, asserted `typeof obs.numeric_value === 'number'`.
   - Result: RED (`AssertionError: expected 'string' to be 'number'`).
   - Restored: GREEN.

### Objective & Context

Narrow safety correction to `DH-CLINIC-003` addressing 3 critical safety blockers identified by independent review:
1. **BLOCKER 1:** Eliminate discarding of unresolved ambiguous order intent (K1). Once mutation enters `uncertain` state, freeze exact order intent (authenticated identity, provider, patient reference ID, catalog entry IDs, and idempotency key). Disable/hide "Modifier les services"; "Annuler" / closing wizard ("Fermer") retains intent; reopening wizard returns to frozen review/retry intent.

Rehydrate pending order per `(userId, providerId, patientReferenceId)` scope in memory (`ClinicApp.tsx`) and durable technical non-PHI metadata in browser storage (`pendingOrderStorage.ts`). Resolve reload deadlock: query server by idempotency key (`getOrderByIdempotencyKey`); if found, authoritatively confirm; if 404, allow clinician to explicitly abandon uncommitted attempt or retry.

Replace hardcoded `"Laboratoire : Pas encore sélectionné"` with truthful status-derived text (`formatOrderLabText`): only `"Pas encore sélectionné"` for `AWAITING_LAB_SELECTION`; `"Non assigné (ordre annulé)"` for `CANCELLED`; `"Laboratoire sélectionné"` for routed statuses (`SELECTED`, `ACCEPTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `REJECTED`).

### Objective & Context

Final order reconciliation safety correction to `DH-CLINIC-003A` addressing 3 independently verified safety gaps:
1. **BLOCKER 1 (Persist-before-POST Durability):** Persist technical reconciliation record (`user_id`, `provider_id`, `patient_reference_id`, `idempotency_key`, `created_at`) and verify read-back BEFORE issuing the network POST. 3. **BLOCKER 3 (Terminal Lab-State Truthfulness):** Correct `formatOrderLabText` so that `REJECTED` and `CANCELLED` do not falsely infer historical lab assignment. Both map to `"Indéterminé pour cet ordre clôturé"`; `AWAITING_LAB_SELECTION` maps to `"Pas encore sélectionné"`; routed states (`SELECTED`, `ACCEPTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`) map to `"Sélectionné"`.

### Human Decision Gate: Cross-Reload Exact Replay Architecture

**Human Decision Required: YES**

The core issue: Across a full browser reload/restart, persistent storage currently stores strictly technical non-PHI metadata (`user_id`, `provider_id`, `patient_reference_id`, `idempotency_key`, `created_at`), deliberately omitting clinical test IDs/codes (`catalog_entry_ids`) to satisfy clinic privacy rules.

If an order POST is in-flight when the browser reloads and the server returns 404 on idempotency key lookup (i.e. not yet committed or never reached server):
- The unresolved intent is preserved.
- Fresh order creation is disabled.
- The clinician clicks "Vérifier / réessayer", which opens the catalog to re-select tests and submit with the EXACT same frozen idempotency key.

There are three long-term architectural choices for cross-reload payload recovery:

1. **Option A: Backend-owned intent (Draft Order Resource)**
   - Before firing the final mutation, the client creates a draft order resource on the backend (e.g. `POST .../orders/drafts`).
   - *Pros:* Zero clinical data stored in the browser; allows seamless resume across devices, browsers, and reloads without re-selecting tests.
   - *Cons:* Requires a new database table/migration, API endpoints, and lifecycle management (garbage collection for abandoned drafts).
   - *Recommendation:* Target for subsequent post-MVP milestone.

2. **Option B: Scoped browser storage with test IDs**
   - Store `catalog_entry_ids: string[]` (opaque UUIDs of catalog items) alongside technical metadata in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.
   - *Pros:* Zero backend schema changes; allows automatic payload restoration on reload.
   - *Cons:* Places diagnostic test selections into browser storage on potentially shared clinic workstation PCs, raising clinical data privacy/governance concerns under ADR-043.
   - *Recommendation:* Do NOT adopt without explicit sign-off from Liban.

3. **Option C: Fail-closed without payload replay across reload (Current Implementation Baseline)**
   - Browser stores strictly technical non-PHI metadata (`user_id`, `provider_id`, `patient_reference_id`, `idempotency_key`, `created_at`).
   - If server already committed the order, `getOrderByIdempotencyKey` reconciles it into confirmed state automatically.
   - If server has not committed (404), the unresolved intent blocks new orders and prompts the clinician to re-select the tests under the exact same frozen idempotency key.
   - *Pros:* 100% compliant with zero-clinical-data-in-storage rule; zero database migrations; duplicate-safe via database unique constraint.
   - *Cons:* In the rare event of a reload during an uncommitted in-flight order, the clinician must re-check the test checkboxes before clicking submit.

**Primary Agent Recommendation:** Adopt **Option C** for MVP 1.0. Await Liban's decision before proceeding with Option A.

## Implementation

- Backend-owned durable `LabOrderIntent`/`LabOrderIntentItem` (migration
  `0020_exchange_order_intents`), completed by the corrective `0021_order_intent_ownership`
  migration that added the `exchange_lab_orders.intent_id` column the ORM already declared.
- Bidirectional ownership invariant (`LabOrder.intent_id == LabOrderIntent.id` and
  `LabOrderIntent.committed_lab_order_id == LabOrder.id`), written and checked in one transaction.
- Legacy `/orders` convergence: the legacy endpoint no longer has an independent creation path — it
  acquires or consumes the same durable intent reservation as native Clinic ordering.
- Immutable commit: the commit endpoint accepts no request body; an adversarial body has zero
  effect on the resulting order (permanently tested, not just structurally argued).
- Clinician-bound recovery: intent retrieval is restricted to the original authoring clinician,
  anti-enumerating `404` for a different clinician at the same provider.
- Browser technical-only persistence: `pendingOrderStorage.ts` stores exactly the approved
  non-clinical field allowlist; never catalog ids, service names/codes, or PHI.
- A stale-reconciliation-state defect (`reconcilingStoredOrder` could remain stuck `true` after a
  patient/provider switch, blocking "Nouvel ordre de laboratoire" for an unrelated scope) was found
  by writing a genuine regression test for the recovery race, fixed with a synchronous scope-reset
  at the top of the recovery effect, and covered by permanent regression tests. Full record: ADR-049.

Full architectural decision record, including the rejected alternatives: **ADR-049**
(`DECISIONS.md`). Runtime-flow detail: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §17, "Durable Provider Lab Order
Intent."

## Final independent advisor review (2026-09-16) — one blocker found and fixed

Liban's own final independent review of the complete DH-CLINIC-003C diff found one substantive
backend compatibility defect, everything else assessed as strong: the Option-A implementation,
migration, UI recovery model, concurrency qualification, and coverage closure.

**Blocker — pre-003C historical legacy order replay regressed to `409`.** A pre-003C `LabOrder`
(`intent_id IS NULL`) retried through the legacy `POST .../orders` endpoint with its exact
original canonical content should replay idempotently (`200`, same order), matching that
endpoint's contract from before durable intents existed. Reproduced directly: the legacy route,
finding no existing `LabOrderIntent` reservation, created a *new* one; that intent's commit then
found the historical order already sitting under the same key and, seeing `existing_order.intent_id
IS NULL` rather than the new intent's own id, raised `IdempotencyKeyConflict` — `409` instead of
`200`, with detail `"idempotency key is already associated with an order outside this durable
intent"`.

**Fix:** the legacy route now looks up an existing `intent_id IS NULL` order under the exact same
`(provider_organization_id, idempotency_key)` *before* reserving any new intent. An exact
canonical match (patient, practitioner, service set) replays it unchanged — `200`, same order id,
zero new `LabOrderIntent` rows, zero new `lab_order_created` audit rows, `intent_id` still `NULL`.
A mismatch still conflicts (`409`), exactly as before. Native intent registration/commit is
unaffected and still fails closed on any collision with a historical key. Two permanent regression
tests added (exact historical replay → 200; mismatched retry → 409), plus the existing NC1 and
PG3–PG6 real-PostgreSQL suites re-verified intact. Full detail: `DECISIONS.md` ADR-049's "Legacy
`/orders` convergence" section.

Two further, narrower items were also corrected in this same pass (component-wide UI state that
could leak an unrelated patient's storage-unreadable fail-closed status across a scope switch —
same defect class as the earlier `reconcilingStoredOrder` fix, labeled **NC26**; and an invalid
unconditional assertion in the real-PostgreSQL PG4 race test that only tolerated one of two valid
interleavings). Both are recorded in the session's negative-control evidence, not detailed again
here.
