## DH-CLINIC-004A (2026-09-17) — native browser authentication + same-origin Exchange routing

**Starting master SHA:** `357bd3578ec86024e6ff787bbd39b2327b47245e` (DH-STATE-001, confirmed merged
via `git fetch` + `origin/master`, not trusted from a prior recap). **Branch:**
`dh-clinic-004a-browser-auth`, cut fresh from `master`, never stacked on the unmerged
`dh-state-001-canonical-status` branch.

**Objective and scope.** Make the native DHealth Clinic frontend structurally capable of
authenticating a real browser user against the `dhealth-exchange` Keycloak realm and calling the
Exchange through the same `app.${BASE_DOMAIN}` origin — as reusable infrastructure future native
apps (DHealth Lab) can adopt without copying Clinic code. Full decision record: `DECISIONS.md`
ADR-050.

**What was built:**

- **Shared native auth layer**, `ui/src/features/auth/exchange/`: `ExchangeAuthProvider`/
  `useExchangeAuth()` (owns the `keycloak-js` session, Authorization Code + PKCE S256,
  `onLoad: 'check-sso'` so initialization itself never redirects as a side effect — `login()` is a
  deliberate follow-up action taken only after `init()` finds no session), `exchangeTokenProvider.ts`
  (single-flight, fail-closed `getAuthToken` callback wired into `ExchangeClient`'s existing,
  previously-unused token-provider architecture), `exchangeAuthConfig.ts` (fails closed on any
  hostname not matching the trusted `app.<domain>` → `id.<domain>` shape, rather than guessing),
  `ExchangeAuthGate` (generic, presentational — blocks rendering, and therefore `/me`, until real
  authentication exists).
- **`App.tsx`** now wraps native Clinic in `ExchangeAuthProvider` + `ExchangeAuthGate` and injects
  the resulting authenticated `ExchangeClient` into `ClinicApp`; Clinic's own logout calls
  `useExchangeAuth().logout()` (terminates only the Exchange session), never the reference
  connector's `logoutLocalSessions()`/`navigateToKeycloakEndSession()`. Switching apps unmounts the
  provider (dropping in-memory token state) without calling either session's logout.
- **Removed the misleading manual `authToken` prop** threaded through `ClinicApp`/`ClinicProvider`/
  `ClinicContext` and every Clinic page — it was always `null` in every real call path (nothing ever
  set it) and every removed argument was already silently falling through to `ExchangeClient`'s own
  `getAuthToken`. Zero behavior change; done as its own commit.
- **`keycloak/realm-config/dhealth-exchange-realm.json`**: added `dhealth-native-ui`, a second,
  public, secretless client alongside the unchanged confidential `dhealth-exchange-api` — standard
  flow only (implicit/direct-grant/service-accounts disabled), `pkce.code.challenge.method: S256`
  enforced server-side, redirect/web-origin scoped to `https://app.${BASE_DOMAIN}` only (no
  wildcard), and the identical `exchange-api-audience` mapper the confidential client already
  carries.
- **`caddy/Caddyfile`**: `app.{$BASE_DOMAIN}`'s existing `route{}` block now also handles
  `/exchange/v1/*` → `adapter:8000`, inside the block and ahead of the `daher-ui` catch-all, mirroring
  the dedicated `exchange.{$BASE_DOMAIN}` vhost's own path scoping (which is untouched and remains).
  No CORS introduced; no CSRF header guard added to this route (deliberately — it is bearer-token,
  not cookie, authenticated, so it carries none of the cross-site-form risk that guard exists for).
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: the two existing Caddy/realm static-check steps (not new steps)
  extended to assert the new client's full security posture (public, secretless, PKCE-enforced,
  non-wildcard origin/redirect, correct audience mapper) and the new `app.` route. Verified locally
  before push by extracting and re-running both embedded Python blocks against the changed files.
- **`ui/scripts/check-no-secrets-in-bundle.mjs`**: also refuses a build containing the literal
  `KEYCLOAK_EXCHANGE_API_CLIENT_SECRET` value (NS1) — the new public client has no secret of its own
  to check for by design.
- **`.env.example`**: documents the three new public Vite variables
  (`VITE_EXCHANGE_KEYCLOAK_URL`/`_REALM`/`_CLIENT_ID`), all safe public configuration, none a
  secret.
- **`adapter/tests/test_exchange_token_validator.py`**: one new unit test proving `TokenValidator`
  accepts a token whose `azp` is `dhealth-native-ui` purely on `iss`/`aud`/signature — converts the
  "the audience mapper should make this work" reasoning into an observed result. Zero backend
  production code changed.

**Deliberately not built (DH-CLINIC-004B's job, not silently patched over here):**

- Real Keycloak import/reconciliation of the two-client realm file on a deployment whose Keycloak
  database already has `dhealth-exchange` imported. `docker-compose.yml`'s `--import-realm` flag
  refuses to overwrite an existing realm, so `dhealth-native-ui` only appears automatically on a
  **fresh** Keycloak database; `keycloak/reconcile-sso.sh` deliberately never touches this realm.
  This is a genuine deployment-correctness gap, recorded honestly rather than fixed by extending the
  reconciliation script under this ticket's scope.
- Any real browser OIDC round trip: redirect, login, PKCE code exchange, token acceptance by a live
  adapter, refresh/expiry against a real Keycloak, live Caddy routing observed end to end. Nothing
  above was booted; every claim in this entry is component/unit/static-config-level.

**Qualification, all run locally before commit:**

- UI: lint, typecheck, build (bundle secret scan clean, includes the new NS1 needle), and the full
  test suite — **29 files, 397 tests, all passing** (370 pre-existing + 23 new exchange-auth-layer

## DH-CLINIC-004B (2026-09-17) — real Keycloak + browser E2E qualification

**Starting master SHA:** `2cf0350ae168df6cb3596324550ed858f028d141` (DH-CLINIC-004A, confirmed
merged fast-forward per Liban's explicit `--ff-only` instructions). **No branch, no PR** — per this
ticket's own explicit instruction ("Liban has explicitly decided not to use pull requests for this
development workflow"), all work landed as focused commits directly on `master`.

**Objective and scope.** Close DH-CLINIC-004A/ADR-050's two named gaps: (1) reconcile
`dhealth-native-ui` onto an already-imported `dhealth-exchange` realm, since `--import-realm` never
overwrites an existing realm; (2) actually observe a real browser complete the Authorization Code +
PKCE round trip against a real Keycloak/Caddy/adapter stack, using synthetic identities through real
admin-API paths, with zero mocking of the OIDC flow.

**Status: PARTIALLY QUALIFIED — INCOMPLETE.** Gap (1) is done and real-Keycloak-runtime-qualified.
Gap (2) is built (code, typecheck, lint all pass) but has never executed against a live browser. Do
not read this entry as ticket closure.

### What was built and is real-Keycloak-runtime-qualified

- **`keycloak/reconcile-exchange.sh`**, mirroring the existing `keycloak/reconcile-sso.sh` pattern
  for the `daher` realm: creates `dhealth-native-ui` if absent, unconditionally converges every
  security field (`publicClient=true`, PKCE S256, disabled implicit/direct-grant/service-account
  flows, redirect/web-origin scoping, the `exchange-api-audience` mapper) via `kcadm update`, using
  list-and-filter lookups throughout (never a name-in-path lookup). Explicitly checks
  `dhealth-exchange-api` is present and still `publicClient=false` but never creates or modifies it.
  Wired into `docker-compose.yml` as a new one-shot `keycloak-exchange-config` service, same shape as
  the existing `keycloak-sso-config` service it sits beside.
- **Real-run evidence** (run `35210377720`, commit `7752bf9`, `workflow_dispatch`, Case A/fresh
  realm, against the real pinned `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.1@sha256:f1f1f01e...c01c6` image):
  Keycloak's own log — `Realm 'dhealth-exchange' imported`; `keycloak-sso-config` and
  `keycloak-exchange-config` both `Exited (0)`; the new reconciler's own success log —
  `Keycloak Exchange clients reconciled: dhealth-native-ui public PKCE browser client`. `git diff
  --check` clean; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s extended DH-EX-008 static checks (verifying the
  compose wiring and that the script never touches `dhealth-exchange-api`) re-extracted and re-run
  locally before every push, all green; fast CI green on every pushed commit (`origin/master`, 9/9
  jobs, most recently run `35210369738` at this ticket's final commit).
- **A genuine deployment-breaking defect found and fixed** (the highest-value finding of this
  ticket): `dhealth-exchange-realm.json`'s `dhealth-platform-admin` role description (327 chars) and
  `dhealth-native-ui` client description (320 chars) both exceeded Keycloak's `VARCHAR(255)` column
  limit. Against a real database this doesn't just refuse the field — it crashes the entire realm
  import (`ERROR: value too long for type character varying(255)`) and takes the Keycloak process
  down with it, which in turn produced a secondary, initially-misleading symptom (both one-shot
  reconciler services hitting `503 Service Unavailable` as Keycloak crash-looped under them). Neither
  DH-CLINIC-004A's own review nor this ticket's own DH-EX-008 static-check extension could have
  caught this — only a real import against a real database enforces the column limit. Fixed
  (commit `7752bf9`), meaning preserved, every string field in every committed realm-config JSON
  re-scanned for length afterward.
- Also fixed, found genuinely blocking this ticket's own qualification run (not merely documented,
  per the "unrelated bugs... unless blocking" rule): a real Keycloak admin-API bootstrap race —
  Keycloak's Docker healthcheck can report healthy several seconds before its own admin REST API
  finishes bootstrapping, during which it returns 503. A 10-attempt/3s-backoff login retry was added
  to `reconcile-exchange.sh`, this ticket's own orchestrator, **and** the pre-existing
  `reconcile-sso.sh` (which races the identical window in the identical `docker compose up`).

### What was built but has never run against a real browser

- **`ui/e2e/`** — a `@playwright/test`-only (no Cypress), Chromium-only real-browser E2E suite:
  12 scenarios (E2E-1 through E2E-12: full PKCE login with `code_challenge_method=S256` assertion,
  real token issuer/audience/azp/subject decoding without ever logging the raw token, real
  JWKS-based adapter validation, same-origin `/exchange/v1/*` routing with a negative control that
  unrelated adapter endpoints aren't exposed through the app vhost, real token refresh, real
  session-revocation-then-fail-closed, logout scoped to Exchange only with an explicit assertion that
  no navigation ever touches OpenMRS/OpenELIS paths, app-switch-is-not-logout via SSO reuse, and a
  truthful "not assigned to any organization" empty state for an authenticated-but-unassigned
  identity) plus 4 negative controls (no token, structurally invalid token, wrong-audience token,
  cross-provider-organization 404 anti-enumeration). All synthetic test identities use
  `@example.invalid` addresses, created through real, already-supported Exchange admin API paths —
  never a database bypass. `tsc -p e2e/tsconfig.json` and lint both pass.
- Two non-discriminating assertions (E2E-6, E2E-7) were found and fixed on the author's own review,
  before any live run reached them — both were written in a way that would pass regardless of
  whether the actual property being tested held (see `STATUS.md`'s edit history / commit `38c0f82`
  for detail).
- **`scripts/qualify-native-auth.sh`** — the one-command qualification orchestrator (`--mode=fresh`
  or `--mode=upgrade`), and **`.github/workflows/qualify-native-auth.yml`** — a separate,
  `workflow_dispatch`-only CI workflow (`mode: fresh|upgrade|both`), per this ticket's explicit
  instruction to never force the real E2E suite into fast/PR-gating CI. Case B (`--mode=upgrade`)
  strips `dhealth-native-ui` from the realm file, boots only Keycloak, confirms the client is absent
  (proving `--import-realm`'s non-overwrite behavior empirically, not just by reading the flag's
  docs), creates a representative pre-existing synthetic user and realm role, restores the real realm
  file, reboots, and (after the full stack + reconciler) asserts both the pre-existing user/role
  survived and `dhealth-native-ui` was added.
- **None of this has executed against a live browser.** The one workflow dispatch that ran
  (`35210377720`, `mode=both`) got through Case A's Keycloak/reconciliation phase (above) but then
  stalled: `openmrs-backend` and `openelis-webapp` — pre-existing, unmodified reference-connector
  services — never reached Docker `healthy` within the run's 3600s `--wait` window. Caddy's own
  `depends_on` (`openmrs-gateway`/`openelis-frontend: condition: service_started`, both transitively
  gated on those two backends) meant Caddy itself never started, so `app.localhost`/`id.localhost`
  were never reachable and Playwright never launched. Case B was `skipped` once Case A failed (same
  workflow, sequential steps). This is consistent with `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s own header
  comment — already on record before this ticket — that full-stack boot is a documented
  ~50-minute-plus manual/fresh-VM procedure, not something asserted to complete on a shared runner.
  No code defect was found in the boot path during this investigation; the constraint appears to be
  real compute/time capacity on the GitHub-hosted runner, not a logic bug in either the reference
  connector or this ticket's own code.

### Deliberately not attempted

- No workaround (e.g., a qualification-only Caddy override that skips the OpenMRS/OpenELIS
  dependency chain) was built. Rejected: it would test a topology that diverges from the real
  deployment's `depends_on`/healthcheck contract in two places, undermining the exact thing real
  qualification is for. The dependency chain Caddy requiring the full clinical stack to boot is a
  real, accurate fact about this repository's architecture, not an artificial obstacle to route

- No retry beyond the one full run was attempted in this session, given each cycle costs 30-70+
  minutes of CI wall-clock time and the blocker is a capacity constraint a retry with the same runner
  would not resolve.

### Qualification actually run and passing, local + CI

- Adapter: full suite unchanged from DH-CLINIC-004A (855 passed, 98 skipped) — no adapter code

- `git diff --check` clean at the final commit. Fast CI (`origin/master`) green at every pushed

- Real-Keycloak reconciliation: qualified (above). Real-browser E2E: **not** qualified — built,

## DH-IDENTITY-001 (2026-09-17) — provider-scoped native Patient directory contract

**Starting master SHA:** `0ed86b8d85ade6a260ec27c49395032ebafb9210` (DH-CLINIC-004B's own final
documentation commit, confirmed via `git status`/`git fetch` before starting). **No branch, no
PR** — per this ticket's own explicit instruction, identical to DH-CLINIC-004B's workflow. **Does
not touch, does not runtime-qualify, and does not change DH-CLINIC-004B's own open item** — that
ticket remains exactly as open as its own entry above states.

**Objective and scope.** `PatientReference` (DH-EX-001) was deliberately designed as an exact
source-identity/provenance binding, never a patient record — but native DHealth Clinic had grown to
treat a browser-generated UUID bound through it as a de facto patient identity. This ticket
establishes the correct underlying model before DH-CLINIC-005 builds wrong-patient-safe human
identity UX on top of it: a real, provider-scoped `Patient` directory, `PatientReference` restored
to its original exact-provenance meaning (now explicitly linked *to* a Patient), zero fuzzy/
demographic matching anywhere, and 1:1 backfill of every existing reference. Full decision record:
`DECISIONS.md` ADR-051.

**What was built:**

- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/models.py`**: new `Patient` (`exchange_patients` —
  `provider_organization_id`, nullable `display_name`/`date_of_birth`/paired contact, composite
  `UniqueConstraint(id, provider_organization_id)` so `PatientReference` can target it with a
  composite FK) and `PatientRegistrationRequest` (`exchange_patient_registration_requests` — the
  immutable idempotency/replay fingerprint record). `PatientReference` gains a NOT NULL
  `patient_id` plus a composite `ForeignKeyConstraint(["patient_id", "source_organization_id"],
  ["exchange_patients.id", "exchange_patients.provider_organization_id"])` — the database-enforced
  guarantee a reference can never point at a Patient belonging to a different provider than the
  reference's own `source_organization_id` (§8). `ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent`'s `event_type`/
  `resource_type` CHECK constraints widened for `patient_created`/`patient`.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/identity.py`**: `PatientReferenceRepository.get_or_create`/
  `get_or_create_with_outcome` now also create the linked `Patient` atomically, in the same
  SAVEPOINT as the reference — a brand-new exact identity gets its own new 1:1 Patient; an existing
  one returns its already-linked Patient unchanged (the legacy endpoint's §36 compatibility rule,
  baked into the repository so it is a structural invariant, not a convention 45 call sites could
  each get wrong). `organizations: OrganizationRepository | None = None` added as an *optional*
  constructor param (defense-in-depth `require_type(PROVIDER)` check) rather than required, to
  avoid a breaking constructor-signature edit across ~45 pre-existing call sites that already only
  ever pass a PROVIDER organization — real HTTP call paths already enforce this via
  `_require_clinician` regardless.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/patients.py`** (new): `PatientRepository` — the native
  registration path. `create()` atomically inserts Patient + native PatientReference
  (`source_system="dhealth"`, `source_identity_system="urn:dhealth:patient-id"`,
  `source_identity_value=str(patient.id)` — deliberately not `"dhealth-clinic"`, so a future
  DHealth Lab frontend shares the identical namespace) + registration-request row, in one SAVEPOINT.
  Idempotency: exact replay (same provider + key + canonical fingerprint) returns the same Patient
  unchanged; a conflicting replay raises `PatientRegistrationConflict` (409). Fingerprint is a
  SHA-256 digest over a fixed, deterministically-canonicalized field tuple
  (`json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"))`), computed identically at creation and
  replay time — never Python's process-randomized `hash()`. `list_for_organization`'s search uses a
  correlated scalar subquery (not a JOIN) for the "primary reference" match, so a Patient can never
  appear twice in a result regardless of how many references it has (D8) — no de-duplication logic
  needed because the query cannot produce a duplicate row.
- **`adapter/migrations/versions/0022_exchange_patient_directory.py`**: creates both new tables;
  backfills 1:1 (`INSERT INTO exchange_patients SELECT id, source_organization_id, ... FROM
  exchange_patient_references` — reusing the reference's own id as its Patient's id, a one-time
  backfill convenience, not a general invariant; then `UPDATE exchange_patient_references SET
  patient_id = id`); widens the two CHECK constraints (`0012`'s exact drop/recreate pattern). A
  §11 safety guard runs first and refuses (before any DDL) if any existing reference's
  `source_organization_id` resolves to a non-PROVIDER or missing organization. Downgrade refuses if
  any native registration-request row exists or any Patient carries a recorded `date_of_birth` —
  the two signals that distinguish genuinely new, non-backfill-equivalent data from a
  legacy-bind-created Patient (which is, by construction, a byte-for-byte duplicate of its own
  reference's existing snapshot, safe to drop). CI's `EXPECTED_HEAD` bumped to
  `0022_exchange_patient_directory` in the same commit as the migration.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`**: `PatientCreateRequest`/`PatientDirectoryEntry`/
  `PatientSearchRequest` Pydantic models (durable product naming, not `ClinicPatientSummary` — §22);
  `POST /organizations/{provider_id}/patients` (idempotent create, reuses the existing
  `_require_idempotency_key` canonical-UUIDv4 dependency), `GET .../patients`, `POST
  .../patients/search`, `GET .../patients/{patient_id}`, `GET
  .../patient-registrations/{idempotency_key}` (§19 recovery). All gated by the existing
  `_require_clinician` authorization (PROVIDER + ACTIVE CLINICIAN membership; a LAB org member is
  refused regardless of role, since CLINICIAN is not an assignable LAB role). Atomic
  Patient+reference+registration+`patient_created` audit commit, mirroring `create_lab_order`'s own
  transaction discipline exactly.
- **`adapter/tests/test_exchange_patients_api.py`** (new, 35 tests): P1-P12 (creation/authorization),
  I1-I8 (idempotency, including I6's explicit proof that identical demographics under a new key
  create a second Patient), D1-D11 (directory/tenancy/search/anti-enumeration), plus registration-
  recovery and audit tests.
- **`adapter/tests/test_exchange_patient_references_api.py`** (+6 tests, L1-L6): the legacy
  exact-identity bind endpoint's new Patient-linkage behavior under the updated model — L4 in
  particular proves the no-fuzzy-matching law applies to the legacy path too (two different exact
  source identities with byte-identical demographics never auto-link). One pre-existing test
  (`test_patient_list_uses_uuid_tie_break_for_equal_created_at`) that directly constructed
  `PatientReference` ORM rows (bypassing the repository) was updated to also construct the now-
  required linked `Patient` row, using the same id-reuse technique the migration itself uses.
- **`adapter/tests/integration/test_dhidentity001_postgres_qualification.py`** (new, CI-wired
  into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s adapter job, `DHIDENTITY001_PG_*` env vars, immediately after
  the existing DH-CLINIC-003C Postgres step): PG1-PG8 (10 concurrent identical registrations →
  exactly one Patient/reference/registration-request; concurrent conflicting payload → exactly one
  created, one conflict, zero orphans) and a direct real-database proof that the composite FK
  rejects a cross-provider PatientReference→Patient link (`IntegrityError`) — SQLite does not
  enforce foreign keys by default, so this claim rests on this real-Postgres run, not the SQLite
  unit suite.
- **`adapter/scripts/qualify_dh_identity_001_migration.py`** (new, CI-wired as its own step
  immediately before the existing "Migration history reaches head" step, same disposable Postgres
  service): seeds legacy `PatientReference` rows (5 across provider A including 2 with identical
  `display_name`, 1 with no snapshot at all; 1 more on provider B reusing provider A's exact raw
  `source_identity_value`) at revision `0021`, upgrades to `0022`, and asserts M2 (every legacy
  reference linked), M3 (the 2 identical-demographic references produced 2 distinct Patients), M4
  (the cross-provider raw-value collision produced 2 distinct Patients), M5 (no fabricated
  `display_name`/DOB), M6 (every backfilled Patient's `provider_organization_id` matches its own
  reference's `source_organization_id`) — 6 legacy references used in total. M1 is implicit (the
  upgrade starts from an empty database); M7 is covered by the adjacent, pre-existing "reaches
  head" CI step, which runs immediately after. Also exercises §41's downgrade guard end-to-end:
  creates one native Patient with a recorded DOB, asserts `alembic downgrade` past `0022` raises
  the specific refusal and leaves the schema unchanged.
- **UI (`ui/src/`)**: `exchangeTypes.ts` gains `PatientDirectoryEntry`/`PatientCreateRequest`/
  `PatientCreateOutcome`; `exchangeClient.ts` gains `createPatientWithOutcome`/`listPatients`/
  `searchPatients`/`getPatient`/`getPatientRegistration` (the legacy `bindPatientReference*`/
  `listPatientReferences`/`getPatientReference` methods are unchanged and still exist — the last
  is still used by Clinic's own Phase-B confirmation-read step, unchanged). `ClinicPatientsPage.tsx`
  migrated its create/list/search calls to the new directory API behind one explicit compatibility-
  bridge conversion, `toClinicPatientSummary()` (§33) — every existing order/results code path in
  that same file, already built against `ClinicPatientSummary`, needed zero further change.
  `pendingPatientStorage.ts` rewritten (`v1` → `v2` storage-key prefix, deliberately not
  reinterpreting old-shape entries under the new schema): the persisted recovery record now carries
  an opaque `idempotency_key` (plus, once confirmed, `confirmed_patient_id`/
  `confirmed_patient_reference_id`) and never any demographic field — the browser no longer mints a
  patient identity (`crypto.randomUUID()` remains, but only as a request identity). Ambiguous-POST
  recovery on reload now resolves through the new §19 `getPatientRegistration` lookup when no
  confirmation was ever observed, and through the existing `getPatientReference` lookup once one
  was.

**Deliberately not built (out of scope, per the ticket's own explicit instruction):**

- No patient merge/link API, no fuzzy/demographic matching, no duplicate scoring, anywhere.
- No national/cross-provider MPI, no government identifier integration, no biometric matching.
- No `Patient` demographic update API (`PATCH`/`PUT`) — correction semantics need their own
  audit/versioning decision, not silently added here.
- No Orders/Results page redesign — DH-CLINIC-005's explicit job, not combined into this ticket.
- No sex/gender/race/nationality/religion/address/marital-status/diagnosis/medication/insurance
  fields — identity architecture only, not a step toward a full EMR demographic record.

**Qualification, all run locally before each commit:**

- Adapter: full suite — **896 passed, 101 skipped** (855 pre-existing + 35 new
  `test_exchange_patients_api.py` + 6 new L-series legacy-compatibility tests; 3 new Postgres-only
  tests correctly skipped without `DHIDENTITY001_PG_*` set locally -- they run for real in CI, see
  below). `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean across `src`/`tests`/`migrations`/`scripts`.
- UI: `tsc -b --noEmit` clean project-wide; `oxlint` **0 errors** (3 pre-existing warnings, all in

  worker-process pool intermittently times out starting a handful of unrelated files across the

  Four local full-suite attempts were made; every test that did start passed (290/290, then
  352/352, then 302/302, then 365/365 -- zero real assertion failures in any attempt, only
  worker-spawn timeouts). **This is a local-sandbox limitation only, not a CI one**: CI's own
  `ui-frontend` job runs on a clean GitHub-hosted runner and its `Vitest` step passed in full, in

- `git diff --check` clean.
- **Push-triggered CI, both runs on `origin/master`, all 9 jobs green:** run `35250365891`
  (commit `902c27f`) failed only on `Ruff format` inside the `adapter` job (one file needed

**Human Decision Required: NO.** Every architectural choice was already scoped by this ticket's own

**Addendum, 2026-09-17, found during DH-CLINIC-005's own adversarial self-review (not this

## DH-CLINIC-005 (2026-09-17) — wrong-patient-safe human identity UX

**Starting master SHA:** `4c55f0418b09c11f85ccbddfbbecf7c36bd9e583` (DH-IDENTITY-001's own final
documentation commit, including its addendum above). **No branch, no PR** — this ticket's own
explicit instruction. **Does not touch, does not runtime-qualify, and does not change
DH-CLINIC-004B's own open item** — unchanged by this ticket, exactly as its own entry states.

**Objective and scope.** DH-IDENTITY-001 built the correct backend identity model (`Patient`
directory vs. `PatientReference` provenance); Native Clinic's Orders and Results screens had not
yet been migrated to use it, and still identified patients to a human by a truncated UUID fragment
(`Réf. Patient: af2b64d1…`) — a real wrong-patient-selection risk in a clinical ordering/results
workflow, not cosmetic. This ticket makes the provider `Patient` directory the human-facing identity
source everywhere a clinician acts on a specific patient, without touching `LabOrder`'s own identity
semantics, without adding fuzzy matching, and without any schema migration.

**What was built — backend (commit `9fc288d`, N+1 proof `0224a9b`):**

- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/patients.py`**: `PatientIdentitySummaryRecord`
  (`patient_id`/`display_name`/`date_of_birth`/`contact_channel_type`/`contact_value` — nothing
  else, deliberately distinct from `PatientRecord`/`PatientDirectoryEntry`'s directory-specific
  fields) and `PatientIdentityIntegrityError`. `PatientRepository.get_identity_summaries_for_references`
  resolves a batch of `PatientReference.id`s to their linked `Patient` identity in one query
  (`JOIN` on `PatientReference.patient_id == Patient.id`, filtered by both
  `PatientReference.source_organization_id` and `Patient.provider_organization_id` against the
  caller's own provider — the same tenant check the composite FK already enforces at the database
  level, re-asserted at this read layer) — never one query per row. A single-reference convenience
  wrapper (`get_identity_summary_for_reference`) backs the detail/results routes.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`**: new `PatientIdentitySummaryResponse` embedded
  (as `patient`) in `LabOrderResponse`, `LabOrderSummaryResponse`, `ProviderOrderResultsResponse`,
  and `ProviderReleaseVersionContentResponse` — all four additive, `patient_reference_id` and every
  existing field unchanged. Two closures (`_require_patient_identity`/`_require_patient_identities`)
  resolve identity after `_require_clinician` and after the tenant 404 check, raising
  `PatientIdentityIntegrityError` (an unhandled exception → 500) rather than ever returning
  `patient=None` for a reference whose linked Patient cannot be resolved — structurally prevented by
  DH-IDENTITY-001's own composite tenant FK, but checked again here since SQLite (the unit-test
  database) does not enforce that FK by default.
- Tests: OI1-OI8 (`test_exchange_orders_api.py`) and RI1-RI6, folded into 4 test functions
  (`test_exchange_results_api.py`) — OI2/RI3 prove the source is the live `Patient` directory, not
  the `PatientReference` snapshot, by constructing mismatched rows directly at the ORM layer (the
  repository's own `get_or_create` always keeps them in sync, so this is the only way to
  distinguish which one the API actually reads). A dedicated test constructs a `PatientReference`
  with a dangling `patient_id` (again only possible because SQLite doesn't enforce the composite FK)
  and proves both the list and detail routes raise `PatientIdentityIntegrityError` rather than
  rendering `patient=None`. A separate test counts actual SQL `SELECT` statements for a 5-order list
  vs. a 1-order list and asserts they're equal, proving the batched resolution is not N+1.
- **No migration.** All four response fields are purely additive; `EXPECTED_HEAD` in
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` stays at `0022_exchange_patient_directory`.

**What was built — frontend (commit `e2e2e53`):**

- **`ui/src/features/clinic/components/PatientIdentity.tsx`** (+ `patientIdentityFormat.ts`, its
  own `.module.css`): the one shared presentation of human patient identity across Patients, Orders,
  and Results. `compact` variant (list/table rows): name, then DOB/contact/limited-identity as small
  secondary lines, no technical identifier at all. `full` variant (workspace header, order review,
  order confirmation, result-detail banner): the same fields more prominent, plus the complete
  (never truncated) technical `Patient` id as a de-emphasized "Réf. DHealth" fallback line. Missing
  name renders `Nom non renseigné`, never blank space and never the raw technical id. Missing
  DOB/contact are simply omitted — never fabricated, never a defaulted January 1. A patient with
  only a name gets a truthful, non-blocking `Identité limitée — vérifiez le patient avant de
  continuer.` notice; care is never blocked on it. Two patients with byte-identical demographics
  render as two separate DOM nodes (`data-patient-id`-keyed), proven by `PI10`/`OU7`. Nothing is
  conveyed by color alone.
- **`formatDateOfBirth`**: a pure string transform on the `"YYYY-MM-DD"` value — splits the string,
  indexes a French month-name array, never constructs a `Date` object. `PI3` proves specific
  UTC-boundary dates (`1990-01-01`, `2000-12-31`) render the identical calendar day regardless of
  environment — the exact class of bug `new Date(dob).toLocaleDateString(...)` is vulnerable to in a
  viewer west of UTC.
- **`ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts`**: new `PatientIdentitySummary` type, embedded as `patient` on
  `LabOrderSummary`/`LabOrder`/`ProviderOrderResultsResponse`/`ProviderReleaseVersionContentResponse`
  — mirrors the backend response shapes exactly.
- **`ClinicOrdersPage.tsx`/`ClinicResultsPage.tsx`**: Patient is now the first table column
  (rendered via `<PatientIdentity>`); the order's own technical id remains visible as a small,
  de-emphasized, right-aligned secondary column (`Référence de l'ordre`), never removed (§37
  additive-compatibility instruction).
- **`ClinicResultsPage.tsx` — a real, previously-untested async race, found and fixed.** The
  pre-existing `handleSelectOrder` started two requests (`getOrderResults`/`getReleaseVersions`) with
  no binding to the current selection, provider, or mount state — selecting a different order while
  an earlier one was still in flight could let the earlier response's stale content silently
  overwrite the current one once it resolved late. Both requests now resolve into one atomic
  `detail` state object, gated by a monotonic generation counter bumped on every new selection and
  on every provider switch, a `currentProviderRef`, and a `mountedRef` — a response updates state
  only if the generation, provider, and mount state it was issued under all still hold. The
  response's own `order_id`/release-history `order_id`/`patient.patient_id` are additionally cross-
  checked against what was actually requested and against the clicked list row's own patient
  identity; any disagreement fails closed to one fixed, generic French string
  (`Impossible de vérifier de manière sûre le résultat demandé.`) that never names an order or
  patient identifier, never a per-case message. The page's list/detail layout was restructured
  (list always visible, detail panel below it, rows stay clickable while a detail is loading) so
  this race is reachable through the actual rendered UI, not only through directly-invoked
  callbacks — a second `Consulter` click while the first is still loading is now an ordinary
  interaction, not something the UI physically prevented. 7 mandatory tests (RR1: out-of-order
  resolution: `select A, select B, resolve B then A late → only B renders`; RR2: a late failure
  from A cannot replace B's success; RR3: a late success from A cannot replace B's truthful error;
  RR4: a stale response from Provider A cannot render after switching to Provider B; RR5/RR6:
  mismatched `order_id` in either response fails closed; RR7: a response after unmount produces no
  state update) plus RS1-RS6 cover this in `ClinicResultsPage.test.tsx` (new, this page previously
  had zero test coverage).
- **`ClinicPatientsPage.tsx` — AC4, full `PatientDirectoryEntry` migration.** The
  `toClinicPatientSummary` DH-IDENTITY-001-era compatibility bridge and its `patientLabel()` helper
  are both removed; `results`/`selected` state, and every function that reads them, now operate on
  `PatientDirectoryEntry` directly. Both confirmed-patient reads (`handleCreate`'s Phase B, and the
  mount-recovery effect's confirmed branch) now call `client.getPatient(providerId, patient_id)`
  instead of the legacy `client.getPatientReference(providerId, patient_reference_id)` — the latter
  cannot represent DOB/`provider_organization_id`/`created_at` at all, so it could never have been
  kept as the native workspace's own read source. **§14 durable-identity discipline, verified, not
  merely asserted:** `currentPatientRef`, `orderScopeKey`, `loadPatientOrders`, the DH-CLINIC-003C
  intent-recovery mismatch check, and the order-creation request body itself all stay keyed on
  `primary_patient_reference_id` (renamed from `patient_reference_id`, same underlying value) — none
  were rekeyed to `patient_id`. 003C's own full existing recovery test suite (persist-before-POST,

## DH-CLINIC-006 (2026-09-18) — Provider-assigned laboratory workflow

**Starting master SHA:** `741af6423a9725d038e2ea5cc0025e44044e6379` (DH-CLINIC-005's own final
documentation commit). **No branch, no PR** — this ticket's own explicit instruction. **Does not
touch, does not runtime-qualify, and does not change DH-CLINIC-004B's own open item** — unchanged
by this ticket. **Does not claim ADR-043 Law 2 ("no double entry") is solved** — this ticket proves
DHealth-side routing to a DHealth lab *organization* only, never that any real lab staff system
received the order; that remains DH-PILOT-TOPOLOGY-001's own future choice.

**Objective and scope.** DH-EX-010 built `LabSelectionRepository.assign_by_provider` — ADR-043's
pre-authorized launch option (a) — but never answered "which labs is a given provider actually
configured to work with?" Without an explicit answer, the only concept already in the codebase that
could plausibly fill that gap is `LabDirectoryProfile.listed`, the public marketplace-visibility
flag — reaching for it would silently turn provider routing into marketplace browsing, exactly what
ADR-043 Law 1 forbids. This ticket introduces `ProviderLabRoute`, the missing routing-authority
concept, and wires the Clinic frontend to it end to end, without rebuilding or weakening anything
`assign_by_provider`/`LabSelectionRepository` already did.

**What was built — backend, commit 1 `c096cca` (model/migration/CI), commit 2 `c48a7e5`
(enforcement/API/tests), fix commits `1b354f0`/`efb628c` (CI-found migration-revision-id and
qualification-script fixes):**

- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/provider_lab_routes.py`** (new): `ProviderLabRouteRepository`
  — idempotent `upsert` (unique on `(provider_organization_id, lab_organization_id)`,
  IntegrityError-as-race-retry, mirroring `LabDirectoryProfileRepository`'s own pattern),
  organization-type enforcement at the repository layer (`InvalidProviderLabRouteOrganizationType`;
  deliberately does *not* also require ACTIVE status, so a route to a since-deactivated lab can
  still be read/deactivated, never permanently stuck), `list_for_provider` (the provider's own
  directory read), and `find_whole_order_eligible_labs` — a three-pass narrowing read mirroring
  `catalog.find_whole_order_eligible_labs` exactly, but keyed on `ProviderLabRoute.active` instead
  of `listed`, and with **no `LabPrice` join anywhere**. Deliberately does not force `REPEATABLE
  READ` (unlike the marketplace version) — this read is advisory UI data only; `assign_by_provider`
  is the sole authoritative re-check under its own row lock.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/models.py`**: new `ProviderLabRoute` model
  (`exchange_provider_lab_routes`), widened `ExchangeSecurityAuditEvent` CHECK constraints for
  `provider_lab_route_created`/`provider_lab_route_updated`/`provider_lab_route`.
  **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/security_audit.py`**: matching `SecurityEventType`/
  `SecurityResourceType` Literal additions.
- **Migration `0023_provider_lab_routes`** (renamed from an initial `0023_exchange_provider_lab_routes`
  after CI caught it exceeding Alembic's default 32-character `version_num` column — see "Errors
  found and fixed" below): new table, widened CHECK constraints, downgrade guard refusing to drop
  the table while any route row exists. `EXPECTED_HEAD` bumped in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/selection.py`**: `assign_by_provider` now checks for an
  active `ProviderLabRoute` *inside its own locked mutation*, first among the fresh eligibility
  re-checks (before the org/profile/offering checks), raising the new `ProviderLabRouteNotActive`
  — so a future caller bypassing HTTP cannot skip the routing boundary, and the check is
  serialized against a concurrent same-order assignment by the `LabOrder` row lock already held
  (it does genuinely race a concurrent route *deactivation*, since that takes its own separate lock
  on the route row — see PG5 below for why that race is benign). New `LabAssignmentSummaryRecord` +
  `get_assignment_summaries_for_orders`/`get_assignment_summary_for_order` (batched, N+1-safe,
  joined straight to `Organization` for the lab's current display name) + `LabAssignmentIntegrityError`
  + `STATUSES_REQUIRING_LAB_SELECTION` (`SELECTED`/`ACCEPTED`/`IN_PROGRESS`/`COMPLETED` — the
  statuses only reachable via SELECTED, which both `select()` and `assign_by_provider()` always
  write in the same flush as the `LabSelection` row itself; `REJECTED`/`CANCELLED` are deliberately
  excluded since they're reachable *directly* from `AWAITING_LAB_SELECTION` with no prior routing).
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`**: new `PUT /organizations/{provider_id}/lab-routes/{lab_id}`
  (platform-admin only via `authz.require_platform_admin`, never `_require_org_admin` — a route
  spans two organizations and needs neutral platform authority; idempotent, audited including an
  `"unchanged"` outcome on a true no-op replay, mirroring `put_directory_profile`'s own convention
  rather than `assign_lab_to_order`'s different idempotent-mutation-suppression one); new
  `GET /organizations/{provider_id}/lab-routes` (CLINICIAN minimum, same gate as `assign_lab_to_order`);
  new `GET /organizations/{provider_id}/orders/{order_id}/eligible-labs` (CLINICIAN, order id alone
  determines the required test set, anti-enumerating — cross-provider order id is 404, same as every
  other provider-scoped order read). `LabOrderResponse`/`LabOrderSummaryResponse` gained
  `lab_assignment`, resolved via new `_lab_assignment_for_order`/`_lab_assignments_for_orders`
  closures at all 6 order-returning call sites — resolved from the canonical `LabSelection`
  *whenever one exists*, regardless of the order's current status (so a SELECTED-then-REJECTED
  order still truthfully shows the lab that rejected it), and raising `LabAssignmentIntegrityError`
  only when a status in `STATUSES_REQUIRING_LAB_SELECTION` has none.
- **Tests**: `test_exchange_provider_lab_routes.py` (new, 21: R1-R7 route CRUD/type-enforcement/

**What was built — frontend, commit 3 `3975c9b`:**

**Errors found and fixed during this ticket (all before any commit landed, or caught by CI and
fixed in a same-day follow-up commit — see the advisor-review discipline this session used):**

1. **`PUT lab-routes` returned an unhandled 500 for a nonexistent organization** — the repository's
   `_require_org_type` calls `organizations.get()`, which raises `OrganizationNotFound`, but the
   route handler only caught `InvalidProviderLabRouteOrganizationType`. Fixed: `OrganizationNotFound`
   → 404, with 2 new tests.
2. **`lab_assignment` was initially hidden for a REJECTED/CANCELLED order that *was* routed before
   closing** — the first implementation skipped resolution entirely outside
   `STATUSES_REQUIRING_LAB_SELECTION`, which would have rendered "Non attribué" for a
   SELECTED-then-REJECTED order even though its `LabSelection` is real and the clinician needs to
   see which lab rejected it. Fixed: always resolve from `LabSelection` when one exists; the
   integrity-error fail-closed path applies only when a status that structurally requires one is
   missing it.
3. **Frontend `LabAssignmentResponse` type initially claimed a `lab_organization_name` field the
   backend response doesn't have** — load-bearing for §30 (never render a lab name from the assign
   response itself). Fixed to the exact 3 fields the backend actually returns.
4. **A code comment overclaimed the route-deactivation-race check as "never racing" a concurrent
   deactivation** — it does genuinely race (the `LabOrder` row lock does not serialize against
   `ProviderLabRouteRepository.upsert`'s own separate lock on the route row); what makes the race
   *benign* is PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED handing the read a consistent, genuinely-committed view
   either way. Fixed the comment in `selection.py` and the PG5 test's own docstring to state the
   true, weaker, still-sufficient guarantee.
5. **Migration revision id too long for Alembic's own bookkeeping** — CI's real-PostgreSQL run (not
   any local/SQLite test) caught `0023_exchange_provider_lab_routes` (33 characters) exceeding
   Alembic's default `alembic_version.version_num` `VARCHAR(32)` column, failing the migration's own
   `UPDATE alembic_version SET version_num=...` bookkeeping statement before any of this migration's
   actual DDL mattered. Fixed by renaming to `0023_provider_lab_routes` (24 characters) throughout
   (filename, `revision` string, `EXPECTED_HEAD`, the PG-qualification test's docstring) — commit
   `1b354f0`.
6. **DH-IDENTITY-001's own pre-existing downgrade-guard qualification script broke against the new,
   moved head** — caught by the *next* CI run. `qualify_dh_identity_001_migration.py` upgrades to
   "head" (now 0023, one migration past what it was written against) then calls
   `command.downgrade(cfg, "0021_order_intent_ownership")` in one step, expecting 0022's own guard
   to refuse and leave the schema at 0022. Alembic wraps a multi-revision downgrade in one
   transaction (this repo's `env.py` never sets `transaction_per_migration`), so when 0022→0021
   correctly refused, the already-successful 0023→0022 step in the *same* transaction rolled back
   too, leaving the schema at 0023 — failing the script's own post-refusal assertion for a reason
   unrelated to either migration's correctness. Fixed by explicitly downgrading 0023→0022 first (its
   own separate transaction, expected to succeed cleanly) before attempting the 0022→0021 refusal
   the script actually exists to prove — commit `efb628c`. **This is the durable lesson for the
   next ticket that adds a migration**: any pre-existing qualification script that upgrades to
   `"head"` and then targets a downgrade destination *older* than the previous head must isolate
   the newest migration's own downgrade first, or a correct refusal deeper in the chain will roll
   back an unrelated, already-successful step in the same transaction.

## DH-CLINIC-007 (2026-09-18) — Released-result review + follow-up UX

**Starting master SHA:** `791d8c74c54e117513db8848884395e5cba262e6` (DH-CLINIC-006's own final
documentation commit) — confirmed exact match at session start. **No branch, no PR** — this
ticket's own explicit instruction. **Does not touch, does not runtime-qualify, and does not change
DH-CLINIC-004B's own open item** — unchanged by this ticket. **Does not resolve `ResultDelivery`'s
own separate, unrelated state machine** — that remains untouched and unresolved.

**Objective and scope.** DHealth already had the exact-version review contract from
DH-EX-014A/014B/ADR-048 (immutable release-version manifests, versioned `DoctorReview`, exact-version
review mutations, explicit-version-required once an amendment exists) — but Native Clinic had no
operational UI for it: no way to see which results were waiting for review, no way to load a
specific historical version's exact content before reviewing it, and no review disposition control
anywhere in the frontend. This ticket is **not** a new clinical state machine — the three existing
`DoctorReview` statuses (`PENDING`/`NO_FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED`/`FOLLOW_UP_REQUIRED`) remain the only
ones; it exposes the existing state machine operationally.

**What was built — backend, commit 1 `e62dc0e`:**

- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/results.py`**: new `ReviewQueueEntryRecord` dataclass and
  `DoctorReviewRepository.list_queue_for_provider` — a single joined query (`DoctorReview` join
  `LabOrder`, outer-join `LabResultReleaseVersion`), one row per outstanding review *obligation*,
  never one per order (an order with two independently-pending amendment versions surfaces as two
  entries). Deliberately gated on `LabOrder.status == COMPLETED`, not merely `DoctorReview.status`
  — a `DoctorReview` row is created `PENDING` in the same transaction as `LabOrder` creation itself,
  long before any result exists; omitting this gate would have wrongly surfaced every in-progress
  order as needing review. Ordered by workflow age (`release_version.created_at` coalesced to
  `order.created_at`, ascending) — explicitly never by clinical urgency/abnormality.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`**: new `GET
  /organizations/{provider_id}/result-reviews` (CLINICIAN minimum, provider-scoped, `status`
  query param defaulting to `PENDING`/`ALL`/either terminal value, `limit`), reusing
  DH-CLINIC-005's own `_require_patient_identities` batched closure for N+1-safe patient
  resolution. Response carries `legacy_unversioned: bool` explicitly for the one grandfathered
  shape, rather than requiring the caller to infer it from three simultaneous `null`s. No new
  Pydantic model reuses raw UUIDs as a primary reviewer identity anywhere.
- **Tests**: `test_exchange_results.py` gained 8 repository-level tests (Q1/Q2/Q4/Q5/Q6/Q7/Q10/Q11/
  §14 ordering); `test_exchange_results_api.py` gained 8 API-level tests (default-pending-shows,
  in-progress-absent, status=ALL reveals finalized, two-pending-versions-are-two-entries,
  provider/lab-role isolation, patient-identity-from-directory, and an N+1-count regression test
  mirroring DH-CLINIC-005's own `before_cursor_execute` SQL-counting pattern). No migration —
  `EXPECTED_HEAD` unchanged at `0023_provider_lab_routes`; the entire backend contract this queue
  reads from already existed.

**What was built — frontend, commits 2 `f06737d` (client/types) and 3 `a9069b9` (page rewrite):**

- **`ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts`/`exchangeClient.ts`**: `DoctorReviewResponse`,
  `ProviderResultReviewQueueEntry`/`Response`, `ReviewQueueStatusFilter`; client methods
  `listResultReviews`, `getReleaseVersion`, `reviewReleaseVersionNoFollowUp`/`FollowUp`,
  `reviewLegacyOrderNoFollowUp`/`FollowUp` — six distinct methods, never a single generic
  `review(status: string)` that would blur the version-specific/legacy distinction. Unit tests
  added to `exchangeClient.test.ts` for each.
- **`ui/src/features/clinic/pages/ClinicResultsPage.tsx`** (full rewrite): sources both the
  pending-review queue and the reviewed-history section from `listResultReviews(status='ALL')`,
  split client-side by `review_status` — the legacy `listOrders`-based list this replaces had no
  review-status field for legacy orders at all, so this redesign closes that gap for free rather
  than adding a new backend field. Key behaviors:
  - Prominent "Résultats à examiner (N)" count; a reviewed result stays discoverable in "Historique"
    — the queue going to zero never means a record becomes inaccessible.
  - A version-history strip per order, sourced from `getReleaseVersions`; amended versions are
    labelled textually ("Version N — Amendée"), never by color/icon/position alone.
  - Exact-version content (`getReleaseVersion`) is always fetched and identity-cross-validated
    (order id, version id, patient id) before any review disposition control is offered — history
    metadata alone never suffices. A genuinely legacy/unversioned order (empty version history)
    falls back to the legacy read (`getOrderResults`) and legacy review routes, labelled "Résultat
    historique — aucune version de libération enregistrée."
  - **Panel state model**: `initializing` (first load only) vs. `contentLoading` (fetching one
    version's content) are tracked separately from a persisted `patient`/`versions` pair, so a
    version switch or a post-mutation recheck never makes the patient banner or version strip
    disappear mid-operation — only the content area itself shows a transient
    "Chargement de la version…"/"Vérification de l'état de la revue…" message. (This split was not
    the first design — see "Errors found and fixed" below.)
  - Exactly two review dispositions ("Aucun suivi requis"/"Suivi requis"), never a third; selecting
    one discloses both the immutability of the decision and, for follow-up, the truthful scope
    limit ("DHealth enregistre ici qu'un suivi est requis... ne planifie pas automatiquement un
    rendez-vous ni un contact patient").
  - Response validation before ever displaying success: `order_id`/`release_version_id`/`status`
    must all match what was requested, else fail closed and re-read authoritative state.
  - A 409 conflict or an ambiguous mutation failure never blindly retries — both re-read
    authoritative state via the same version-aware `loadPanel` path and either show the terminal
    disposition (with a truthful "already reviewed" notice) or an explicit
    "La revue n'a pas pu être confirmée" retry prompt.
  - Extends DH-CLINIC-005's generation-ref/mounted-ref/provider-ref stale-response discipline across
    the new version-switching dimension.
- **`ClinicApp.test.tsx`/`ClinicA11y.test.tsx`**: their mock `ExchangeClient`s predated
  `listResultReviews`/`getReleaseVersion` and would otherwise throw `TypeError` on render — updated
  to the new contract shape (a PENDING queue entry, matching `getReleaseVersion`/`getReleaseVersions`
  responses), and the golden-flow test's click target changed from "Consulter" to "Examiner" to
  match the new pending-entry action label.
- **`ClinicResultsPage.test.tsx`**: fully rewritten (22 tests) against the new architecture —
  UI-Q1-Q4 (queue count/history-split/two-pending-versions/legacy-labelling), UI-V1-V5 (exact-version
  loading, version switching, response-mismatch fail-closed ×2, legacy fallback), UI-R1-R8 (two
  choices only, confirm-gated-on-selection, disclosure copy, version-specific-not-legacy routing,
  success/terminal display, 409-conflict-shows-authoritative-outcome, ambiguous-failure-rechecks,
  status-mismatch-fails-closed), RR8-RR11 (independent version obligations, stale version-switch
  response discarded, stale provider-switch response discarded, unmount safety), plus a patient-
  identity-before-observation-value ordering check.

**Errors found and fixed during this ticket (all before any commit landed):**

1. **First implementation gated the entire detail panel (patient banner, version strip, content) on
   a single `loading` boolean.** Switching versions or re-checking after an ambiguous mutation
   re-fetched the full history and briefly set `loading: true`, which hid the version-strip tabs
   entirely mid-switch — a direct violation of this ticket's own §16/§35 ("the version strip must
   remain visible and interactive while switching"). Caught by the RR9 stale-version-switch test:
   after opening Version 2, clicking Version 1 (stalled) then clicking back to Version 2, the test
   could not find the Version 2 tab at all, because it had vanished. Fixed by splitting panel state
   into `initializing` (whole-panel first load) and `contentLoading` (content-area-only), with a
   persisted `patient`/`versions` pair carried across a version switch or recheck via a
   `knownVersions` fast path that skips re-fetching the version list entirely for a switch.
2. **The post-mutation recheck's own explanatory message ("déjà revue"/"n'a pas pu être confirmée")
   was rendered only inside the same conditional tree it had just caused to disappear.** The
   `.catch()` handler set `submitState.error` and immediately called `loadPanel` for the recheck,
   which set `panel.loading: true` in the same render batch — hiding the very message meant to
   explain what was happening. Caught by UI-R6/UI-R7 (`findByText` on the disclosure text timed
   out). Fixed by hoisting the `submitState.error` alert outside the loading/content conditional
   entirely, and by having `loadPanel` skip resetting `submitState`/`disposition` when called as a
   recheck (`isRecheck: true`) rather than a fresh open.
3. **Queue-list version-label text was split across sibling text nodes**, so
   `getByText(/^Version 1$/)` (an exact match) could never find it once a released-date suffix was
   appended in the same paragraph. Fixed by wrapping the version label in its own `<span>`.
4. **The review-mutation response validation initially checked only `order_id`/`release_version_id`,
   not `status`** — a response claiming success for the *wrong* disposition would have been
   displayed as success. Added the `response.status !== disposition` check per this ticket's own
   §43, with a test (UI-R8) proving the fail-closed path.
5. **`ClinicApp.test.tsx`'s and `ClinicA11y.test.tsx`'s pre-existing mock clients had no
   `listResultReviews`/`getReleaseVersion`**, since both predate this ticket — the rewritten page
   threw `TypeError: client.listResultReviews is not a function` on mount. Caught by the full
   clinic-suite regression run (not by the new page's own test file, which supplies a complete mock).
   Fixed by extending both mocks to the new contract shape.

None of the above (1-5) reached a commit before being fixed — all caught during this session's own
local qualification, before `git commit` was ever run for the affected file.

**Six more findings surfaced by an independent review after the first four commits had already
landed and been pushed — fixed in a same-session follow-up commit, honestly recorded here rather
than folded silently into the numbering above:**

6. **`reReadPanelAfterAmbiguousMutation` reused the *pre-mutation* `knownVersions` snapshot,** so a
   version's own review-status label in the tab strip stayed stale after that exact version was
   just reviewed (e.g. the tab kept saying "À examiner" while the content area correctly said "Revu
   — aucun suivi requis"). Fixed by decoupling "keep the patient banner/strip mounted during the
   fetch" (`preserveContext`) from "skip re-fetching the version list" (`knownVersions`, now used
   only by a genuine version *switch*) — a recheck always re-derives history fresh. Strengthened
   UI-R5 to assert the tab's own label updates.
7. **`GET .../result-reviews?status=ALL` alone can silently undercount the pending queue.** The
   endpoint orders oldest-first across every status and applies its `limit` after that ordering;
   with more than one page of total obligations, newer PENDING entries could fall off the page
   before older reviewed ones did. Fixed by fetching `status=PENDING` (authoritative for the
   count/queue) and `status=ALL` (for history) as two separate calls, each at the endpoint's own
   100-item cap — an accepted, disclosed limit on combined history depth, not a silent one.
8. **Switching versions or rechecking after a mutation passed `expectedPatientId: null`,**
   skipping the patient-identity cross-check §42 requires on every content load. Fixed to pass the
   already-known `panel.patient.patient_id`.
9. **A queue/history disagreement (entry says `legacy_unversioned`, but fresh version history is
   non-empty) silently rendered whichever version was "latest".** This is exactly the §5 behavior
   the whole ticket exists to forbid. Fixed to fail closed with the same generic consistency error
   used everywhere else, rather than picking a version nothing asked for.
10. **The whole-panel skeleton was gated on `queueState.loading` alone,** so every background queue
    refresh (including the one this page itself triggers right after a review mutation) briefly
    unmounted the detail panel — hiding the very "Vérification de l'état de la revue…"/"already
    reviewed" messages §71 exists to show. Fixed to show the skeleton only on a genuine first load
    (`loading && entries.length === 0`); once entries exist, a background reload never nukes the
    already-rendered panel.
11. **DH-CLINIC-005's own RS6 regression:** the rewritten queue rows dropped the secondary order-
    reference line the old list carried, leaving two orders for the same patient visually
    indistinguishable before opening either. Restored as a small monospace "Référence de l'ordre"
    line per row.
12. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s new step comment overclaimed** that PG-R1/PG-R3 were "already
    qualified by the DH-EX-014A/014B steps above" — no such CI steps exist; those two suites are
    opt-in/manual and were qualified locally this ticket, not in CI. Corrected the comment to state
    exactly what this CI run itself does and does not prove.

Also added two test gaps an independent review flagged: a legacy order's confirmed review targets
`reviewLegacyOrderNoFollowUp`, never a version-specific route (UI-V6); and a stale review-mutation
response for a since-switched-away version never touches the newly-opened version's own controls
(RR12).

**One more finding, surfaced by a second independent review pass after commit `eb9307f` (items 6-12
above) had already landed and been pushed — fixed in a second, separate follow-up commit
(`6bf571c`), not folded into `eb9307f`:**

For traceability, this ticket's full commit sequence is: `e62dc0e` (backend queue), `f06737d`
(client/types), `a9069b9` (page rewrite), `f4fbed8` (docs), `eb9307f` (fixes 1-12), `6bf571c` (fix
13 below).

13. **The provider-switch reset cleared `panel`/`disposition`/`submitState` but never `queueState`
    itself**, and `loadQueue`'s own `setQueueState` only ever sets `loading: true` without clearing
    `entries` — before finding #10 above, that was masked by the whole-panel skeleton always firing
    on `loading: true`; after fixing #10 to gate the skeleton on `loading && entries.length === 0`,
    switching providers opened a window where provider A's own patient names rendered under
    provider B's own "Résultats libérés pour :" heading until B's fetch resolved. A genuine §47/§73
    violation. Fixed by explicitly clearing `queueState` to `{ entries: [], loading: true, error:
    null }` in the same provider-switch block, so the skeleton-gate fix from #10 and this one work
    together correctly. Added RR13, which resolves provider A's queue before switching (so its
    entries are actually in state, unlike RR10's own never-resolving provider A) and asserts its
    patient name is gone immediately after switching, before provider B's own deferred fetch is
    ever resolved.

    Same review pass also flagged three smaller issues, all fixed in this same commit: (a) the two
    parallel `listResultReviews` calls in `loadQueue` could disagree if an entry flipped
    PENDING→terminal between them, landing in both halves under the same `review_id` — fixed by
    excluding from the "reviewed" half any id already present in the "pending" half, rather than
    trusting each response's own status label; (b) a queue entry legitimately missing from the
    reloaded queue (transient reload failure, or beyond the 100-item cap) rendered a fabricated-
    looking "Revue enregistrée — Non renseigné" instead of a neutral "unavailable" message with no
    controls — fixed with an explicit `null`-status branch; (c) the RS6 restoration (#11 above) had
    no test assertion — added one to UI-Q1. A fourth suggestion — disabling the version tabs while
    a submission is in flight — was tried and then reverted: it directly contradicts RR12, which
    deliberately proves that switching versions mid-submission is already safe (a stale mutation
    response for the abandoned version never touches the newly-opened one). Disabling "Fermer le
    détail" during submission was kept (no test exercises it, and closing the panel mid-submission
    would lose the outcome entirely, unlike switching versions).

## DH-LAB-001 (2026-09-18) — Native DHealth Lab shell + assigned-order queue + accept/reject

**Starting master SHA:** `e8021f5939d287c647eb10904fd565bc14b12891` (DH-CLINIC-007's own final
documentation commit) — confirmed exact match at session start; migration head confirmed
`0023_provider_lab_routes`. **No branch, no PR** — this ticket's own explicit instruction. **Does
not touch, does not runtime-qualify, and does not change DH-CLINIC-004B's own open item.**

**Critical correction carried by this ticket's own text (§0), recorded first because it reshapes
everything after it:** native DHealth Lab and DHealth Connect are not mutually exclusive product
directions to choose between — both are permanent, parallel capabilities of the same DHealth
Exchange backbone. A complete native DHealth environment (Clinic + Lab, full golden journey) is
itself a product requirement, not a stepping stone to a connector decision. DH-PILOT-TOPOLOGY-001
is accordingly no longer the immediate next ticket; it only decides which deployment model a real
target facility uses, once one exists. Full seven-point correction: `DECISIONS.md` ADR-043's
2026-09-18 dated clarification. This is an append-only correction to how the roadmap was being
read, not a rewrite of DH-CLINIC-007's own historical entry above, which stands unchanged.

**Objective and scope.** The Exchange backend has had a lab-side workflow — assigned queue, accept,
reject, and later-stage capabilities (collection, processing, result entry, completion, release,
amendments) — since DH-EX-010/011/012. None of it had ever had a DHealth Lab frontend; only direct
API access existed. This ticket builds that frontend's first slice only: authentication → lab
organization context → assigned order queue → safe order detail → accept/reject. Deliberately
excluded (per the ticket's own scope, §3/§46-49): result entry (the existing APIs are too
free-form to expose without a controlled result-definition layer — deferred to DH-LAB-003/004),
collection recording (DH-LAB-002), LIS/Connect integration, and demo seed data (DH-DEMO-001).

**What was built — backend, commit 1 `22da104`:**

- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/organizations.py`/`identity.py`**: `get_many()` added to
  `OrganizationRepository` and `PatientReferenceRepository` — batched siblings of the existing
  `get()`, never raising on a missing id.
- **`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`**: extended DH-CLINIC-005's "human-facing patient
  identity comes from `Patient`, not `PatientReference`'s own snapshot" rule (§15) to Lab. New
  `LabPatientIdentityResponse` (`patient_id`/`display_name`/`date_of_birth` — no contact fields at
  all, structurally, not merely hidden) added to `LabWorkflowOrderResponse` as a `patient` field,
  alongside the pre-existing `patient_display_name` (kept, now unused by the new frontend, for
  compatibility). New `_lab_workflow_order_responses()` batched builder: since a lab's queue can
  span **multiple** distinct ordering providers (unlike Clinic's own always-single-provider lists),
  this groups `patient_reference_id`s by `provider_organization_id` and calls the existing
  provider-scoped `_require_patient_identities()` once per distinct provider — bounded by provider
  count, not order count. Fails closed (`LabAssignmentIntegrityError`/`PatientIdentityIntegrityError`)
  on any unresolvable id, matching existing codebase convention.
- **Tests** (`test_exchange_lab_workflow.py`, +~500 lines): BI1-BI7 (patient identity sourced from
  `Patient`, including a same-name-different-identity discriminating test that directly mutates
  `Patient.display_name` via a raw session to prove divergence from `PatientReference`'s own
  snapshot; unknown DOB stays `null`, never fabricated; no contact fields anywhere in the response;
  no standalone patient route exists for Lab; cross-tenant queue isolation). BQ1/BQ2: query-count
  regression tests, precisely scoped (via `before_cursor_execute`) to only the three
  identity-related tables (`exchange_organizations`/`exchange_patients`/`exchange_patient_references`)
  — deliberately excluding an unrelated, pre-existing `LabOrder.items` lazy-relationship N+1 that
  the initial combined test draft conflated with this fix before being split apart. BQ1: query count
  does not scale with order count for a single provider. BQ2: query count scales with distinct
  provider count, not order count, for orders split across providers.

**What was built — frontend, commit 2 `520625c`, fix commit 3 `92f6791`:**

- **`ui/src/api/exchangeTypes.ts`/`exchangeClient.ts`**: `LabWorkflowPatientIdentity`,
  `LabWorkflowOrderItem`, `LabWorkflowOrder` types (reusing the existing `LabOrderStatus`); client
  methods `listLabOrders`/`getLabOrder`/`acceptLabOrder`/`rejectLabOrder` against the existing
  `GET/POST .../organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders...` routes — no new backend, no mock fallback, no
  result-entry method added.
- **`ui/src/features/lab/`** (new directory): `LabContext`/`LabProvider` mirror
  `ClinicContext`/`ClinicProvider`'s pattern — a fresh `ExchangeAuthProvider` instance wrapping Lab
  exactly as Clinic's own, per ADR-050 Decision 6, so switching apps unmounts/remounts in-memory
  token state only and never calls Keycloak logout (verified by `App.test.tsx`'s existing
  Clinic-side tests for the identical property, plus new Lab-side coverage). Lab-membership
  eligibility: ACTIVE `LAB` org + ACTIVE membership + (`LAB_TECH` or `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`, never
  both required — holding both counts as one eligible membership). A `canWorkOrders`/
  `canReleaseResults` capability model, explicitly UX-only and never weakening backend
  authorization: a releaser-only user still authenticates and selects a lab, and sees a truthful
  "not yet available" message rather than a fabricated queue (§11).
- **`LabShell.tsx`**: Accueil/Ordres tabs, active-lab display, a lab selector for multi-membership
  users, switch-to-Clinic, logout. A no-labs state renders truthfully, never blank or auto-redirect.
- **`LabHomePage.tsx`**: truthful, derivable-only counts (new/accepted/in-progress) from the same
  bounded `listLabOrders(limit:100)` read the queue uses — no invented KPI, no pricing.
- **`LabOrdersPage.tsx`** (the largest file, ~550 lines after the fix commit): the work queue and
  order-detail/accept/reject panel.
  - Information hierarchy leads with patient identity (via the new, deliberately narrower
    `LabPatientIdentity` component — cannot reuse Clinic's own, whose prop type requires contact
    fields `LabWorkflowPatientIdentity` structurally lacks) / provider / tests / status / date /
    action; the technical order reference is present but secondary, never truncated.
  - Truthful status labels distinguish `SELECTED` ("Nouvel ordre — à accepter") from `ACCEPTED`
    ("Accepté") textually, never by color alone. A default "Nouveaux" filter plus five others.
  - Order detail shows "Collection non enregistrée dans DHealth" for a null collection timestamp —
    worded to never imply collection definitely did not happen elsewhere.
  - Accept/reject are mutually exclusive in the UI, matching the backend state machine. Reject
    requires an explicit confirmation step and takes no free-text reason or reason code — rejection
    is terminal.
  - **Race/staleness discipline** — the generation-ref/mounted-ref/tenant-ref pattern
    DH-CLINIC-005/007 established, extended across the lab-switch dimension from the very first
    implementation (not a post-hoc fix, per this ticket's own explicit instruction not to repeat
    DH-CLINIC-007's "item 13" class of bug): a lab switch clears panel, mutation, confirmation, and
    queue state to empty in the **same render pass** (not merely `loading: true` on stale data,
    and not only in an effect, which would still let one paint show the old lab's data under the
    new lab's already-updated header). `runMutation`'s three-way lost-response recovery (§36/§37):
    an ambiguous accept/reject error triggers a separate authoritative `GET`, branching on whether
    the target status was actually reached (success), the order is still `SELECTED` (genuinely
    unconfirmed, retry available), or the *opposite* terminal status was reached by a concurrent
    caller (a real conflict, never mislabeled "unconfirmed"). Every response validates its own
    `order_id` against what was requested before ever being displayed, failing closed on mismatch.

**Errors found and fixed — backend:**

- A dead, broken helper (`_add_order_to_lab`, an unreachable `NotImplementedError` plus an
  undefined variable) was written and removed during self-review before running any test.
- The first combined query-count test conflated "provider count" with "order count" and measured
  every SELECT rather than only the identity-related ones, so it grew by exactly one per added
  order regardless of the batching fix — a pre-existing, unrelated `LabOrder.items` lazy-relationship
  N+1 it hadn't isolated. Diagnosed by inspecting the SQL statements' own target tables; fixed by
  splitting into BQ1/BQ2 and scoping the measurement helper to only the three identity tables.

**Errors found and fixed — frontend, independent review (`advisor()`) before push:**

- **`runMutation` had no generation guard of its own.** Accepting/rejecting order A, then
  navigating to order B before A's response (or its lost-response recheck) resolved, let A's late
  response overwrite B's now-visible panel and mutation state — exactly the class of bug §41
  requires guarding against, and one the initial implementation's own commit message claimed was
  already handled but wasn't. Fixed (fix commit `92f6791`) by capturing `panelGenerationRef`'s
  value when a mutation starts and checking it after every `await`; `handleClosePanel` now also
  bumps the ref so a mutation in flight for an already-closed panel cannot resurrect it. Covered by
  two new tests, RR5 (late accept) and RR6 (late reject), each opening order A, triggering the
  mutation, navigating to order B before it resolves, then resolving A's response and asserting
  B's panel is untouched.
- **`LabHomePage` had no lab-switch clear at all**, unlike `LabOrdersPage`. A viewer switching labs
  saw the new lab's header next to the *previous* lab's stale order counts until the new fetch
  resolved — the same stale-tenant rendering bug class DH-CLINIC-007 found, which this ticket's own
  §12 explicitly says not to repeat. Fixed with the same render-phase clear `LabOrdersPage` already
  uses. **Disclosed, not fixed:** `ClinicHomePage` has this identical latent gap (confirmed by
  inspection — no render-phase or lab/provider-switch clear exists there either); out of scope for
  this ticket, left as a candidate for a future Clinic-track fix.
- **Verified empirically, not assumed:** RR1b (queue rows clear before the new lab's fetch resolves)
  was checked against the pre-fix code by temporarily reverting the render-phase clear to a
  prev-preserving effect-phase one and re-running RR1b alone — it failed as expected, confirming the
  test actually discriminates the fix rather than passing against both versions. The clear was then
  restored (`git diff --stat` confirmed a clean 5-line net diff from the round trip, no stray
  changes). **The same check caught that RR5/RR6 themselves did not discriminate the `runMutation`
  generation-guard fix**, on a second independent review pass: their original button-presence/absent-
  text assertions passed even with the guard's four checks disabled, because the pre-fix recheck
  fetch still returns `SELECTED` for order-a, so "Accepter l'ordre" stays visible and "Décision
  enregistrée" stays absent regardless of which order the panel actually swapped to. Rewritten to
  the same identity-count assertions RR2 already used (`getAllByText('Patient B').length === 2` /
  `'Patient A').length === 1`, inverting if the panel wrongly swaps to order-a) and re-verified:
  fails with the guard disabled, passes restored.
- `<ErrorState>{queueState.error}</ErrorState>` — TS2741, `ErrorState` takes a `code: ErrorCode`
  prop, not children. Fixed to `<ErrorState code="NETWORK_ERROR" onRetry={...} />`.
- A pre-existing `App.test.tsx` test broke because the new header's "DHealth Laboratoire (Natif)"
  button also matched its old loose `/Laboratoire/` name regex (now ambiguous, two matches). Fixed
  by scoping that test's query to the sidebar `navigation` landmark specifically, preserving its

Before writing any code, the actual state of `adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/lab_workflow.py`
and its test suites was read directly (not assumed from the ticket text). DH-EX-011 had already
shipped and real-PostgreSQL-qualified the entire backend this ticket's §6-§13/§36-§42 describe:
`LabWorkflowRepository.record_collection`/`start_processing`, the `LabSampleCollection` model and
its `0014_exchange_collection` migration, the two HTTP routes (`POST .../record-collection`,
`POST .../start-processing`), idempotent replay semantics, the ACCEPTED-only creation rule, the
no-retroactive-fabrication rule for legacy orders, the start-processing collection-gate (duplicated
in both `lab_workflow.py` and `orders.py`'s generic `transition()` on purpose), and role/cross-lab
authorization for every role *except* `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER` (introduced later, by DH-EX-012).
`adapter/tests/integration/test_dhex011_postgres_qualification.py` (340 lines, not run by CI —
confirmed via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which lists only `dhex003c`/`dhidentity001`/`dhclinic006`/
`dhclinic007` postgres-qualification files by name) already covered PG-C1/PG-C2/PG-P1/PG-P2 and the
collection-vs-processing race, along with 10-way and 25-way concurrency. This meant the ticket's own
§63-§65/§77 backend test matrix was **already satisfied** except for two gaps, found by reading the
