### What this ticket actually built

**Backend (commit `6363e40`).**
- `LabWorkflowRepository.list_for_lab` gained `.options(selectinload(LabOrder.items))`. Root cause:
  `_to_record`'s `order.items` access triggered one lazy-load query per returned order — found and
  disclosed by DH-EX-011's own `test_list_for_lab_collection_join_adds_no_marginal_per_order_query`,
  which *tolerated* rather than fixed it (its assertion allowed a delta scaling with order count).
  That test's assertion is now tightened to `delta <= 1` (flat, not scaling), and a new test,
  `test_list_for_lab_items_selectinload_issues_one_bounded_query_regardless_of_order_count`,
  measures queries against `exchange_lab_order_items` specifically (not total query count) for a
  1-order and an 8-order lab, asserting exactly 1 in both cases. Before the fix this count equalled
  the order count; after, it is 1 regardless of N.
- Two new tests: `test_releaser_alone_cannot_record_collection`,
  `test_releaser_alone_cannot_start_processing` (`adapter/tests/test_exchange_sample_collection.py`)
  — a `LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`-only identity gets 403 on both endpoints; the second also asserts the
  order stays `ACCEPTED` afterward, not silently advanced.
- No new endpoint, no new table, no new `LabOrderStatus` value, no migration.

**Frontend (commit `124e147`).**
- `exchangeTypes.ts`: `LabCollectionResponse { order_id, recorded_at }`, matching the backend's own
  Pydantic model field-for-field (verified by reading `api.py`'s `LabCollectionResponse` directly).
- `exchangeClient.ts`: `recordLabOrderCollection(labId, orderId, options)`,
  `startProcessingLabOrder(labId, orderId, options)` — thin typed wrappers over the two existing
  endpoints, no mock fallback.
- `LabOrdersPage.tsx`: the order-detail panel now offers, per the action-availability matrix (§48):
  `ACCEPTED` + no milestone → `Enregistrer la collecte` (explicit confirm, patient identity stays
  visible in the same panel); `ACCEPTED` + milestone present → `Commencer l'analyse` (explicit
  confirm); `IN_PROGRESS` → truthful "result entry comes later" text, no fabricated control.
  `mutationState.action` extended to `'collect' | 'start'`; the single `confirmingReject` boolean

  `runMutation` — each has a genuinely different recovery predicate (collection: judged by
  `collection_recorded_at`, never `status`; processing: a real fourth "prerequisite not met" branch
  the other three actions never have), and forcing them through one generic helper would have hidden
  that distinction, which §28 explicitly warns against.
- `LabHomePage.tsx`: its count-request `useEffect` — previously a bare `let isMounted` closure with
  no `AbortController` and no explicit tenant-id check — is now hardened to the identical
  generation-ref/`currentLabRef`/`AbortController` pattern `LabOrdersPage.loadQueue` already used.

### Collection UI behavior (AC1, AC3, AC6, AC7)

Explicit `Enregistrer la collecte` button appears only for `ACCEPTED` orders with no recorded
milestone (CUI1/CUI2/CUI3). Clicking it shows an inline confirmation naming the action in plain
French ("Enregistrer la collecte ? Confirmez que la collecte correspondant à cet ordre doit être
enregistrée dans DHealth.") with **Confirmer la collecte** / **Annuler** — Annuler makes no request
(CUI5/CUI6). No specimen/tube/barcode/free-text/manual-timestamp field exists anywhere in this flow
(CUI10, `queryAllByRole('textbox'|'spinbutton')` asserted empty). A recorded milestone displays as
"Collecte enregistrée" plus the French-locale date+time (CUI4); an unrecorded one displays "Collecte
non enregistrée dans DHealth" — worded as *not recorded*, never *not collected* (AC3, CUI3 for the
legacy-`IN_PROGRESS`-with-null case specifically).

### Collection confirmation / timestamp / replay behavior (AC5, AC7, AC8)

No request body — the endpoint takes none, and the client sends none. Timestamp is exclusively
server-generated (`LabSampleCollection.recorded_at`, DH-EX-011); no client-side clock is ever read
or displayed as authoritative. Replay safety is the backend's own pre-existing, DH-EX-011-qualified
behavior (`_record_collection_in_session`'s unconditional existing-row short-circuit); this ticket's
own new test, `LR-C1`, additionally proves the *frontend* accepts a replay's recorded state (from a
recheck after a lost response) as success without ever issuing a second POST.

### Collection lost-response recovery (AC13, §25)

Three-way, matching §25 exactly: (Case A) recheck shows `collection_recorded_at != null` → success,
no error, no second POST (`LR-C1`); (Case B) recheck shows `ACCEPTED` + still `null` → unconfirmed,
explicit retry stays available (`LR-C2`); (Case C) recheck shows the order moved on with no milestone
ever recorded → conflict shown, never fabricated (`LR-C3`).

### Processing UI behavior (AC10, §18, §48)

`Commencer l'analyse` appears only for `ACCEPTED` orders with a recorded milestone (PUI1/PUI2); never
for `ACCEPTED` without one, never once `IN_PROGRESS` (PUI7). No result-entry control appears at any
point (PUI8, LAB-003/004 scope untouched).

### Processing confirmation / prerequisite / replay behavior (AC9, AC11, AC12)

Explicit confirmation ("Commencer l'analyse ? L'ordre passera à l'état « En cours ».") with
**Commencer** / **Annuler** (PUI3). The prerequisite (a recorded milestone) is enforced
authoritatively by the backend (unchanged DH-EX-011 gate, duplicated in both `lab_workflow.py` and
`orders.py`); the frontend never offers `Commencer l'analyse` without a milestone in the first place
(PUI1), so a direct-API bypass attempt is the only way to exercise the gate, and that path is
DH-EX-011's own qualified behavior, unchanged. Replay of an already-`IN_PROGRESS` order is the
backend's own pre-existing idempotent short-circuit (§13); `LR-P1` proves the frontend accepts that
recheck result as success.

### Processing lost-response recovery (AC14, §26)

Four-way, the one genuinely new recovery shape in this ticket: (Case A) recheck shows
`IN_PROGRESS` → success (`LR-P1`); (Case B) recheck shows `ACCEPTED` + milestone present →
unconfirmed, explicit retry stays available (`LR-P2`); (Case C) recheck shows `ACCEPTED` + **no**
milestone → prerequisite not met, `PROCESSING_PREREQUISITE_ERROR` shown, **no auto-retry offered**
— the panel's own status/collection-driven render falls back to `Enregistrer la collecte` instead,
since that is what the authoritative state now calls for (`LR-P3`); (Case D, not separately tested
beyond the shared conflict path accept/reject also exercise) a terminal status reached by a
concurrent caller → conflict shown.

### LabOrder.items N+1 — root cause, fix, before/after evidence (AC20, §33-§34, §66)

Root cause: `LabWorkflowRepository._to_record`'s access to the ORM relationship
`LabOrder.items` (no eager-load option on the query that produced `order`) triggers one lazy `SELECT
... FROM exchange_lab_order_items WHERE lab_order_id = :id` per row in `list_for_lab`'s result set —
disclosed by DH-EX-011, left unfixed as out of its own scope. Fix: `.options(selectinload(LabOrder.
items))` added to `list_for_lab`'s query (`selectinload`, not `joinedload`, because the primary query
already returns one row per order via its own joins — a `joinedload` of the one-to-many `items` would
multiply rows and require deduplication). Before/after, measured directly against `exchange_
lab_order_items`: **before**, 1 query per order (N queries for N orders, confirmed by re-reading the
pre-fix test's own tolerant assertion); **after**,
`test_list_for_lab_items_selectinload_issues_one_bounded_query_regardless_of_order_count` asserts
exactly 1 query against that table for both a 1-order and an 8-order lab.

**Local-only, found before pushing, never reached CI:** the pre-existing

documentation commit) — confirmed exact match at session start (`git status` clean, `git pull
--ff-only` no-op). Alembic head confirmed `0023_provider_lab_routes` before any code change.

**Ending master SHA:** `7f2962b` (frontend commit), with this documentation commit following it.
Backend commit `3815e91` and a small CI-config fix `d1bfa12` immediately precede it (see below).

**Commits, in order:**
1. `3815e91` — `feat(DH-LAB-003): controlled, LabOffering-scoped Native Lab result templates + entry plan`
2. `d1bfa12` — `fix(DH-LAB-003): bump CI's EXPECTED_HEAD to 0024_result_templates`
3. `7f2962b` — `feat(DH-LAB-003): read-only result-structure preview in Native Lab`
4. (this commit) — `docs(DH-LAB-003): record templates/entry-plan evidence`

**Direct master, no PR — confirmed.** No branch was created; every commit landed directly on
`master` per this ticket's own explicit instruction.

### Backend — new schema, first migration since DH-LAB-001 (§9-§34, AC1-AC15, AC23)

**New tables** (`adapter/migrations/versions/0024_result_templates.py`):
- `exchange_lab_result_templates` — `id`, `lab_offering_id` (FK, RESTRICT), `version` (CHECK `>=
  1`), `active`, `created_at`. `UNIQUE(lab_offering_id, version)`, plus a partial unique index
  (`postgresql_where`/`sqlite_where` `active = true`/`active = 1`, mirroring `LabPrice`'s own
  current-row pattern) enforcing at most one active row per offering at the database level.
- `exchange_lab_result_template_observations` — `id`, `result_template_id` (FK, RESTRICT),
  `source_code` (String(64)), `display_label` (String(256)), `result_type` (String(16), CHECK
  `NUMERIC`/`TEXT`), `numeric_unit` (String(32), nullable), `required`, `sort_order` (CHECK `>=
  0`). `UNIQUE(result_template_id, source_code)` and `UNIQUE(result_template_id, sort_order)`. All
  four `source_code`/`display_label`/`result_type`/`numeric_unit` column shapes deliberately match
  `LabObservation`'s own exactly, so a template value can never be too long to copy into the
  observation a future LAB-004 will derive from it.
- `exchange_security_audit_events`'s `event_type`/`resource_type` CHECK constraints widened for
  `lab_result_template_created`/`lab_result_template_activated`/`lab_result_template` — the same
  drop/recreate delta pattern `0006` through `0023` already established, applied both in the
  migration and directly in `models.py`'s own CHECK strings (the latter is what SQLite's
  `Base.metadata.create_all()`-based test schema actually uses — found and fixed locally before
  ever pushing, when the first local test run hit a CHECK-constraint IntegrityError on the new
  audit event types; see "bugs found" below).

**Why `LabOffering`, not `TestCatalogEntry`.** `TestCatalogEntry` is the provider-facing ordered
*service* identity; `LabOffering` is one particular lab's own implementation of that service. Two
labs offering the identical catalog test may legitimately report a different observation structure
(methodology, local reporting format, observation count) without that being a second
ordered-service identity. Recorded as ADR-053 Decision 1, not merely an implementation choice.

**Repository** (`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/lab_result_templates.py`,
`LabResultTemplateRepository`):
- `create_template`: validates (version ≥ 1; ≥ 1 observation definition; ≥ 1 required; non-empty
  `source_code`/`display_label`; `result_type` in `{NUMERIC, TEXT}`; TEXT never carries
  `numeric_unit`; `sort_order ≥ 0`; no duplicate `source_code`/`sort_order` within the request) all
  in Python *before* any row is inserted, so a rejected create is never partially committed.
  Insert-first-wins on `(lab_offering_id, version)` (the `create_entry`/`create_offering`
  IntegrityError-then-compare pattern this codebase already uses); an exact-content replay
  (normalized as a sorted tuple of `(sort_order, source_code, display_label, result_type,
  numeric_unit, required)` per definition, both sides) returns the existing row unchanged; a
  same-version request with different normalized content raises `TemplateConflict` (409) — never
  silently overwrites version N.
- `activate_template`: locks the owning `LabOffering` `FOR UPDATE` first, then discovers-and-
  deactivates the current active row (if any) in one `UPDATE ... RETURNING`, mirroring
  `CatalogRepository.set_price`'s own established discover-and-swap-in-one-statement discipline
  (see that method's own docstring for why a separate prior `SELECT` is unsafe under PostgreSQL's
  READ COMMITTED isolation). If the deactivated row *is* the target, it is reverted to active
  within the same transaction and reported `"unchanged"` — a safe replay regardless of what
  `expected_current_template_id` claimed, identical to `set_price`'s own already-correct-value
  exception. Otherwise `expected_current_template_id` is compared against what was actually
  deactivated (`None` means "I expect nothing active yet"); a mismatch raises
  `TemplateActivationConflict` (409).
- `get_active_templates_for_offerings`: batched — exactly two queries (active templates, then
  their observation definitions) regardless of how many offering ids are passed. Used by the
  entry-plan read below.
- No edit or delete method exists anywhere on this repository (AC10) — a structural change is
  always a new version, never a mutation of an existing one.

**API** (`adapter/src/daher_adapter/exchange/api.py`): `GET`/`POST
.../organizations/{lab_id}/offerings/{offering_id}/result-templates`, `POST
.../result-templates/{template_id}/activate` — all three gated by `_require_org_admin`, the same
authority offerings/prices already use (never `LAB_TECH`; the staff entering Patient results are
not automatically the authority who defines the structure they enter results into). Cross-offering
anti-enumeration (`_existing_template_for_offering_or_404`) mirrors
`_existing_offering_for_lab_or_404`'s own convention exactly.

**Audit:** `lab_result_template_created` fires once per genuine new version (never on an
exact-content replay); `lab_result_template_activated` fires once per real active-template switch
(never on an already-active-target replay) — both verified by a dedicated no-duplicate-event test
(`test_a2_same_target_activation_replay_unchanged`).

### Backend — read-only result-entry plan (§34-§39, AC16-AC18)

New `GET .../organizations/{lab_id}/lab-orders/{order_id}/result-entry-plan`, gated by
`_require_lab_tech` (same tenant as the rest of the lab-workflow surface), exposed only while
`order.status == IN_PROGRESS` (409 otherwise — result entry is not yet operationally meaningful in
any other status). For each order item: `LabOffering` for `(lab_id, catalog_entry_id)` is looked
up (`CatalogRepository.get_offerings_for_lab_and_entries`, one batched query for the whole order);
the currently active template for that offering (if any) is resolved via
`get_active_templates_for_offerings` (two more batched queries); `is_synthetic` is derived from the
item's own `TestCatalogEntry` (`CatalogRepository.get_entries_by_ids`, one more batched query) —
never stored as a second, potentially divergent flag on the template itself. Total: five queries
for the whole read, flat regardless of item count — proven by
`test_result_entry_plan_query_count_is_flat_regardless_of_item_count` (1-item vs. 5-item order,
delta ≤ 1).

**Missing template is a valid, honest read state** (`template: null`), never fabricated, never a
free-form fallback. **An item whose catalog entry has literally no `LabOffering` row at this lab at
all** is treated differently — `ResultEntryPlanIntegrityError`, raised unhandled (mapped to a 500,
matching `LabAssignmentIntegrityError`/`PatientIdentityIntegrityError`'s own established fail-closed
convention) — because a *currently assigned* order's every item is guaranteed to have had an active
offering at assignment time (`LabSelectionRepository.assign_by_provider`/`select` both require it),
and offering rows are never deleted, only deactivated. Reaching that branch would mean a genuine
data-integrity violation, never an honestly-absent configuration.

### Frontend (§40-§50, AC19-AC21)

`ExchangeClient.getResultEntryPlan`; `ResultEntryPlan`/`ResultEntryPlanItem`/
`ResultEntryPlanTemplate`/`ResultEntryPlanObservation` types, matching the backend response shape
field-for-field. `LabOrdersPage`'s `IN_PROGRESS` branch now renders "Structure des résultats": each
item's own card shows its configured observations (label, NUMERIC/TEXT, unit if present,
requis/facultatif) in the server-given sort order; a missing template shows "Aucune structure de
résultat n'est configurée pour cette analyse."; a synthetic template shows "Configuration de
démonstration — ne pas utiliser pour des soins réels."; no value input, no complete-entry button,
no release button exists anywhere in this branch. Patient identity/ordering facility/requested
tests stay above the preview, unchanged hierarchy (§46).

The plan load is deliberately a **third request sharing `panelGenerationRef`**, not a dedicated
ref/counter — this plan only ever makes sense for the order currently occupying the panel, so any
event that already invalidates the panel (a different order, closing it, a lab switch) must
invalidate it identically, with no separate bookkeeping to drift out of sync. The generation is
*read*, never incremented, by `loadPlan` — incrementing would wrongly invalidate whatever
`loadPanel` call is concurrently in flight for the very order the plan belongs to. Triggered by a
`useEffect` watching `panel?.order?.status`/`panel?.orderId`, so it also fires correctly after a
start-processing success moves an order into `IN_PROGRESS` via its own recheck, with no separate
wiring needed.

## DH-LAB-004 (2026-09-18) — Native Result Entry + Completion + Release

**Starting master SHA:** `619a77b` (DH-LAB-003's own final documentation commit). Alembic head
confirmed `0024_result_templates` before any code change.

**Commits, in order:**
1. `d50d597` — `feat(DH-LAB-004): Native result entry backend -- template pinning, batch values, fingerprint-gated release`
2. (frontend commit, this session) — `feat(DH-LAB-004): Native entry form, Libération queue/release UI, PG qualification`
3. (this commit) — `docs(DH-LAB-004): record evidence, ADR-053/ADR-044 addenda`

**Direct master, no PR — confirmed.** No branch was created.

### Backend — first-write template pinning, Native batch values, hardened raw API, fingerprint-gated release

Migration `0025_native_result_binding`: nullable `LabResult.result_template_id` and
`LabObservation.template_observation_definition_id` (both `ON DELETE RESTRICT`), plus a partial
unique index enforcing at most one effective observation per controlled definition per container.
Downgrade refuses if any row carries bound provenance, mirroring `0023`/`0024`'s own precedent.
CI's `EXPECTED_HEAD` bumped to `0025_native_result_binding` in the same commit — the exact class
of drift DH-LAB-003 found and fixed as a late follow-up, not repeated here.

`LabResultRepository.record_native_values` (the Native controlled batch value endpoint's backing
method): first write for an item locks the owning `LabOffering FOR UPDATE` — the identical lock
`activate_template`'s own compare-and-swap acquires — verifies the named `template_id` is that
offering's active template at the locked instant, and pins the container to it permanently
(`NoActiveTemplateForOffering` otherwise). Every subsequent write must name that identical pinned
template (`TemplateNotPinnedToThisResult` otherwise) — the pin survives any later template
activation. Per value: unknown `definition_id` → 422; a value shape that doesn't match the
definition's own `result_type` → 422 (server derives type from the definition, never the client).
Replay is idempotent per definition (exact value → safe no-op; different value →
`ObservationValueConflict`, never overwritten); every replay/conflict/type check for a batch
resolves before any row is inserted, so a rejected batch writes nothing. A value after entry
completion is refused unless it is an exact replay. A pre-existing non-template-bound container
(`LegacyOrExternalResultContainer`) refuses Native adoption outright.

The browser never submits result structure: `POST .../items/{item_id}/native-result-values`
accepts only `template_id` and, per value, `definition_id` + `numeric_value`/`text_value`.
`source_code`/`display_label`/`result_type`/`numeric_unit`/`source_system` are always derived
server-side from the pinned template's own `LabResultTemplateObservation` row.

The raw, free-structure observation API (`record_observation`/`correct_observation`) now refuses
to mutate a Native-template-bound container/observation
(`TemplateBoundContainerRefusesUnstructuredWrite`) — proven with a genuine red→green
discrimination test (the guard was temporarily disabled, the test failed exactly as predicted,
then the guard was restored and the suite re-verified green). A non-template-bound container is
entirely unaffected; ADR-053 Decision 8's "untouched, fully source-flexible" promise holds.

`complete_entry` additionally requires every `required=true` definition on a template-bound
container to have an effective value, checked by definition identity, never `source_code` string
matching. Legacy completion is unchanged.

New `GET .../result-entry-workspace` resolves each item's governing template (the container's own
pinned version if one exists — even if no longer active — else the offering's current active
template for an unstarted item) plus what has already been entered; `entry_mode` truthfully
distinguishes `NATIVE_TEMPLATE`/`LEGACY_OR_EXTERNAL`/`UNSTARTED_NO_TEMPLATE` — no free-form
fallback when no template is configured. Bounded, batched (query-count-flat proof:
`test_w9_workspace_query_count_does_not_scale_with_item_count`, 1-item vs. 5-item order).

New `GET /organizations/{lab_id}/release-queue` (`LabResultReleaseRepository.
list_release_candidates`): this lab's own least-privilege queue — `IN_PROGRESS`, every item's
entry complete, not already released — never the `LAB_TECH` work queue broadened.
`LAB_RESULT_RELEASER`-only.

**Release-inspection fingerprint** (`compute_result_fingerprint`): a SHA-256 digest over the
canonical sorted set of every effective `(item_id, observation_id)` pair — immutable identities,
never raw values (a correction mints a new observation id, so it always changes the digest).
Computed once inside `get_for_lab` (extends `LabResultInspectionResponse` with `result_fingerprint`
+ `patient` + `ordering_provider_name`, never forked into a second endpoint) and once inside
`release`'s own re-check, from the identical `_effective_observation_rows` data both already used.
`POST .../release-results` now requires `expected_result_fingerprint`; a mismatch raises
`StaleResultFingerprint` (409) *before* any release row is created — proven with a second genuine
red→green discrimination test. A replay of an already-completed release is unconditionally safe
regardless of the fingerprint passed. See `DECISIONS.md`'s ADR-044 addendum for the full race
closure this mechanism provides.

### Real PostgreSQL qualification — actually executed this session (a first for this ticket sequence)

Unlike DH-LAB-002/DH-LAB-003 (both blocked by this sandbox's Docker Hub CDN pull failure), this
session found a **native, already-installed PostgreSQL 18 instance** inside the WSL2 sandbox (no
image pull needed) with qualification databases from earlier, real DH-EX tickets already present
— establishing that real-PostgreSQL qualification *is* possible in this environment when it
doesn't require pulling a container image. `tests/integration/
test_dhlab004_postgres_qualification.py` (`DHLAB004_PG_*` env-var-gated, skipped by default,
never in CI) was written and **actually run** against a fresh `dhlab004_qual` database (migrated
to `0025_native_result_binding` via real `alembic upgrade head`):

- `test_pgt1_activation_vs_first_write_never_produces_a_mismatched_pin` — first-write pin vs.
  concurrent `activate_template`, both locking the same `LabOffering FOR UPDATE`.
- `test_pge1_concurrent_identical_batch_converges_no_duplicate` — 10 concurrent identical-value
  callers, exactly one effective observation.
- `test_pge2_concurrent_different_values_exactly_one_wins` — 2 concurrent different-value callers,
  exactly one wins, the other conflicts, never last-write-wins.
- `test_pgrel_correction_winning_the_lock_invalidates_a_concurrent_stale_release` — the release-
  vs-correction fingerprint race.

All 4 passed on first run; re-run 5x as a batch (20 total executions) plus 15 additional direct
repetitions each for PG-T1 and PG-REL (30 more) — zero flakes, zero failures. This is genuine,
executed real-PostgreSQL concurrency evidence for this ticket's own most safety-critical claims,
not merely written-but-undisclosed-as-unexecuted.

### Frontend

`NativeResultEntryForm` (`ui/src/features/lab/components/`): renders exactly the pinned/active
template's own configured definitions — never a hardcoded field. An unentered required/optional
definition is a labeled `TextInput` ("Requis"/"Facultatif", unit shown in the label for NUMERIC);
an already-entered value is shown read-only, never editable (no correction UI exists yet — that is
DH-LAB-005's own scope). No autosave anywhere — an explicit "Enregistrer les valeurs" button is
the only write trigger, disabled with no draft. "Terminer la saisie" is enabled only once every
required definition has a value, with its own confirmation step. Draft state lives in component
memory only, never `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`.

`LabOrdersPage`'s `IN_PROGRESS` branch now renders this controlled form per item (replacing
DH-LAB-003's read-only preview), backed by the new result-entry-workspace read
(`loadWorkspace`, sharing `panelGenerationRef` exactly as `loadPlan` did).

New `LabReleasePage` (`ui/src/features/lab/pages/`): the release queue plus an inspection/release
flow. Release requires an explicit confirmation ("Libérer ces résultats ? Ils deviendront
disponibles pour l'établissement prescripteur.") carrying the exact `result_fingerprint` from the
inspection on screen. A 409 conflict shows "Les résultats ont changé depuis votre vérification.
Veuillez les examiner à nouveau avant de les libérer." and forces a fresh re-inspection — never a
blind retry. Lost-response recovery re-reads authoritative state (`getLabOrderResults`) rather
than assuming failure. `released`/`delivered`/`reviewed` stay untouched, independent concepts —
this ticket adds no code path that touches `ResultDelivery` or `DoctorReview` beyond what release
already bound under ADR-048.

New `LabShell` "Libération" tab, gated on `capabilities.canReleaseResults` (already computed in
`LabProvider` since DH-LAB-001) — a dual-role user sees Accueil/Ordres/Libération; a releaser-only
user sees Accueil/Libération, with no route to the `LAB_TECH` queue at all, closing the "truthful
not-yet-available placeholder" DH-LAB-001 left for that role.

**Local vitest was intermittently broken for a large part of this session** (WSL and native
Windows, `npm run test` and direct `npx vitest`, with and without cache clearing all hit
`[vitest-pool]: Failed to start forks worker ... Timeout waiting for worker to respond`) after a
`wsl --shutdown`/restart performed mid-session to recover from a genuine host-machine network
outage (confirmed at the Windows-host level via `Test-NetConnection`, not merely WSL's own
resolver). Basic `child_process.fork`/IPC was independently confirmed working in the same WSL
instance throughout, so the breakage was scoped to vitest's own worker-pool startup handshake, not
a deeper environment failure. It self-recovered later in the session with no further intervention
(no root cause isolated) -- once it did, `npm run test` (the full UI suite, not only
`src/features/lab`) was run repeatedly and used to find and fix the four real issues CI's own
first two runs had already caught (see "Final CI state" below): the full local suite is now green

(`ExchangeAuthProvider.test.tsx`'s `retry()` test, last touched by DH-CLINIC-004A). CI remained the
actual gating verification throughout regardless of local availability, consistent with this
repository's own established practice.
